result.other_findings: Non-compliance with prescribing was due to prescribers following BNFC rather than trust guidance. Therapeutic concentrations were still not achieved in over 80% of patients, prompting a call to re-evaluate the dosing guideline.

result.setting: Community Adult Mental Health Services, Taylor Centre, Southend; outpatient clinics
result.standard: NICE CG178 1.5.8 (offer supported employment to people with psychosis or schizophrenia who wish to work) and NG181 1.8.9 (facilitate alternative educational or occupational activities)

cycle1.result: Supported employment offered to 35% of the non-working sample; alternative educational or occupational options offered to 26%.

cycle2.result: Employment status documented in 97%; supported employment offered to 38%; alternative educational or employment options offered to 47%.

result.other_findings: 64% of those offered supported employment declined; 78% were not actively seeking work. Only 33% were followed up, and employment was most often discussed at follow-up appointments (87%).

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in early intervention in psychosis
result.setting: Mid and North Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Hampshire and Isle of Wight NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Physical health monitoring and intervention standards of the National Audit of Schizophrenia 2021 and National Clinical Audit of Psychosis 2022 (75% standard); Lester UK tool; local target 80% after interventions

cycle1.result: 54/118 identified as high risk. Monitoring of smoking, alcohol, illicit substances, BMI, blood pressure, lipids and glucose exceeded the 75% standard. Acceptance of interventions was low: smoking cessation 18%, alcohol interventions 33%, illicit substance advice 6%, HbA1c-related recommendations 8%, lipid lifestyle advice 10%; 100% accepted interventions for high BMI and hypertension.

result.other_findings: Standards for monitoring were met but not for interventions; an action plan (patient education and team training on Lester tool interventions) was recommended before the next cycle, with re-audit every 6 months.

result.setting: Acute hospitals in the UK and Ireland; national trainee collaborative (protocol)
result.standard: WHO Mastitis Guidelines 2000; GAIN Guidelines 2008; ABM Clinical Protocol #4: Mastitis 2014; NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries: Mastitis and Breast Abscess

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Protocol only: planned three phases (national practice survey, prospective audit, prospective re-audit) collecting antibiotic prescribing, operative versus radiological management, time to ultrasound, inpatient versus outpatient treatment, length of stay and breast surgeon follow-up.

result.topic: Serious infections in early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA), England; observational cohort with NHS Digital linkage
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 519 serious infection admissions and 17 deaths; incidence per 100 person-years 3.19 (95% CI 2.93-3.48) for admissions and 0.10 (0.06-0.16) for deaths. MTX-based strategies HR 0.75 and csDMARD combination HR 0.70 versus no DMARD; each 1-unit DAS28 rise HR 1.08.

result.other_findings: Age, smoking, comorbidity, disease activity, symptom burden and disability predicted admissions; corticosteroid association was not significant in fully adjusted models.

result.setting: Old age psychiatry inpatient ward
result.standard: Patients detained under the MHA should have Section 17 leave facilitated as granted by the responsible clinician, with documented discussion and updated risk assessment before leave

cycle1.result: Section 17 form not uploaded to RIO in 25% (7); no documented discussion of leave in 46.42% (13); no evidence whether leave facilitated in 25% (7); 42% (6) of those granted leave off grounds had it facilitated; no updated risk assessment before leave in 83% (5/6).

result.other_findings: All facilitated leave was escorted as specified. Recommendations: discuss leave at ward rounds and one-to-one sessions, document risk assessment and use the pre-leave form; re-audit after 12 months.

result.topic: Tocilizumab approval criteria in giant cell arteritis
result.setting: Bristol and Bath regional GCA multidisciplinary team meeting
result.standard: NHS England criteria (Blueteq) for tocilizumab in refractory or relapsing GCA; MDT discussion required before starting

cycle1.result: 38 cases discussed, 31 approved for tocilizumab; 100% of approved cases met criteria for refractory (n = 11) or relapsing (n = 20) disease.

result.other_findings: High glucocorticoid toxicity burden; 77.4% cranial GCA, 48.4% large vessel, 25.8% ischaemic visual loss. Patients with ocular involvement were referred earlier (478.2 vs 648.1 days).

result.topic: Vitamin D testing in paediatric haematology and oncology
result.setting: Paediatric haematology/oncology; new diagnoses of malignant disease
result.standard: Trust guideline for vitamin D deficiency: 100% tested at diagnosis; 100% of results acted on; 100% given appropriate dose

cycle1.result: 56% tested for vitamin D during admission; 35% of oncology and 83% of haematology patients tested. 6% of haematology and 5% of oncology patients with sufficient levels received treatment not indicated; the 5% of oncology patients with insufficient levels were not treated. Standards not met.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: follow the revised trust guideline, pharmacists to check vitamin D for all new admissions, and build a default test into the new prescribing system.

result.topic: Bone health assessment after inpatient falls
result.setting: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Kings Mill Hospital); inpatients who fell, identified via DATIX
result.standard: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group: FRAX to estimate 10-year fracture risk and guide bone protection; NICE CG161; Trust post-fall assessment guidance

cycle1.result: Falls assessment sheet completed in over 80%; FRAX calculated in only 33.3%. Of those with FRAX, 60% intermediate, 20% high and 10% very high risk; only 50% of high-risk patients received oral bisphosphonates. Retrospective FRAX in those not assessed showed 60% very high risk.

result.other_findings: Calcium and vitamin D checks were done more often than FRAX but still below optimal; renal impairment limited bisphosphonate eligibility. Falls Alert Stickers with checkboxes and QR code, a revised post-falls proforma with a bone health section, and clinician education were introduced.

result.setting: Outpatient department, Punjab Institute of Mental Health, Lahore
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) for long-acting injectable antipsychotics

cycle1.result: All patients on fluphenazine decanoate with a concurrent second antipsychotic (100% polypharmacy); 78% informed of side effects; none had post-injection observation; no test doses given; no baseline ECG or physical health assessment; fluphenazine used in rapid tranquillisation.

result.other_findings: Recommendations included staff training on Maudsley guidance, test dose protocols, mandatory baseline ECG, revised rapid tranquillisation protocol and regular re-audit.

result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit
result.standard: Trust guideline: Labinic probiotic for babies <32 weeks and/or <1.5 kg at birth, at correct dose, given with first feed or within 12 hours of birth

cycle1.result: 76/76 (100%) eligible babies prescribed and given Labinic; 76/76 (100%) correct dose; only 17/76 (22%) received it within the first 12 hours.

result.other_findings: Unit went from 0% to 100% of eligible babies receiving probiotics after the GIRFT recommendation. Planned nurse education, updated guidance and e-prescribing to stress first dose within 12 hours, and re-audit.

result.topic: COVID-19 outcomes in shielded rheumatology patients
result.setting: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust and Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust rheumatology departments
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 28/5876 (0.48%) shielded patients hospitalised with COVID-19 (23/4914, 0.47% MSE; 5/962, 0.52% BHR); 10/28 (36%) died. Shielded rheumatology patients were 0.76% (28/3695) of all COVID-19 admissions.

result.other_findings: Admitted patients were mostly elderly with multiple comorbidities; only one was on anti-TNF therapy.

result.topic: Antibiotic choice and duration in necrotising enterocolitis
result.setting: Single UK tertiary children's hospital providing neonatal intensive care and neonatal surgery
result.standard: Local NEC guideline: first-line amoxicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole for up to 10 days

cycle1.result: Guideline regimen (amoxicillin, gentamicin, metronidazole) used in 1/7; ceftazidime, vancomycin and metronidazole in 4; meropenem and vancomycin in 2. Median course 10 days (range 2 to 16).

result.intervention: Results presented to a neonatal surgery quality improvement meeting in January 2019 to highlight the issue to surgical and neonatal teams.

cycle2.result: Guideline regimen used in 4/5; ceftazidime, vancomycin and metronidazole in 1. Median course 11 days (range 5 to 12).

result.other_findings: Compliance with antibiotic choice improved but treatment duration still varied considerably.

result.topic: Axial spondyloarthritis management against NICE QS170
result.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath; tertiary axSpA centre; patients starting bDMARDs
result.standard: NICE QS170 (MRI if no radiographic evidence, structured exercise programme, patient information) and clinical practice guidelines

cycle1.result: MRI in 18/19 (94.7%) with X-rays showing no sacroiliitis; education in 228/267 (85.4%); referral to structured exercise 217/259 (83.8%); first-line NSAIDs 246/248 (99.2%); 6-monthly renal monitoring on NSAIDs 80.3%; 12-week bDMARD response assessment 198/233 (85.0%).

result.other_findings: 300 sampled from 539, 269 met inclusion. Median time from symptom onset to diagnosis 6.26 years.

result.topic: Postoperative care documentation in operation notes
result.setting: Spinal surgery, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: MDT consensus of 15 essential criteria for complete post-operative care documentation (no published standard)

cycle1.result: Baseline: >75% compliance in 4 criteria and <50% compliance in 10 of 15 criteria.

result.intervention: Post-operative care template based on the 15 criteria embedded in existing IT software as a non-overwriting suffix needing two mouse clicks; later template update after a usage questionnaire.

cycle2.dates: 12 months after template update (5 years post baseline)

result.other_findings: Six audit cycles, >400 operation notes over 5 years: improvement sustained at 3 and 12 months, declined at 24 months (new staff unaware of template, response option problems), then >75% in 11 criteria after template update.

result.setting: Marsden House CAMHS, Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust; internal referrals to psychiatry
result.standard: Referral quality indicators (demographics, consent, prior therapy interventions per NICE, risk assessment)

cycle1.result: Mean 2.7/5 demographic identifiers; consent documented 43% (10/23); prior therapy documented 65% (15/23); risk mentioned 39% (9/23); mean 2.43 emails per referral.

result.other_findings: Lack of a standardised referral form was the main cause; recommendations were a form with mandatory fields, referrer training and a streamlined process.

result.topic: MRA and ICD therapy after myocardial infarction with LV dysfunction
result.setting: Ulster Hospital, Dundonald; MI patients from MINAP database
result.standard: MRA for eligible patients with post-MI LVEF ≤40% and heart failure or diabetes (EPHESUS); repeat LV imaging at 6-12 weeks and device therapy if LVEF ≤35% persists

cycle1.result: 47 (14%) eligible for MRA, 22 (47%) prescribed. 27 eligible for device consideration; 23 (85%) had repeat LV assessment (mean 107 days); 4 had ongoing severe LVSD, of whom 1 (25%) had an ICD.

result.other_findings: Of those with ongoing severe LVSD, 25% died before review and 50% had no documented reason why device therapy was not considered.

result.topic: Benzodiazepine and Z-drug prescribing in inpatient psychiatry
result.setting: Heddfan acute adult inpatient psychiatric unit, North Wales
result.standard: National guidelines on benzodiazepine and hypnotic treatment duration and dosage limits

cycle1.result: 38/40 prescribed PRN benzodiazepines (lorazepam 35/38, 92%); only 12/38 reviewed within a week; one had PRN stopped; half continued PRN benzodiazepines for more than 3 weeks. 20 (50%) received zopiclone, 66% (8) of these for 3 weeks or more.

result.other_findings: 11 (27.5%) were already on regular benzodiazepines. Planned pharmacist-led weekly PRN review at ward rounds and a protocol for reducing and stopping PRN medication.

result.setting: Two autism specialist rehabilitation wards (Springs Centre and Springs Wing), Cygnet Harrow Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Considerable proficiency across about 11 of 18 assessed domains; persistent deficits in six areas including autonomous decision-making, behavioural adaptation under stress, social cognition, transition preparedness, proprioception and motor planning.

result.other_findings: Multidisciplinary assessment across 18 domains; findings to inform care planning and bespoke therapeutic pathways.

result.topic: Liver function monitoring on CFTR modulators
result.setting: Large tertiary paediatric cystic fibrosis centre; patients newly started on Kaftrio
result.standard: Local trust guideline, SmPC and MHRA Drug Safety Update: baseline LFTs, then every 3 months in the first year; defined actions for raised ALT/AST

cycle1.result: Baseline LFTs 30/31 (97%); LFTs at 3 months 10/31 (32%) (15 too early, 6 late); 0 patients had four sets at correct 3-monthly intervals; 4 (13%) had abnormal LFTs, 50% of which were acted on per guidelines.

result.other_findings: Rate of liver impairment was low; authors suggest reviewing whether local practice should deviate from national guidance to fit real-world practice.

result.setting: Tertiary PICU and paediatric high dependency unit (Royal Brompton and Harefield guideline)
result.standard: Local PICU analgesia and sedation guideline (2020): approved indication; dose not above 1.4 microgram/kg/hour; duration not above 72 hours

cycle1.result: 32/33 (97%) prescribed for approved indications; no patient exceeded 1.4 microgram/kg/hour; infusion exceeded 72 hours in 3 (9%).

result.other_findings: COMFORT scores recorded for 15/18 non-extubation courses but none had documented target scores; guideline education and a monthly 'DRUGgle' update were delivered before and during data collection. Repeat audit planned.

result.topic: Antipsychotic use for non-cognitive symptoms of dementia
result.setting: Southwest Crisis Function Team, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines on managing non-cognitive symptoms of dementia (structured assessment, psychosocial interventions first, antipsychotics only if indicated, risk-benefit discussion, lowest dose, reassessment at 6 weeks)

cycle1.result: Structured assessment 55/55 (100%); psychosocial and environmental interventions offered 55/55 (100%); new antipsychotics in 7/55 (12.7%), all appropriate and at lowest effective dose; risk-benefit discussion documented 0/7 (0%); reassessment at 6 weeks documented in 4/19 (21%).

result.other_findings: 247 referrals screened; 12 of the 55 referrals were repeat referrals of 6 service users.

result.topic: Sodium levels with heparin line flush solutions
result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean admission sodium 139.96 mmol/L, 138 mmol/L at line removal or discharge (mean fall 2 mmol/L); 1 needed sodium supplementation; 2 lines blocked.

result.intervention: Switch from heparin in sodium chloride 0.9% to heparin in sodium chloride 0.45% for arterial and CVP line flushes (cost saving), June 2018.

cycle2.result: Mean admission sodium 135.68 mmol/L, 135.72 mmol/L at line removal or discharge (mean change 0.04 mmol/L); 1 needed sodium supplementation; 2 lines blocked.

result.other_findings: The 0.45% flush did not lower sodium levels; other sodium sources were not assessed.

result.setting: Rheumatology services at 16 hospitals in northwest England (regional audit and survey)
result.standard: BSR guidance on giant cell arteritis (revised)

cycle1.result: 14/16 sites responded; 2 sites had a GCA pathway; routine steroid leaflets 6/14 (43%); 1 site had a GCA database; 8 had a steroid taper protocol.

result.intervention: 2017 audit and survey results fed back to sites and regionally; sites introduced GCA pathways, temporal artery ultrasound, steroid leaflets and local QI.

cycle2.result: 15/16 sites responded; 6 sites had a GCA pathway; temporal artery ultrasound 6/15 (40%); routine steroid leaflets 12/15 (80%); GCA database 4 (27%); steroid taper protocol 7.

result.other_findings: 9/15 (60%) sites said the 2017 audit prompted changes. No change in steroid card provision; 8/15 (53%) reported COVID-19 harmed services, mainly access to diagnostics.

result.setting: Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH)
result.standard: 100% of positive m.1555A>G results recorded on prescribing record; 100% tested before aminoglycoside; 100% of positives not given an aminoglycoside

cycle1.result: 12 (0.31%) tested positive; 100% had the result recorded as an aminoglycoside allergy on JAC; 5/12 (42%) positives had received aminoglycosides, 1 before testing.

result.other_findings: Unclear whether aminoglycoside use in positive patients was an informed risk-benefit decision; follow-up (including audiology) of these patients is being arranged.

result.setting: Hull Royal Infirmary; general surgery admissions during COVID-19
result.standard: AUGIS guidance (March 2020) favouring conservative non-surgical management of acute cholecystitis during COVID-19

cycle1.result: Conservative management 15 (62.5%); percutaneous cholecystostomy 4 (16.6%); laparoscopic cholecystectomy 5 (20.8%). Mean stay 5.67 days; 30-day readmission 5 (20.8%).

result.intervention: Initial audit presented at the general surgery clinical governance meeting in September 2020 as an educational intervention.

cycle2.result: Conservative management 22 (88%); percutaneous cholecystostomy 1 (4%); laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2 (8%). Mean stay 3.88 days; 30-day readmission 0 (0%).

result.other_findings: Conservative management was not associated with complications such as empyema or perforation; two patients over 60 died of unrelated causes.

result.setting: Tertiary NICU (ITU and HDU) with neonatal surgical service
result.standard: NICE NG154 and local guidelines on indications and timing of standardised (NEON) PN (within 6 hours of life if <31+0 weeks) and on electrolyte and glucose corrections

cycle1.result: 11/11 correct indication; PN on time in 2/5 babies <31+0 weeks and 11/11 for other indications; electrolyte or glucose corrections per guideline 1/3; reasons for switching or stopping documented 11/11.

result.other_findings: Delays attributed to night-time staff shortages for line insertion and lack of confidence giving peripheral PN; switches to bespoke PN were by consultants unfamiliar with NEON.

result.setting: Doctor-led rheumatology clinics without obstetric input, University College London Hospital
result.standard: BSR 2022 guideline on prescribing drugs in pregnancy and breastfeeding (linked BSR audit tool)

cycle1.dates: Clinics 24 April to 30 April 2023; notes from preceding year
cycle1.result: Antibody screening 70%; asked about wish to conceive 26%; contraception asked in 21% of those not wishing to conceive; referred to obstetric-rheumatology clinic 17%; appropriate pre-pregnancy drug counselling 22.8% of 35 on medication; none signposted to further information.

result.other_findings: 46% of patients without documented pre-pregnancy advice were taking medications unsafe in pregnancy. Audit to serve as baseline for a QI project.

result.topic: Mental Health Act treatment form accuracy
result.setting: NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde adult Community Mental Health Teams (five HSCPs)
result.standard: Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 and Mental Welfare Commission guidance on T2B/T3B forms

cycle1.result: Forms and consent uploaded to EMIS 99.8%; clinic letters mentioning treatment orders 85%; referencing treatment forms 14%; medication matching forms 90%; GP Emergency Care Summary correspondence 80%.

result.other_findings: Clozapine was missing from ECS in two cases; discrepancies mainly from additional psychotropics and dose changes. Teams contacted and clinic letter format changed; re-audit planned in 12 months.

result.setting: 147 UK hospitals; national prospective multicentre audit
result.standard: Guideline adherence in AUGIB, notably pre-endoscopic risk stratification and restrictive transfusion thresholds

cycle1.result: Pre-endoscopic risk stratification not performed in 42%. Of early transfusions (38%), 43% given at Hb >70 g/L and 24% inappropriate due to haemodynamic stability. Inpatient endoscopy 83%; endotherapy 27%; rebleeding 9.7%; in-hospital mortality 8.8%; median stay 5 days.

result.other_findings: Compared with the 2007 audit: transfusion 50% vs 43%, inpatient endoscopy 83% vs 74%, rebleeding 9.7% vs 13.3%, mortality 8.8% vs 10.0%. Inappropriate transfusion at 80 g/L was linked to higher adjusted mortality (aOR 1.60).

result.topic: VTE risk assessment in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Four acute psychiatric wards, St Ann's Hospital and Chase Farm Hospital (North London NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Trust policy and Department of Health VTE risk assessment guidance

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment done in 0/40 admissions.

result.other_findings: Action plan: present at induction, share with consultants, nurses to check VTE assessment at clerking, and re-audit in 12 months.

result.setting: National primary care prescribing dataset (ECLIPSE) linked to ophthalmology e-referrals across 32 Integrated Care Boards in England
result.standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists guideline: annual retinopathy screening after 5 years of HCQ, or after 1 year if tamoxifen, eGFR <60 or dose >5 mg/kg/day

cycle1.dates: Prescriptions from 1 January 2016; data downloaded 28 August 2025
cycle1.result: Of 13,298 meeting screening criteria, 2,808 (21.1%) seen in ophthalmology in the previous 365 days; range 0% to 45.9% by ICB.

result.other_findings: 52,419 patients prescribed HCQ; 5,338 on >5 mg/kg and 1,115 on >6.5 mg/kg. Rejected referrals and community optician attendance were not captured.

result.topic: Bosentan for digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis
result.setting: Nurse-led Rapid Access to Digital Ulcer Clinic, Royal Free Hospital, London
result.standard: NHS England clinical commissioning policy for sildenafil and bosentan in SSc digital ulceration (bosentan for severe vasculopathy or ≥3 digital ulcers; oral agents before IV prostanoids)

cycle1.result: All 21 had severe/≥3 digital ulcers; 20/21 started bosentan after inadequate response or intolerance to both sildenafil and iloprost. At 6 months (11/21), total ulcers fell from 5±2.2 to 2.7±2.2 (p < 0.05); 8/11 (72.7%) had fewer ulcers.

result.other_findings: Bosentan stopped in 3/21 in the first 6 months (2 liver function derangement, 1 non-compliance with monitoring), 2 restarted. More patients now start bosentan before IV prostanoids; to be audited in future.

result.setting: Four Older Adult Community Mental Health Teams, Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
result.standard: Trust guideline: FBC, glucose, prolactin, U&E, lipids and LFTs every 6 months; HbA1c and clozapine plasma assay annually

cycle1.result: Full compliance: FBC 100%; HbA1c 100%; LFTs 71%; U&E 57%; clozapine level 43%; glucose 0%; prolactin 0%; lipids 0% (43% had at least one test).

result.other_findings: Many tests were done by GPs or hospitals for other reasons (e.g. 50% of U&Es, 71% of LFTs); authors suggest considering dedicated clozapine clinics.

result.topic: Work loss risk in early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit cohort
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 168 (10.1%) reported work loss within three months. Predictors: age (IRR/decade 1.65), manual work (1.54), poor musculoskeletal health (1.55), anxiety/depression (1.45); final model C-statistic 0.708.

result.other_findings: An 8-point risk score was developed; DAS28 >5.1 was not independently associated with work loss.

result.topic: Prescribing errors in paediatric intensive care
result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit (24 beds)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 36 pharmacist interventions: 92% per patient and 2.3% per prescription reviewed; 77.5% (n=31) related to intravenous medicines and 52.5% (n=21) to intravenous antibiotics.

result.other_findings: Most errors were near misses on long day shifts; none with 15 or fewer items needed intervention. PDSA cycles planned towards a Trust target of 20% error reduction.

result.setting: Therapies Department, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: CSP Musculoskeletal physiotherapy service standards (2022), MSK Core Capabilities Framework (2018), Rheumatology Physiotherapy Capabilities Framework (2021), CSP Quality Assurance Standards (2012), HCPC standards

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Describes development, piloting and external review of a documentation audit tool including 'asked and cleared' inflammatory and serious pathology screening; no audit results reported.

result.setting: One adult male psychiatric intensive care unit and one adult female mental health ward
result.standard: Trust seclusion policy: reviews and documentation of commencement, periodic reviews and termination (target 100%)

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 100%; initial medical review within 1 hour 81.82% (27); 2-hourly nursing review 93.94% (31); 4-hourly medical review on time 24/33; 8-hour MDT consultant review 78.79% (26); physical health observations 100%.

result.other_findings: Delays in MDT review mainly when seclusion started at weekends or after hours. Recommendations: teaching, adding guidance to junior doctor handbook and induction, posters, and re-audit.

result.topic: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
result.setting: Paediatric rheumatology clinic, Colchester General Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: BSPAR/RCOphth 2006 uveitis screening guidelines

cycle1.result: Initial screen within 6 weeks 40/42 (95%); symptomatic seen within 1 week 4/13 (30%); screening after stopping DMARDs 9/13 (70%); ongoing screening 15/20 (75%).

result.other_findings: Non-compliance was mainly due to unavailable ophthalmology appointments. After presentation, paediatric ophthalmology clinics increased to weekly, nurse specialist liaison and a shared database were introduced; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Psoriatic arthritis management against NICE NG65
result.setting: Outpatient rheumatology clinic, Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading
result.standard: NICE NG65 spondyloarthritis guideline (NICE baseline assessment tool)

cycle1.result: CASPAR or peripheral ASAS criteria documented 78%; X-rays of symptomatic hands/feet 83%; information on PsA 58%; csDMARD monotherapy escalated 83%; flare advice access 100%; CV and skin cancer risk discussion on anti-TNF 30%.

result.other_findings: Action plan: best practice pathway on electronic patient records (CASPAR/ASAS, GRAPPA domains, CV and skin cancer risk) and nurse/therapist-led education sessions for all patients.

result.topic: Calcium monitoring after denosumab in renal impairment
result.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Bath; secondary care
result.standard: Local protocol: weekly calcium and renal function for 4 weeks after each denosumab injection if CrCl <35 ml/min

cycle1.result: 29/52 (56%) missed one or more post-injection blood tests, most often the 1st and 4th weekly checks. 18/54 (33%) developed hypocalcaemia; only 3 had adjusted calcium <2.0 mmol/l.

result.other_findings: Hypocalcaemia was generally mild, most often at 1 week, sometimes delayed to 4-6 weeks, and rarely needed treatment; CrCl did not differ between those with and without hypocalcaemia.

result.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit
result.standard: Desired vancomycin plasma concentration 15-25 mg/L

cycle1.result: 28% of concentrations within the therapeutic range.

result.intervention: Switch to continuous intravenous vancomycin infusion (loading dose 15 mg/kg then 20-50 mg/kg/day by creatinine and corrected gestational age), based on another hospital's regimen.

cycle2.result: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (60.8% first, 60% second, 65.6% subsequent); 71.3% within a 10% widened range.

result.other_findings: Comparator hospital achieved 77%; doses were prepared on the ward without aseptic facilities. Prefilled syringes and re-audit recommended.

result.setting: Tertiary referral centre, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local standard of routine feeding jejunostomy at oesophagectomy; literature morbidity 3-61%

cycle1.result: Any complication 81.8% (n=90); jejunostomy-specific complications 21.8% (n=24), commonest leak (44.8%); 4 major (Clavien-Dindo ≥III); no ischaemic small bowel necrosis (0.0% vs 3.74% in prior audit, p=0.029).

result.other_findings: Re-audit planned July 2022 to July 2023 after departmental presentation. No at-risk population identified; ERAS warnings and electronic alerts on concurrent jejunostomy feed and inotropes are being introduced.

result.topic: Vaccination uptake in immunosuppressed rheumatology patients
result.setting: Rheumatology outpatient clinics, Salford Royal Hospital
result.standard: Public Health England, BSR and EULAR vaccination guidance; target 90% uptake; departmental vaccination advice in standard letter template

cycle1.result: Influenza 63/87 (72%); pneumococcus 61/87 (70%); zoster 7/12 (64%); vaccination advice in 24/126 (19%) clinic letters.

result.other_findings: 22 of 109 had no vaccination status in GP records. Planned: writing to patients about influenza vaccination, changing the letter template, and re-audit.

result.setting: Psychiatry department inpatients, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
result.standard: Recommended baseline physical, laboratory and additional investigations before starting atypical antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Weight/BMI 64%; blood pressure 28%; waist 0%; CBC 56%; LFTs and RFTs 52%; glucose/HbA1c 44%; lipids 48%; CPK and prolactin 0%; ECG 40%; pregnancy test 0. Combined compliance about 29%.

result.intervention: Staff education, standardised baseline investigation checklists, visual reminders and better coordination with laboratory and ECG services.

cycle2.result: Weight/BMI 68%; blood pressure 76%; waist 48%; CBC 100%; LFTs 88%; RFTs 84%; glucose/HbA1c 76%; lipids 60%; CPK 48%; prolactin 60%; ECG 68%; pregnancy test 88%. Combined compliance 68%.

result.other_findings: Physical assessments improved from 30.7% to 64%, laboratory from 36% to 76.6% and additional investigations from 20% to 62% over a two-month prospective audit.

result.topic: Glycaemic monitoring in giant cell arteritis on steroids
result.setting: Fast Track GCA pathway, University College London Hospital
result.standard: BSR GCA guideline: baseline HbA1c within two weeks of steroid start; wean steroids within 18 months

cycle1.result: Baseline HbA1c 32 (69.57%); HbA1c at least 3 months after starting steroids 36 (78.26%); both baseline and follow-up by rheumatology 17/46 (36.96%); steroids weaned within 18 months 31 (67.39%).

result.other_findings: A simple glucocorticoid-induced diabetes algorithm was developed with endocrinology for use in clinic.

result.topic: Uveitis screening in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
result.setting: Paediatric tertiary centre and satellite clinics (Childhood Arthritis Prospective Study patients)
result.standard: BSPAR/RCO uveitis screening guidelines (screen within 6 weeks of referral); NHS England JIA treatment recommendations

cycle1.result: Referred for screening 50/54 (92.6%); screened 45/50 (90%); screened within 6 weeks of referral 8/45 (17.8%); JIA treatment in line with NHS England 100% of 41 documented.

result.other_findings: 4/45 (8.9%) diagnosed with uveitis. Recommendations: better communication with satellite clinics and training for junior staff on screening targets.

result.topic: MRCP use in suspected biliary disease
result.setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin; major teaching hospital
result.standard: BSG gallstone guidelines used as an adjunct

cycle1.result: 82 inpatient and 9 outpatient MRCPs; mean inpatient wait 3.2 days; ultrasound before MRCP in 41 (45%); CBD stones found in 15 (16%); 20 (22%) had surgical biliary decompression.

result.other_findings: Recommendation to develop a hospital guideline with radiology and gastroenterology.

result.setting: Community mental health resource centre (local CMHT)
result.standard: NICE guidance: lipid profile at baseline, 3 months and annually, and cardiovascular risk assessment with a validated tool (QRISK3 or ASSIGN score)

cycle1.result: Lipid profile done in the past 12 months in 22/27 (81.1%); cardiovascular risk assessed in 1/27 (3.70%); lipid results communicated to GP in 4/22 (18.18%).

result.intervention: Proposed structured process: clozapine clinic nurse creates an electronic task for the medic to review results, calculate cardiovascular risk and communicate lipids and risk to the GP in the annual review letter. Re-audit planned after 12 months.
result.other_findings: Of 40 patients on clozapine, 13 were excluded (on statins, recently started, or outside age 30–74). Of those tested, 13/22 (59.9%) had total cholesterol above 5 mmol/L.

result.topic: Carboplatin therapeutic drug monitoring in children
result.setting: not reported
result.standard: Local carboplatin protocol requirements for age criteria, baseline audiology, creatinine clearance and pharmacokinetic monitoring before administration

cycle1.dates: Data collected December 2018 to January 2019 for patients treated from 2017 to present
cycle1.result: Audiology done in 85.7% (n=6) but at baseline pre-treatment in only 28.6% (n=2); creatinine checked before first course in 71.4%; 20/26 courses (76.9%) had PK monitoring with dose modification as per protocol; 2 (29%) patients did not meet the age criteria for PK monitoring.

result.intervention: Recommended information for all practitioners on monitoring requirements and production of an SOP.
result.other_findings: Seven patients received 26 courses of carboplatin; patients were often monitored beyond 3 months of age throughout treatment.

result.topic: Live vaccination in children on immunosuppression
result.setting: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital paediatric rheumatology service, tertiary centre
result.standard: 2017 Public Health England / Green Book guidance supporting MMR and varicella vaccination on methotrexate and case-by-case after MDT assessment

cycle1.result: 81 vaccinations (38 VZV, 43 MMR) recommended by the vaccine MDT; 34/81 (42%) administered (20/38 VZV and 14/43 MMR).

result.intervention: Recommended strengthening follow-up pathways, standardising communication and reinforcing primary care engagement.
result.other_findings: Four VZV-negative patients developed varicella; 2 needed hospital admission and one developed acute kidney injury. Seven patients received prophylactic aciclovir.

result.setting: Alder Hey Children's Hospital paediatric rheumatology department, tertiary centre
result.standard: Blood monitoring guidelines for methotrexate, etanercept and adalimumab: starters must meet 6 criteria (frequency, FBC, LFTs, renal function, varicella and measles immunity); maintenance patients 4 criteria

cycle1.result: Over 60% of patients on methotrexate not monitored according to guidelines.

result.intervention: A blood clerk was introduced to the team to chase patients for blood results.

cycle2.result: 76/216 (35%) appropriately monitored, similar to the previous audit. Main failure was delayed blood timing (50% methotrexate, 65% maintenance biologics); missing varicella/measles immunity documentation in 42% of biologic starters.

result.other_findings: 72% of patients with inappropriate test frequency received a blood clerk intervention; allowing for appointment time after intervention, appropriate monitoring rose to 64% (methotrexate) and 67% (maintenance biologics). No correlation with distance to centre in the re-audit.

result.topic: Acute pain assessment and analgesia timing in children
result.setting: Paediatric wards excluding intensive care and day surgery
result.standard: Locally developed MDT standards: 80% of severe pain scores to get analgesia within 20 minutes and mild/moderate within 30 minutes with timely reassessment; 80% on regular analgesia to have pain scored at least 4-hourly; 90% on strong opioids co-prescribed naloxone

cycle1.result: Analgesia given in the same hour for 58% (34/59) severe and 30% (28/92) mild/moderate pain scores; pain reassessed within 60 minutes after 52% (37/71) and 34% (31/92) of administrations; 15/18 (83%) on regular analgesia assessed at least 4-hourly; of 11 on strong opioids 45% had no naloxone, 27% fully prescribed and 27% for respiratory depression only.

result.intervention: Planned: specific timing guidance added to the revised guideline, with medical and nursing training sessions.
result.other_findings: Observation charts allowed 15-minute pain score documentation but only hourly recordings were seen.

result.setting: Hinchingbrooke Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: NICE quality standards / CG141 for acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding

cycle1.result: Blatchford score used in 12.5% (5/40); endoscopy <24 hours in stable patients 91.4% (32/35); PPI for non-variceal bleeds 74.4% (29/39); aspirin stopped 60% (3/5); immediate endoscopy in unstable patients 100% (4/4).

result.intervention: Education of doctors about the NICE quality standards for AUGIB management over a 1-year interval.

cycle2.result: Blatchford score used in 50% (11/22); endoscopy <24 hours in stable patients 53% (10/19); PPI for non-variceal bleeds 77% (17/22); aspirin stopped 80% (4/5); immediate endoscopy in unstable patients 100% (3/3).

result.other_findings: Endoscopic management was fully compliant in both cycles (clips 100%; variceal bleeds all given terlipressin, antibiotics and band ligation). Time to endoscopy in stable patients worsened.

result.topic: Aminoglycoside prescribing and level monitoring in neonates
result.setting: Two neonatal units in one Trust
result.standard: Trust Neonatal Infection Guideline: 100% adherence to criteria, amikacin 15 mg/kg, level at 24 hours before second dose, further doses only if level <5 mg/L or on pharmacist advice

cycle1.result: 100% adhered to guideline criteria and 100% prescribed 15 mg/kg; 12 (24%) had no level at 24 hours; of 38 with 24-hour levels only 6 (16%) were <5 mg/L; 17/23 (74%) in range at 36 hours; 2 patients received doses despite levels >5 mg/L.

result.intervention: Recommended change from 24-hourly to 36-hourly dosing; re-audit planned in one year.
result.other_findings: No direct correlation seen between gestational age, severity of illness and amikacin levels.

result.setting: Paediatric gastroenterology centre
result.standard: BSPGHAN guidelines: eleven azathioprine monitoring points (clinic attendance, height, weight, baseline VZV status, TPMT, and FBC, U&Es, amylase, CRP and LFT monitoring)

cycle1.result: Only 16 patients (19%) met all eleven points; 27 (24.5%) fully compliant with blood monitoring frequency; TPMT measured in 104 (97%) but late in 48 (46%); weight and height not documented in 31 (28%) and 47 (43%); baseline VZV not checked in 23 (21%).

result.intervention: Suggested shared-care guidelines, order sets with all parameters at diagnosis and a tick-box monitoring proforma for clinic.
result.other_findings: Suboptimal monitoring correlated with living further from the centre (p=0.008) and tablet formulation (p=0.000); NHS England specialist commissioning rules prevent paediatric shared care.

result.topic: Employment loss in early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 168 (10.1%) reported employment loss within three months; manual work IRR 1.82 (95% CI 1.37-2.42); direct effect after mediators IRR 1.54 (95% CI 1.15-2.06).

result.other_findings: Disease activity, mental health and symptom burden together explained only 16.5% of the occupational effect.

result.setting: MBT-I groups within Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: Cohorts in October 2023, July 2024 and February 2025
cycle1.result: Median attendance 8.5 sessions; inpatient admission during MBT-I 2.1%; 20.8% completed and referred for further therapy, 12.5% completed needing no further intervention; 22.9% did not complete and 37.5% did not commence.

result.other_findings: Referrals mostly from secondary mental health services with minimal primary care referrals.

result.setting: Tertiary/quaternary paediatric hospital
result.standard: PHE Start Smart then Focus: blood culture before therapy, senior antimicrobial review at 48–72 hours, and IV to oral switch when set clinical criteria are met

cycle1.result: 100% had blood cultures within 72 hours of starting therapy; 82% had senior review at 48–72 hours; 46% eligible to switch to oral at 72 hours, of whom 33% were switched.

result.intervention: Recommended an IV to oral switch guideline, education of pharmacists and nurses, and exploring hard stops on IV antimicrobials in the electronic system.
result.other_findings: 55% had a positive blood culture. Small sample due to complex inclusion criteria and multiple hospital interfaces; need for better documentation of prescribing decisions.

result.topic: Early inflammatory arthritis waiting times and DMARD start
result.setting: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust rheumatology department, Preston
result.standard: NICE QS33: QS2 seen in rheumatology within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 newly diagnosed RA offered short-term glucocorticoids and combination DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral

cycle1.dates: First year of the NEIAA (dates not stated)
cycle1.result: 22 patients (8.9%) seen within 3 weeks of referral; 5 (7%) started DMARD within 6 weeks; mean wait 66 days (range 5-138) to be seen and diagnosed; 65 (90%) given bridging steroids; 65 (92%) started DMARDs.

result.intervention: Process mapping and driver diagrams identified changes: primary care referral guidelines, more triage and new appointment capacity, simpler booking, text reminders, one-stop clinic with ultrasound, more drug education clinic capacity.
result.other_findings: 246 patients recruited, 71 with confirmed RA; 3-month follow-up forms completed in 61 (86%). Further waits of about 50 days if sent for investigations and 25–39 days for drug education.

result.setting: Rohallion Clinic medium and low secure forensic psychiatry unit, Murray Royal Hospital, NHS Tayside
result.standard: Local and national guidance: 100% documented plan for oral and IM as-required medication; 100% offered oral before IM; 100% side-effect monitoring within 1 hour of rapid tranquillisation

cycle1.result: 38 (81%) had as-required medicines prescribed; 24 (63%) of these had a documented plan; reasons for IM medication and side-effect monitoring documented 25.42% of the time. Standards 1, 2 and 3 not met.

result.intervention: Action plan: work with clinical team and pharmacist to improve documentation, and add headers to online assessment templates. Re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Lorazepam was most often prescribed, in line with local guidance; dosing frequency (mostly 4-hourly) was compliant.

result.setting: Croydon University Hospital rheumatology department
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 33 internal referrals (18 from FLS, 7 COTE, 3 orthopaedics) and 71 GP referrals; commonest reason intolerance to oral medication (36), then declining BMD (14).

result.intervention: GPs advised to try alternative oral bisphosphonates or effervescent alendronic acid before referral; COTE team agreed to initiate and continue IV zoledronate.
result.other_findings: Workload review aimed to free rheumatology slots for early inflammatory arthritis.

result.setting: 36 dermatology teams from 30 NHS trusts (national audit)
result.standard: BSDS sustainable skin surgery audit standards and checklist (scored out of 30), based on BSDS 2022 sustainability guidance

cycle1.result: Mean score 17.3/30 (95% CI 16.3–18.3; range 12–23); mean waste 1.0 kg per procedure; mean recycling rate 8.6%; 17/30 trusts (57%) had recycling bins; 19/30 (63%) had a mobile smoke evacuator.

result.other_findings: Recycling rate was lower than the 16% in the 2022 study; Mohs lists generated more waste; trusts recycling single-use instruments had high recycling rates.

result.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham, teaching hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Teriparatide (n=24): 17 (70%) had a documented post-teriparatide plan, 2 adverse events, no fractures after cessation. Romosozumab (n=26): 7 adverse events including heart failure and hypocalcaemia, no fractures after cessation. All met NICE criteria.

result.other_findings: Most transitioned to zoledronic acid after anabolic therapy.

result.topic: Early inflammatory arthritis waiting times and DMARD start
result.setting: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham rheumatology service, compared with national NEIAA data
result.standard: NICE RA quality standard 33: QS1 referral within 3 working days of primary care presentation; QS2 conventional DMARD within 6 weeks of referral

cycle1.dates: April 2018 to March 2024 (QEHB); May 2018 to March 2020 (national)
cycle1.result: QEHB QS1: 79% (115/146) White vs 21% (31/146) BAME referred within 3 days; QS2: 26.5% (27/102) BAME vs 73.5% (75/102) White. Nationally QS1 43% (12,561/29,417) White vs 47% (2,333/4,964) BAME; QS2 60% (723/1,204) BAME vs 57% (4,919/8,695) White.

result.other_findings: 24% of QEHB patients were BAME vs 14% nationally; authors call for research into causes of ethnic disparities.

result.setting: 36 dermatology teams from 30 NHS trusts (national audit)
result.standard: BSDS sustainable skin surgery audit standards and checklist (scored out of 30), based on BSDS 2022 sustainability guidance

cycle1.result: Mean score 17.3/30 (95% CI 16.3–18.3; range 12–23); mean waste 1.0 kg per procedure; mean recycling rate 8.6%; 17/30 trusts (57%) had recycling bins; 19/30 (63%) had a mobile smoke evacuator.

result.other_findings: Recycling rate was lower than the 16% in the 2022 study; Mohs lists generated more waste; trusts recycling single-use instruments had high recycling rates.

result.topic: Influenza vaccination and asthma prescribing in children
result.setting: GP surgeries in Liverpool CCG (seven participating), primary care
result.standard: BTS/SIGN British guideline on the management of asthma 2016 for prescribing; influenza vaccine uptake

cycle1.result: 148 (31.2%) had flu vaccination; 194/297 (65.3%) prescriptions followed BTS guidelines.

result.other_findings: Commonest non-compliance was salbutamol monotherapy or no medication. Low deprivation and age 5 or under associated with higher vaccination (p<0.05).

result.topic: Self-management advice in early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust rheumatology department, Preston
result.standard: NICE QS33 QS4: RA patients offered educational and self-management activities within 1 month of diagnosis

cycle1.dates: Second year of the NEIAA (dates not stated)
cycle1.result: All RA patients received written information at baseline; only 39 (71%) documented as given self-management advice at 3-month follow-up; 41 (56%) started DMARD within 6 weeks of referral.

result.intervention: Driver diagrams with patient group input identified changes: agreed definition of self-management, patient activation measure, different delivery formats and expert patients.
result.other_findings: Patients felt self-management advice within the first 3 months was too soon, questioning the QS target. 3-month follow-up available for 56 (77%).

result.setting: Complex Musculoskeletal Clinic, rheumatology department, secondary care
result.standard: 2017 EULAR recommendations for the management of fibromyalgia

cycle1.result: Before referral: pharmacological treatment 34/50 (68%), physiotherapy 5/50 (10%), psychological input 3/50 (6%); referred to multidisciplinary pain management programme 4/50 (8%).

cycle2.result: Before referral: pharmacological treatment 71/82 (87%, p=0.008), physiotherapy 28/82 (34%, p=0.002), psychological input 16/82 (20%, p=0.03); referred to pain management programme 64/82 (78%, p<0.0001); all had pain and function assessed; psychosocial context assessed in 64/82 (78%); information given to 53 (65%).

result.other_findings: All medication recommendations were EULAR compliant. Giving patients information about their condition was identified as an area for improvement.

result.topic: Monocyte count in giant cell arteritis diagnosis
result.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases GCA clinic, Bath
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 109/301 (36%) diagnosed with GCA; monocyte count predictive of GCA (AUC 0.83, 95% CI 0.77-0.90, p<0.0001); cut-off ≥0.9 gave specificity >95% and positive LR of 10.

result.other_findings: 55/301 had started glucocorticoids before baseline bloods; monocyte sensitivity dropped 20% after at least one glucocorticoid dose.

result.setting: General adult psychiatry services, NHS Grampian
result.standard: MHRA valproate guidance and Pregnancy Prevention Programme, including completed Annual Risk Acknowledgement Form

cycle1.result: 97% in contact with psychiatry services; only one patient (3%) had an ARAF completed and scanned to e-notes.

result.intervention: Teams contacted by telephone and email and encouraged to complete the documentation.

cycle2.result: Completed ARAF in 21 patients; completion rose from 3% to 54%.

result.other_findings: 66% of women in cycle 1 were aged 45–60.

result.setting: Children's hospital
result.standard: MHRA May 2014 drug safety update and NPPG May 2015 statement on domperidone (dose, duration, indication, ECG monitoring in high risk, non-pharmacological trial in GORD)

cycle1.dates: 1 January 2014 to before the NPPG alert (May 2015)
cycle1.result: Dose 43/50 (86%); duration 6/50 (12%); indication 9/50 (18%); ECG monitoring in high risk 12/33 (36%); non-pharmacological trial in GORD 11/17 (64%).

result.intervention: National MHRA and NPPG alerts on domperidone.

cycle2.result: Dose 10/10 (100%); duration 1/10 (10%); indication 1/10 (10%); ECG monitoring 0/4 (0%); non-pharmacological trial 2/3 (66%).

result.other_findings: Cardiac monitoring in at-risk patients remained poor; many children still received domperidone off-licence long term.

result.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Royal United Hospitals Bath
result.standard: NICE NG100 rheumatoid arthritis annual review standards

cycle1.dates: 12 months before an appointment in January 2019
cycle1.result: DAS28 documented 74.4% (253/340); erosions 42% (144/340); blood pressure 33% (113/340); mental health screen 7.9% (27/340); neck pain 14%; respiratory 21%; eye 21%; bone health 27.9% (95/340); AHP referral considered 38%; HAQ 22%.

result.intervention: Planned digital RA annual review tool incorporating PROMs.
result.other_findings: Variation between clinicians in documentation; VAS recorded in 73% (248/340).

result.setting: Occupational therapy rheumatology service, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean BMI 33.5 kg/m²; 38% BMI >35; only around half of letters for BMI >30 recorded weight, and none discussed weight management plans or referrals.

result.intervention: Recommended training for rheumatology staff on raising weight and better BMI recording.
result.other_findings: Mean 5.2 comorbidities and 6.6 medications per patient; fatigue reported by 61%.

result.setting: Three adult mental health inpatient units (East, Central, West), Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NCISH, NHS CQUIN and Welsh Crisis Care Concordat: follow-up within 72 hours of discharge and discharge documentation of risk, MSE, medication and care plan

cycle1.result: Previous regional audit found variable compliance and incomplete documentation.

result.intervention: Initial quality improvement measures (not detailed) after the first audit; standardised electronic templates, discharge checklists, automated alerts and audit feedback introduced.

cycle2.result: 72-hour follow-up 78.4% (29/37); discharge plan 86.5%; MSE 78.8%; risk assessment 72.7%; medication 63.6%. Modest improvement from baseline.

result.other_findings: Central site 100% follow-up; East 57% with medication documentation 20%; West 66.7% with risk recorded in 46.2%.

result.topic: Early inflammatory arthritis waiting times and DMARD start
result.setting: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust rheumatology department, Preston
result.standard: NICE QS33: QS2 seen within 3 weeks of referral; QS3 RA started on DMARDs within 6 weeks of referral

cycle1.result: 10% of all patients seen within 3 weeks; 7% of RA cohort (n=77) started DMARD within 6 weeks.

result.intervention: Primary care referral guidelines, prompts for RF/CCP requests and changed antibody report wording, more triage and new appointment capacity (extra consultant, upskilled ESP), simpler booking, more drug education and monitoring clinic capacity, signposting to NRAS.

cycle2.result: 54% seen within 3 weeks; 56% of RA cohort (n=73) started DMARD within 6 weeks.

result.other_findings: Remission/low disease activity at 3 months rose from 54% (year 1) to 69% (year 2); baseline disease activity was lower in year 2.

result.setting: Rheumatology unit, University Hospital Southampton
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 24 PJP cases; 79% on methotrexate, 70% on glucocorticoids; lymphopenia in 75%; 18/24 needed HDU/ICU and 7 died; only one on prophylaxis at diagnosis.

result.other_findings: Regular audits of BSR PJP prophylaxis in vasculitis on cyclophosphamide since 2016 may explain few cases in that group.

result.setting: East Bromley Intensive Case Management in Psychosis team, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: 2024 MHRA valproate guidance including male patients: risk discussion, contraception advice, informed consent, MHRA materials, dual-signed ARAF

cycle1.result: Risk discussions 37% (F 80%, M 17%); contraception advice 15% (F 80%, M 3%); informed consent 61% (F 80%, M 20%); MHRA materials 11% (F 60%, M 6%); dual-signed ARAF in eligible females 0%.

result.intervention: Clinician education, 26 structured outpatient reviews, distribution of MHRA materials and a live ARAF tracking system.

cycle2.result: Male cohort: risk discussions 17%→87%; contraception advice 3%→83%; informed consent 20%→87%; MHRA materials 6%→83%; 100% of eligible females reviewed for second-consultant sign-off.

result.other_findings: 13% of patients switched to alternative treatments after structured reviews and 9% were considering alternatives.

result.setting: Six institutions in five countries (Myositis Audit and Research Collaborative)
result.country: Multinational (Australia, Brazil, Hong Kong and others)
result.standard: IMACS guidelines for malignancy screening in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies

cycle1.result: Full IMACS screening panel received by 7.5% of high-risk, 6.6% of intermediate-risk and 27.5% of standard-risk patients; 9.1% of high-risk patients had annual screening for 3 years as recommended.

result.other_findings: Over-screening seen in intermediate-risk (6.0%), standard-risk (6.6%) and IBM/JDM (41.2%) cohorts; following IMACS would raise screening costs 1.5-2.9-fold.

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatric units, Hamad Hospital (Hamad Medical Corporation)
result.standard: Institutional Smoking Cessation Policy (smoking status, dependence severity, NRT initiation and monitoring, education, referral, discharge planning)

cycle1.result: Initial nicotine dependence screening >97%; dependence severity documented in 30.2%; appropriate NRT strength 12.3%; NRT side-effect monitoring 0%; 20% of smokers received NRT; Tobacco Control Center referral 18%; motivational interventions 1.8%; patient/family education 0%; NRT on discharge summary 3.3%.

result.intervention: Recommended targeted staff training, better access to educational resources and structured monitoring and documentation systems.
result.other_findings: About 40% of admitted patients were current smokers; 29% declined NRT.

result.setting: North Staffordshire Fracture Liaison Service, Midlands Partnership Foundation Trust
result.standard: FLS policy (in line with national guidance) that patients aged 85 or over with fragility fracture are started empirically on oral bisphosphonate by the GP

cycle1.dates: Fractures December 2018 to October 2020; audited October 2020
cycle1.result: 160 (40%) had a bisphosphonate prescribed; over 90% alendronic acid.

result.intervention: The standard GP recommendation letter was rewritten using GP feedback to address barriers, including advice on relative contraindications and referral.

cycle2.dates: Fractures December 2020 to May 2021; audited July 2021

result.other_findings: Median time from fracture to assessment was shorter in cycle 2 (5 vs 9 months), which may partly explain the rise.

result.setting: Mater Dei Hospital (Clinical Genetics Laboratory records)
result.standard: EULAR 2016 recommendations for FMF management

cycle1.result: Initial follow-up within 6 months 54.1% (33); 3-monthly SAA/CRP with dose escalation 8.3% (2/24); 6-monthly monitoring 31.2% (19); SAA and CK on yearly bloods 20.9% and 12.5%; no 3-monthly SAA/CRP during dose reduction.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic delay over 10 years in 29.5%; colchicine delayed over 1 month after genetic diagnosis in 18.0%; no patients received canakinumab.

result.setting: Torbay and South Devon NHS Trust
result.standard: Joint ESGAR/EAES/EFISDS/ESGE guidelines on gallbladder polyp management

cycle1.result: 86% appropriately offered surgery for polyps ≥10 mm; 40% with polyps >5 mm and risk factors not offered cholecystectomy; 44% without risk factors not offered appropriate follow-up; all without risk factors with polyps ≤5 mm appropriately managed.

result.intervention: Recommended unified local or national guidelines and multidisciplinary consensus.
result.other_findings: Most patients with polyps ≤5 mm and risk factors were not offered ultrasound surveillance.

result.topic: Outsourced clinical trial medicine delivery times
result.setting: Hospital clinical trials unit without onsite aseptic unit
result.standard: IMP arrival at the clinical trials unit by 1300h (later arrival defined as delayed treatment)

cycle1.dates: Six to twelve months (dates not stated)
cycle1.result: Manufacturing unit 1: 33 items, 71.86% late. Manufacturing unit 2: 23 items, 30% late (mostly due to late prescribing at site).

result.intervention: Recommended agreed KPIs with third-party suppliers, scoping local aseptic manufacture, and timely prescribing.
result.other_findings: The closer unit (5.9 miles vs 63 miles) had fewer late deliveries.

result.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: SWYT seclusion and long-term segregation policy and seclusion toolkit (medical review within 1 hour, 4-hourly reviews, first MDT, independent MDT within 8-18 hours, daily reviews)

cycle1.result: First MDT within 08:00–22:00 next day 92.7%; out-of-hours reviews adherent 95%; daily non-RC medical reviews 87.2%; independent MDT reviews 24.2%; resident doctor review within 1 hour 64.4%; daily MDT reviews 66.6%.

result.intervention: Recommended prompts for independent MDT reviews, seclusion toolkit in new doctors' induction and discussion with RCs on documentation.
result.other_findings: Low daily MDT review figure was linked to incorrect documentation on the seclusion proforma.

result.setting: Community (primary care) ANA requests across West of Scotland, tested at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 605 (19.67%) positive; 190 (31.57%) of positives referred; new CTD diagnosed in 38 patients; 314 (51.9%) of positives were 1/80 homogeneous.

result.intervention: Recommended clearer testing guidelines and targeted education for primary care clinicians.
result.other_findings: Testing cost approximately £41,393 with low diagnostic yield.

result.setting: Medway Community Mental Health Team (Gillingham, Chatham, Rochester localities)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Report completion Chatham 66.7%, Gillingham 73.3%, Rochester 33%; capacity forms completed in over two-thirds (100% Rochester to 66% Chatham); completion 73% and 50% for the two responsible clinicians.

result.intervention: Centralised communication system, improved documentation access and enhanced administrative processes; further audit planned.
result.other_findings: Only three of six clinicians completed reports; reports clustered around review dates.

result.topic: Analgesia in sickle cell pain crisis
result.setting: Paediatric inpatient admissions in one Trust
result.standard: 100% prescribed regular paracetamol and NSAIDs unless contraindicated (NICE CG143, BCSH); 100% prescribed appropriate doses by weight and age per local policy

cycle1.result: 45% (95% CI 31.9%–58.1%) prescribed regular analgesia; 78% (95% CI 67.9%–88.9%) prescribed appropriate doses. Neither standard met.

result.intervention: Recommended education and training, an integrated care pathway booklet and a compulsory weight field on electronic prescribing.
result.other_findings: Incorrect doses were due to wrong weights on the electronic system (n=4) and age-only dosing (n=8).

result.setting: Milton Keynes University Hospital, district general hospital
result.standard: BAD national non-melanoma skin cancer excision audit 2016 benchmarks (concordance 95%, complete excision ~98%); RCPath 10-day histology target; 28-day faster diagnosis standard

cycle1.result: Clinical–histological concordance 91%; complete excision with good margins 83% (involved margins 6%); only 22% of histology reports within 10 days (mean 33 days); mean 8 days from report to outcome communication; 9.5% considered for Mohs though 48% anatomically suitable.

result.intervention: Recommended referral documentation templates, GP awareness of routine referral for low-risk BCC, a dermatology surgical logbook and better local access to Mohs surgery.
result.other_findings: 45% of referral types were undocumented; 36% came via the 2-week-wait pathway.

result.setting: West Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust rheumatology, district general hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Active synovitis in 17 (40%); 27 (63%) had DMARD started or switched after ultrasound; fibromyalgia patients less likely to escalate (8/20, 40% vs 19/23, 82.6%; p=0.004).

result.other_findings: Synovitis on ultrasound was associated with DMARD escalation (82.4% vs 50%, p=0.03); ultrasound avoided escalation in a sizeable proportion.

result.topic: Falls and bone health assessment after fracture
result.setting: University College London Hospital, central London
result.standard: 2017 NOGG guidelines, NICE CG161 falls in older people, and local hospital osteoporosis screening policy

cycle1.result: Only 5 (12%) had a full falls assessment. Osteoporosis assessment in 8/8 (100%) NOF vs 9/35 (25.7%) non-NOF; FRAX in 3/8 (37.5%) vs 3/35 (8.6%); referral to bone health clinic 1/8 vs 0/35.

result.intervention: Planned education programme and a standardised proforma embedded in the electronic record.
result.other_findings: Lying/standing BP recorded in 37.5% NOF and 14.3% non-NOF; hip fracture patients had more complete assessments than other fractures.

result.topic: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in children
result.setting: Redcar generic CAMHS, TEWV
result.standard: NICE guidance on baseline investigations and monitoring for children and young people on antipsychotics; TEWV (2024) Psychotropic Monitoring Guide

cycle1.result: Overall compliance below 50%; side-effect assessment at 3 months 80%; ECG consideration/completion at 12 months 100%; weight, height, growth chart, waist, BP, HR, bloods and pre-treatment ECG below 80%.

result.intervention: Recommended improved handover between teams, better communication and documentation with GPs, and agreement on where to record monitoring data.
result.other_findings: No physical health clinic in the team; bloods and ECGs requested from GPs and results hard to track.

result.setting: Meadowbrook Unit inpatient mental health unit, Salford, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust seclusion policy: eight core medical review criteria plus two best-practice criteria

cycle1.result: No reviews met all eight criteria; most common number met was one (n=9). Physical health 70%, psychiatric health 40%, medication side effects 0%, harms of seclusion 2%, decision to continue 97%, steps to end seclusion 25%.

result.intervention: Local teaching and presentations, communication to line managers and posters of trust standards in clinical areas.

cycle2.result: Seven reviews met all eight criteria; most common number met was four or five (n=12). Physical health 82%, psychiatric health 66%, medication side effects 19%, harms of seclusion 14%, decision to continue 91%, steps to end seclusion 23%.

result.other_findings: Small declines in documenting the decision to continue and steps to end seclusion; asleep, senior-led and undocumented reviews may have affected 2025 results.

result.topic: Employment loss in early inflammatory arthritis
result.setting: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit, rheumatology services in England and Wales
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 5999 (48%) in paid work; at diagnosis 171 (4.7%) had stopped work and 336 (9.2%) changed jobs due to EIA; absenteeism in 685 (29.5%). Good EULAR response at 3 months associated with improved work outcomes (p<0.001).

result.other_findings: Semi-routine and routine workers were more likely to stop work.

result.topic: Sodium monitoring on antidepressants in older adults
result.setting: Psychiatry of Old Age inpatient unit, North Dublin Mental Health Services for Older Persons
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines: serum sodium monitoring 2–4 weeks after antidepressant initiation or dose change in high-risk patients

cycle1.result: Baseline U&E on admission in all patients; follow-up within 2–4 weeks of initiation in 50%; U&E within four weeks of dose escalation in 16%.

result.intervention: Reminder stickers placed in each patient's file and educational discussion with the MDT. Second cycle underway.
result.other_findings: Mirtazapine and venlafaxine were the most common antidepressants; 50% had dose increases during admission.

result.topic: COVID-19 vaccination in patients on biologics
result.setting: Rheumatology clinics, Southend University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 329 received two doses, 8 one dose and 15 (4.3%) unvaccinated; 146 had mild side effects; 3 (2.1%) grade 3 or above; 15 (10%) reported arthritis flare.

result.other_findings: Reasons for declining included fear of reactions or flares and mistrust of the vaccine.

result.setting: Royal Berkshire Hospital rheumatology, district general hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Side-effect discussion documented at baseline in <10%; 2% MACE and 3% herpes zoster; 36% discontinued; remission or significant reduction in disease activity in 64%.

result.intervention: Recommended better patient education before starting treatment.
result.other_findings: 43% had failed two or three biologics before a JAK inhibitor; 64% started on baricitinib.

result.setting: 39 UK dermatology centres (BAD national audit)
result.standard: BAD 2016 UK guidelines for management of SJS/TEN in adults, audit standards

cycle1.result: Within 24 h: SCORTEN 52% (76/147), medication list 77% (113), medication timelines 71% (104). Initial assessment: eyes by ophthalmologist 48% (71), mouth 88% (130), genital skin 70% (103), urinary tract 63% (93). Daily assessments in first 10 days: mouth 18%, eyes 8%, urinary tract and genital skin 10%. Culprit drug avoidance advice 58% (76/130); medic alert request 6% (9/147).

result.intervention: Suggested an assessment and clinical review checklist.
result.other_findings: Drug causality assessment was documented adequately; 29% of UK dermatology centres took part.

result.topic: Measurable oral liquid doses in children
result.setting: Paediatric inpatient areas in one Trust (paper and electronic prescribing)
result.standard: Local dispensing standard: prescribed volumes measurable on the printed graduations of one oral syringe

cycle1.result: Electronic prescriptions: 61/257 (24%) not measurable; paper charts: 57/303 (19%) not measurable (p=0.19). 77 of 457 liquid doses needed up to 4% adjustment and 10 up to 9%; 19/560 (3.4%) needed measuring to two decimal places.

result.intervention: Recommended dose rounding at prescribing and adding liquid strength information to local guidelines.
result.other_findings: Frequently non-measurable drugs included diazepam, alimemazine, chloral hydrate, azithromycin, metronidazole, paracetamol and ibuprofen; the electronic system had no automatic rounding.

result.setting: Inpatient addiction ward, Allied Hospital II, Faisalabad
result.standard: Predefined standards from NICE guidance, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and international recommendations

cycle1.result: Met targets: stimulant history 94.7%, temporal relationship 89.5%, exclusion of delirium 100%, baseline observations 94.7%, MSE 94.7%, prescribing details 100%. Below target: toxicology 42.1%, blood glucose 52.6%, structured risk assessment 78.9%, de-escalation 73.7%, medication safety checks 78.9%, post-medication monitoring 84.2%, reassessment 73.7%.

result.intervention: Standardised MIP admission checklist and targeted staff education; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: MIP accounted for 19/82 (23.2%) of inpatient addiction admissions, ranging 18.2% to 33.3% per month.

result.topic: Surgical site infection surveillance in hip fracture
result.setting: Irish Hip Fracture Database, national clinical audit across Irish hospitals
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: First full year of data received May 2024
cycle1.result: Overall SSI incidence <1%; SSI increased length of stay from 19 to 34 days; completeness of additional variables 68 to 100%.

result.intervention: SSI dataset (ECDC-based) embedded into the IHFD portal after a three-hospital pilot, with monthly training webinars and infographics; dataset refined by PDSA.
result.other_findings: Hip fracture governance committees now include infection prevention and control members; quarterly SSI reports are sent to hospitals.

result.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit
result.standard: Aciclovir dosing per BNF for Children and trust empirical antibiotic guidelines

cycle1.result: 26% (9/35) of aciclovir doses incorrect; wrong drop-down option chosen in 78% (7/9) of incorrect prescriptions.

result.intervention: Aciclovir drop-down options in the electronic prescribing system reordered so the most frequently used option appeared first (from 01/02/17).

cycle2.result: 17% (5/30) of doses incorrect; wrong drop-down option in 0% (0/5) of incorrect prescriptions.

result.other_findings: Error rate was 14% (7/50) when the correct drop-down was chosen vs 47% (7/15) when the wrong option was selected.

result.topic: Proton pump inhibitor prescribing in children
result.setting: Hospital outpatient pharmacy
result.standard: Trust guidance: lansoprazole capsules/orodispersible tablets first line; three standards (appropriate PPI, documented indication, appropriate dose)

cycle1.result: Appropriate PPI 76%; documented indication 88%; appropriate dose 100%. Infants and toddlers had the lowest appropriate PPI choice (63%).

result.intervention: Recommended clinicians monitor prescribing and switch omeprazole suspension to lansoprazole where appropriate.
result.other_findings: Lansoprazole accounted for 64 (77%) prescriptions; 12% had no documented indication.

result.setting: Inpatient psychiatry ward, Allied Hospital II, Faisalabad
result.standard: Pre-RT standards from NICE guidance, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and BAP/NAPICU consensus

cycle1.result: De-escalation documented 71%; clear indication 83%; pre-RT workup 47%; baseline observations 85%; capacity/consent 90%; cardiac/QT risk 85% (haloperidol); reassessment before repeat dosing 42%; airway risk 78% (benzodiazepines); contraindications/interactions 66%.

result.intervention: Structured pre-RT checklist and staff education.

cycle2.result: De-escalation 92%; clear indication 96%; pre-RT workup 85%; reassessment before repeat dosing 92%; airway risk 92%; contraindications 85%; other domains met or exceeded standards.

result.other_findings: Medication details were documented in 100% at baseline.

result.setting: Two district general hospitals, Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust; day case laparoscopic cholecystectomy and inguinal hernia repair
result.standard: GIRFT guidelines for day case discharge prescribing (analgesia, antiemetics, laxatives)

cycle1.result: 25% of patients received the correct discharge medications.

result.intervention: Pre-populated discharge medication order set created in the EPIC electronic record.

cycle2.result: 83% of patients received the correct discharge medications.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Three inpatient mental health wards across two hospitals
result.standard: NICE guidance and local trust policies on cardiovascular assessment, ECG, metabolic monitoring and risk–benefit documentation when prescribing antipsychotics

cycle1.result: BP, heart rate and weight recorded in 19/20; ECG on admission in 8; ECG before or within 72 hours of antipsychotic start in 3; QTc documented in 6; HbA1c checked in 11; ongoing metabolic monitoring in 7; no documented cardiovascular risk–benefit discussion in any case.

result.other_findings: Medication was reviewed regularly at MDT meetings for all patients. Suggested actions include staff awareness, prescribing checklists and electronic prompts.

result.setting: All Scottish centres with Code Red activations for major trauma (national audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 56 activations; pre-hospital TXA 70%; ED arrival to CRC transfusion 9 mins; ED arrival to FFP 50 mins; clotting screen order to result 119 mins; survival to discharge 63%.

cycle2.result: 96 activations; 77 (93%, n=93) received pre-hospital TXA; median ED arrival to CRC transfusion 4 minutes (IQR 0–17) and to FFP 16 minutes (IQR 5–28); median ED arrival to FBC result 70 mins and clotting 74 mins; 65 (68%) survived to discharge.

result.other_findings: A middle audit (1 Nov 2015–31 Dec 2017, 66 activations) was also compared; pre-hospital transfusions rose (16, 48, 73) and CRC and FFP wastage increased. Median 999 call to Code Red activation was 80 minutes.

result.topic: Patient involvement in national early inflammatory arthritis audit results
result.setting: Rheumatology department, Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust, Preston
result.standard: National Early Inflammatory Arthritis Audit (NEIAA) seven quality standards

cycle1.result: Significant room for improvement across all seven quality standards (figures not given).

result.intervention: Results shared with MDT and an NRAS patient support group (45 patients and carers), driver diagrams developed and a patient waiting-area poster produced.
result.other_findings: Patients suggested community awareness posters, an awareness day, more lunchtime meetings and an Expert Patient role; they advised removing alarming statistics from the poster.

result.topic: Contact allergy to alkyl glucosides on patch testing
result.setting: Eleven patch testing centres in the UK and Ireland
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 57 patients (2.1%) had a positive reaction to at least one alkyl glucoside; DG 5% pet. positive in 36 (1.3%), LG 3% aq. in 24 (0.9%).

result.other_findings: Six centres testing 1099 patients in a cosmetic series found a further 14 (1.3%) positives. Concomitant positivity between petrolatum and aqueous preparations was variable, and irritant reactions were frequent.

result.topic: MRI requesting and reporting in axial spondyloarthritis
result.setting: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, inflammatory back pain MRI protocol
result.standard: ASAS guidance on requesting and reporting MRI in suspected axial spondyloarthritis

cycle1.result: Requests: age in 11 (11.4%), sex in 6 (3.8%), HLA-B27 in 35 (22.2%), back pain duration in 30 (18.9%), suspected diagnosis in 149 (94.3%). Reports: bone marrow oedema mentioned in 128 (81.0%), fat metaplasia in 10 (6.3%), statement on whether 'in keeping with axSpA' in 98 (62.0%).

result.other_findings: Chronic structural changes were mentioned in only 82 (51.2%) of reports. Joint rheumatology–radiology work is ongoing with a re-audit planned.

result.topic: Steroid emergency card and adrenal insufficiency advice
result.setting: Royal National Hospital for Rheumatic Diseases, Royal United Hospitals, Bath; new giant cell arteritis cases
result.standard: National Patient Safety Alert (August 2020) on steroid emergency cards and adrenal insufficiency risk

cycle1.result: No patients given steroid emergency cards at first visit (4 during follow-up); 5/90 given written information on adrenal insufficiency risk at first visit; 1/90 given information on symptoms; none given sick day rules at first visit (9 during follow-up).

result.intervention: Dedicated GCA clinics and improved follow-up, standardised written steroid information and personalised reduction plans, education sessions for medical and nursing teams, and electronic prescribing of emergency cards (being incorporated).
result.other_findings: Inconsistent follow-up pathways may have compounded the problem. Re-audit planned for January 2022.

result.topic: Treatment pathway before prostanoid therapy in Raynaud's and digital ulcers
result.setting: Rheumatology day unit, Freeman Hospital, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: NHS England 2015 commissioning policy pathway for digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis

cycle1.result: Prior trials: CCB 77.4%, ACEi/ARB 41.1%, fluoxetine 9.59%, sildenafil 87.1%, tadalafil 25.8%; 22.6% of SSc patients had tried bosentan; only 2 SSc patients (6.45%) had trialled all pathway drugs before prostanoid.

result.other_findings: Mean 5.92 epoprostenol infusions per patient per year, estimated £2700 per patient per year versus about £1350 for first-year bosentan with monitoring.

result.setting: Mulberry Ward, acute adult psychiatric inpatient ward, Scunthorpe
