result.standard: NICE NG10 (2015); traffic-light compliance green ≥80%, orange 60–79%, red <60%

cycle1.result: 37 RT incidents in 17 patients; seclusion used in 30%; compliance figures not given.

cycle2.result: 79 RT incidents in 10 patients; seclusion fell to 5%; NICE compliance remained excellent for risk assessment, patient rights and documentation, but post-RT monitoring, debriefing, medication review and incident reporting remained below standard.

result.other_findings: Advance directives were absent in both audits. RT frequency among women rose from 2.2 to 10.5 incidents per patient, and lorazepam became the main agent (43% to 69.6%).

result.setting: Outpatient and community patients receiving melatonin from hospital pharmacy
result.standard: Regular clinic review of melatonin treatment (efficacy, dose, duration)

cycle1.result: 238 (59%) had melatonin reviewed at follow-up; 81 (20%) attended clinic without documented review; 42 (10%) on long-term melatonin not seen for over a year; 39 (10%) newly started not followed up.

result.other_findings: Of those without review, 52 (64%) had failed to attend clinic. 26 (6.4%) were on other sedatives concurrently; re-audit planned for end of 2016.

result.topic: Medication safety and errors on psychiatric wards
result.setting: West Ward, adult mental health inpatient ward
result.standard: Ward medication practice audit domains (including MHRA alerts, controlled drugs, record keeping, prescribing and administration)

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed significant errors across multiple medication safety domains (figures not given).

result.intervention: Three PDSA cycles over six months: targeted training for doctors and nurses, standardised documentation templates, revised induction, controlled drug procedure review and a system for recording MHRA alerts.

cycle2.result: 51% reduction in the total number of medication errors over six months.

result.other_findings: Largest improvements were in prescribing technicalities, administration errors and controlled drug management; follow-up audits showed the reduction was sustained.

result.setting: Paediatric wards
result.standard: 90% adherence to empirical anti-infective guidelines; 90% indication recorded; 90% duration or review date recorded; 95% initial doses per children's dose table

cycle1.result: Guideline adherence 40/41 (98%); indication recorded 40/42 (95%); duration or review date recorded 26/42 (62%); initial doses per dose table 67/69 (97%).

result.other_findings: Compared with a 2013 audit, guideline adherence rose from 72% and indication recording from 16%; duration recording remained below target. Proposed actions include electronic prescribing prompts, an updated antibiotic app and compulsory junior doctor teaching.

result.topic: Diabetes care and education in severe mental illness
result.setting: Broadmoor Hospital, secure forensic psychiatric hospital
result.standard: NICE guideline and Public Health guideline PH38 (Type 2 diabetes: prevention in people at high risk)

cycle1.result: 71% of inpatients with type 2 diabetes reported never being offered a structured education course; 54% of nurses had received diabetes training, only 21% within the past year (20.7% staff response rate from 106).

result.other_findings: Nearly half of nurses were unsure of guidelines and 43% cited lack of training as a barrier. Recommendations include mandatory nurse training and a structured patient education programme such as DESMOND.

result.setting: Multiple mental health hospital sites (acute, PICU, rehabilitation, learning disability, personality disorder units), London and South region
result.standard: NHS England Clinical Governance Framework (2022) and local STEELL agenda standards

cycle1.result: Qualitative findings only: progress in safety, patient experience and activities; improvement needed in digital tracking of engagement and MDT participation in governance meetings (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Recommendations include standardising incident reporting, better AWOL and contraband security, and sharing best practice; a follow-up audit is planned.

result.topic: Delirium recognition and screening before psychiatry referral
result.setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital; referrals from Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Orthopaedics and ICU
result.standard: CAM-ICU delirium screening before psychiatry referral

cycle1.result: 82/130 (63%) referrals for suspected psychosis were delirium; CAM-ICU use 0%; mean time to delirium management 22 hours.

result.intervention: Four-week CAM-ICU training: didactic sessions (Medicine, Surgery), bedside demonstrations (ICU, Orthopaedics), and quick-reference materials with brief ward teaching (Obstetrics and Gynaecology).

cycle2.result: Misdiagnosis fell to 39/126 (31%); CAM-ICU uptake 56%; mean time to delirium management 11 hours.

result.other_findings: Bedside training gave the highest uptake (ICU 72%, Orthopaedics 65%); orthopaedic misdiagnosis fell from 62% to 25%.

result.setting: MHSOP community mental health team, Bassetlaw Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists, GMC and NHS England guidance; Mobile and Remote Access Work and Consent to Examination and Treatment standards

cycle1.result: Remote consultation documented in 81%; consent documented in 57%; addressed concerns documented in 90%; about 40% met standards for management plan documentation.

result.other_findings: Communication, mental state examination and risk assessment were well documented in about 50–70%. A remote consultation letter template is being developed.

result.setting: The Harbour, 154-bed mental health hospital (general adult, older adult, dementia and PICU wards)
result.standard: Mental Capacity Act (2005), MCA Code of Practice, Trust MCA policy and NICE NG97; target ≥80% of assessments meeting all components

cycle1.result: Decision and time specificity 100%; diagnostic test 77.5%; functional components 70% each; clinical reasoning 60%; correct template use 67.5%; decision-specific framing 60%; outcome stated 92.5%.

result.intervention: 30-minute targeted teaching for resident doctors on MCA principles and the capacity template, reinforced through MDT discussions, handovers and optional quick-reference guidance.

cycle2.result: Diagnostic test 95%; understand 92.5%, retain 90%, use/weigh 90%, communicate 100%; clinical reasoning, template use and decision-specific framing 92.5%; outcome 97.5%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Rheumatology unit, Airedale NHS Trust, Keighley
result.standard: GIRFT (Getting It Right First Time) guidance on rheumatology referrals

cycle1.result: 134 of 674 referrals rejected; 101/134 (75.3%) rejected as more appropriate for MSK/pain services or atypical for RMD; 52/134 (37.9%) advised further assessment or investigations in primary care.

result.other_findings: 17 (12.6%) were re-referred with more information; 15 were seen and 5 were diagnosed with inflammatory disease. Recommendations include GP training, standardised referral protocols and referral templates or checklists.

result.setting: Rheumatology, University College London Hospitals, fast-track pathway including PET-CT
result.standard: British Society for Rheumatology audit tool standards for suspected GCA

cycle1.result: All reviewed within 3 days (95% by next day); all started on corticosteroids with FBC and ESR; all with visual symptoms given high-dose steroids and ophthalmology review (60% same day); 95% had baseline glucose, 75% vitamin D checked, 70% DEXA; of confirmed GCA, 54% had documented written information and 77% safety-netting advice.

result.other_findings: 76% had PET-CT (56% positive) and 95% temporal artery ultrasound (11% positive); 7 patients (33%) had negative ultrasound but positive PET-CT. Only 1 patient (4.8%) had temporal artery biopsy.

result.topic: Antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring in young people with eating disorders
result.setting: Children and Young People (CAMHS) Eating Disorder Service covering York, Scarborough, Harrogate and Northallerton
result.standard: RCPsych Medical Emergencies in Eating Disorders (May 2022) and local TEWV guidelines

cycle1.result: Physical health monitoring 100%; blood-test monitoring 17%; medication information given 50%; unlicensed indication protocol followed 13%.

result.intervention: Spreadsheet to monitor antipsychotic prescriptions and advice on documenting unlicensed indications and providing medication information.

cycle2.result: Physical health monitoring 100%; blood-test monitoring 100%; medication information 67%; unlicensed indication protocol 0%.

result.other_findings: All patients were on olanzapine for distress/rumination; psychiatric follow-up and medication review were regular in both audits. Patients from the first audit were excluded from the re-audit.

result.topic: Biologic home delivery stock checks and cost saving
result.setting: Rheumatology department, Croydon University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 133/168 patients answered; home stock 0 to 12 weeks; repeat prescriptions delayed in 62 patients by 1 to 8 weeks, a theoretical saving of £13,546.585 (6.5% of the monthly anti-TNF cost of £208,099.94).

result.intervention: Biologic patient education programme launched and patients encouraged to contact the biologic coordinator if non-compliant.
result.other_findings: Reasons for excess stock included infection (20), holiday (6), forgetting (7) and delivery delays or double delivery (3).

result.setting: Rheumatology, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: BSR guidance (at least 6-monthly review) and a local guideline for annual bDMARD prescribing

cycle1.result: 233/644 (36.2%) eligible patients switched to annual prescribing; 6/233 (2.6%) flared and 1/233 (0.43%) had a significant blood abnormality; 177 (43.1%) met criteria but were not switched.

result.intervention: Local guideline moving suitable patients from 6-monthly to annual bDMARD prescriptions.
result.other_findings: Annual prescribing patients had fewer contacts (>1 appointment 7.7% v 28.7%; >1 blood test 20% v 36.9%). Past audits 2017–2022 showed bDMARD prescriptions rose 76%.

result.topic: Smoking status and cessation support in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Mount Carmel Hospital, psychiatric inpatient admissions
result.standard: Documentation of smoking status, cessation advice or referral, and medication adjustment for smoking status change

cycle1.result: Smoking status documented in 87.7%; 113 (51.6%) current smokers; only one discharge letter mentioned cessation advice or referral; no documented medication adjustments for smoking status.

result.other_findings: Smoking was associated with male sex, younger age, secondary education and alcohol use disorders (89% smokers, OR 15).

result.topic: Medical referral and follow-up for psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
result.standard: Good clinical practice for managing medical comorbidities in psychiatric inpatients

cycle1.result: IM referral made in 65.7%; indication documented 78.3%; investigations attached 60.9%; same-day referral 39.1%; IM review documented 42.9%; recommendations implemented 31.4%; complete loop 28.6%.

result.intervention: Standardised IM referral proforma, reminders to junior doctors, combined verbal and written handover of IM advice, and a ward-round checklist.

cycle2.result: IM referral 88.6%; indication 93.5%; investigations 87.1%; same-day referral 71.0%; IM review documented 80.0%; plans 74.3%; recommendations implemented 71.4%; complete loop 68.6%.

result.other_findings: Audit ran over a 4-month period with interventions over 3–4 months.

result.topic: Temporal artery ultrasound for suspected giant cell arteritis
result.setting: Vascular ultrasound unit and rheumatology, Dudley Group NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 9 (35%) ultrasound diagnostic of GCA; 10 (38%) had biopsy with 100% concordance between ultrasound and biopsy.

result.intervention: Training of vascular sonographers in temporal and axillary artery scanning (meeting, co-scanning, visit to Oxford unit, image and report review) before starting service scanning.

cycle2.result: Diagnostic, equivocal and negative findings in 4, 2 and 17; no ultrasound-positive patient had biopsy; 3 ultrasound-negative biopsies were all negative.

result.other_findings: Median steroid duration before ultrasound was 1 day versus 6.5 days before biopsy.

result.setting: Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust inpatient personality disorder pathway
result.standard: NHFT Complex Emotional Needs guideline: pre-admission goals, care plan and engagement contract within 24 hours, consultant review within 72 hours, admission under 14 days

cycle1.result: Admission goals documented within 24 hours in 57%; engagement contracts in 9.5%; discharge dates within 24 hours in 48%; consultant review within 72 hours in 48%; only 21% stayed ≤2 weeks and 26% stayed 5 weeks or longer.

result.other_findings: About half of referrals lacked clearly documented admission goals. Recommendations include Structured Clinical Management training, group supervision with community PD services and a re-audit.

result.setting: Paediatric surgical inpatients and discharge prescriptions
result.standard: Local 2012 perioperative pain guideline (dosing by ideal body weight) and BNFC; 100% compliance with weight and height documentation, ideal-weight dosing, separate IV prescribing and 48-hour IV-to-oral review

cycle1.result: Weight recorded on 84% of inpatient and 94% of discharge prescriptions; height never documented; IV/PO prescribed together in 32 inpatients; 20 of 52 on IV paracetamol not reviewed at 48 hours (only 3 appropriate).

result.intervention: Feedback led to amended local guidelines in 2015 (dosing by lean body mass and ideal weight; maximum 75 mg/kg/day).
result.other_findings: Sample was 100 inpatient and 35 discharge prescriptions. Overweight or obese children received doses up to 33 mg/kg/dose on discharge.

result.setting: AI-enabled NHS teledermatology skin cancer pathways; 10 NHS consultant teledermatologists
result.standard: NHS England teledermatology audit and quality control standards (no target stated)

cycle1.result: 90% of dermatologists missed two to four high-risk malignancies; management sensitivity 78.3% (95% CI 70.2–84.8) and specificity 47.5% (95% CI 39.3–55.8); Fleiss' kappa 0.43.

result.intervention: Anonymised results discussed in a forum with personalised feedback to each dermatologist.
result.other_findings: Describes the Teledermatology Audit Risk Scoring System (TARSS). Authors are employed by the AI provider.

result.topic: Enoxaparin prescribing and anti-Xa monitoring in children
result.setting: Children's Hospital
result.standard: BNFc dosing and anti-Xa monitoring

cycle1.result: 71% (n=17) of therapeutic prescriptions dosed per BNFc; 35% had anti-Xa within 36 hours; 71% of levels taken 4–6 hours post dose; 82% (n=11) out-of-range levels led to dose change, 56% (n=9) rechecked within 24 hours; 76% (n=25) prophylactic prescriptions per BNFc.

result.other_findings: 93% (n=42) of prescriptions were whole-number doses. Local guidelines are to be developed with re-audit 12 months after publication; indication was often poorly documented.

result.setting: Same Day Emergency Care, North Middlesex University Hospital (district general hospital), London
result.standard: BSR and GIRFT guidelines for GCA assessment and management

cycle1.result: Steroids 34%; rheumatology referral 55%; temporal artery ultrasound 15%; CRP 92%; median time to eye clinic 2 days.

result.intervention: Trust SDEC GCA pathway guideline, streamlined temporal artery ultrasound order on IT system, local teaching, pathway poster in clinic rooms and Southend GCA probability score.

cycle2.result: Steroids 54%; rheumatology referral 77%; temporal artery ultrasound 77% (p < 0.001); CRP 100%; median time to eye clinic 1 day.

result.other_findings: Time to rheumatology assessment did not change significantly (1 to 1.5 days). A GCA probability score >12 had an AUC of 0.978.

result.setting: AI-enabled NHS teledermatology skin cancer pathways; 10 NHS consultant teledermatologists
result.standard: NHS England teledermatology audit and quality control standards (no target stated)

cycle1.result: 90% of dermatologists missed two to four high-risk malignancies; management sensitivity 78.3% (95% CI 70.2–84.8) and specificity 47.5% (95% CI 39.3–55.8); Fleiss' kappa 0.43.

result.intervention: Anonymised results discussed in a forum with personalised feedback to each dermatologist.
result.other_findings: Describes the Teledermatology Audit Risk Scoring System (TARSS); same abstract as BT07. Authors are employed by the AI provider.

result.setting: Nurse-led telephone gout clinic, Craigavon Area Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Clinic protocol based on BSR guidance; serum urate <360 µmol/L (<300 µmol/L with erosions or tophi)

cycle1.result: Mean serum urate 509 µmol/L at referral and 322 µmol/L at discharge; all offered and took prophylaxis (85.8% for 3–6 months); 95% had ≤2 flares; no ED attendances for gout.

result.other_findings: Mean 3.38 appointments before discharge; lower urate-lowering doses than expected were needed. The telephone model struggled with patients needing an interpreter.

result.setting: Meridian Ward, older adult functional inpatient ward
result.standard: Trust guidance: 3-monthly sodium levels for patients on antidepressants at risk of hyponatraemia

cycle1.result: 11/13 (85%) at-risk patients on antidepressants had 3-monthly sodium levels; only 2 (15%) had a plan for GP sodium monitoring in the discharge summary.

result.other_findings: 3 patients had antidepressant-related hyponatraemia (one with seizure); 1 had no documented plan. Re-audit recommended in 6–12 months.

result.topic: Pulmonary hypertension screening in systemic sclerosis
result.setting: Rheumatology, Freeman Hospital, Newcastle
result.standard: Every SSc patient screened annually with echocardiography or NT pro-BNP (European Society of Cardiology)

cycle1.result: 65% screened, all by echocardiography.

result.intervention: NT pro-BNP introduced as an adjunct to echocardiography in 2014.

cycle2.result: 88% screened; 25% had echocardiogram and 83% NT pro-BNP; 63% screened by NT pro-BNP only.

result.other_findings: Only 6 new PH cases in 1476 patient-years, and all 3 PAH cases came from symptom-driven echocardiograms. Annual screening cost per patient fell from £82 (2014) to £59 (2018).

result.topic: Antipsychotic physical health monitoring in children and young people
result.setting: CAMHS Head-to-Head community service, Nottinghamshire
result.standard: NICE-recommended physical health monitoring at baseline, 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6-monthly for antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Complete baseline monitoring 0% (44.4% had at least one parameter); 6-week weight 22.2%; complete 12-week monitoring 22.2%; across 25 six-monthly windows height 20.0%, weight 20.0%, BP/HR 16.0%, bloods 20.0%, waist circumference 0%.

result.other_findings: No six-monthly window contained all recommended measures, but all patients had some ongoing monitoring and no related adverse outcomes were found.

result.setting: Five inpatient rehabilitation wards, Royal Edinburgh Hospital
result.standard: NICE guidance and local shared-care protocols for lithium monitoring

cycle1.result: Urine ACR absent in all patients; serum calcium and thyroid function missed in about 60%; over 10% of results supratherapeutic; renal function not consistently rechecked after high levels.

result.other_findings: Several patients had overdue lithium, renal or thyroid tests. Planned next steps are standardised lithium order sets and MDT education.

result.setting: Rural general practice
result.standard: NICE NG222: documented suicidal ideation enquiry (95%) and antidepressants not first-line for less-severe depression without patient preference (90%)

cycle1.result: Suicidal ideation enquiry documented in 17/20 (85%); non-drug first-line treatment for less-severe depression in 9/11 (81.8%).

result.other_findings: Proposed EMIS prompts and templates plus staff training, with re-audit in 12 months.

result.setting: Neuropsychiatry service, Mater Dei Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean Y-BOCS improved from 32.5 (SD 6.1) to 20.5 (SD 10.4); 3 (50%) full responders, 1 partial responder, 2 non-responders; no post-operative complications.

result.other_findings: One non-responder's inpatient days fell from 32% to 1% of time.

result.topic: Equality and inclusion in adult autism assessment
result.setting: Skylight Psychiatry adult neurodiversity assessment service (NHS-commissioned and self-funded)
result.standard: NHS inclusion health principles, NICE guidelines and inclusive communication principles

cycle1.result: Strong representation of women, gender-diverse and LGBTQIA+ patients; lower than expected representation of some ethnic minority and religious groups; some inconsistent inclusive language in documentation (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Suggested actions include accessibility review of sites, easy-read and translated materials, and inclusion training.

result.setting: Airedale General Hospital rheumatology; patients on six-monthly denosumab
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 34/166 (21%) did not receive denosumab on time; 21/166 (12.6%) delayed and 13/166 (7.8%) missed; 8/166 (4.8%) sustained a fracture, 6 of whom had a delayed or missed dose during Covid-19.

result.other_findings: Reasons for delay were patient choice (44.1%), clinician safety decisions (35.3%) and clinical reasons (20.6%).

result.setting: Neonatal units
result.standard: Local neonatal vancomycin guideline; 100% adherence

cycle1.result: Correct initial dose 28/28 (100%); level taken at correct time 13/15 (87%); 19/31 levels (62%) within 10–20 mg/L; all 6 levels >20 mg/L had next dose held, but follow-up adjustment often suboptimal; 3 of 4 low levels not acted on.

result.intervention: Guideline amended (single safe range 10–20 mg/L, doses adjusted on levels not age) and teaching sessions with worked examples planned for prescribers and nurses.
result.other_findings: 19 patients had 28 courses and 31 levels. Levels appeared to be interpreted in isolation, causing avoidable repeat high levels.

result.topic: Ethanol line lock prescribing and documentation
result.setting: Paediatric inpatients prescribed ethanol line locks
result.standard: Trust paediatric ethanol line lock guideline (volume, concentration, indication, review, duration and consent documentation)

cycle1.result: 98% prescribed accurately per guideline; only 28% had documented indication, review and duration; 0 had consent documented.

result.intervention: Change to the electronic prescribing order suggested to aid documentation.
result.other_findings: 36/46 (78%) line infections were eradicated and 40 (87%) did not need catheter removal; one adverse effect followed a prescribing error.

result.setting: Stroke rehabilitation ward, Caerphilly, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
result.standard: NICE CG162 and Stroke Quality Standard QS2: 100% mood screening within 6 weeks, follow-up at discharge or 6–12 months, and all with depression offered treatment or referral

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: Data collection was ongoing at the time of the abstract.

result.setting: Paediatric wards (patients ≥1 month) on intermittent IV vancomycin
result.standard: Trust intermittent IV vancomycin guideline (2016) with loading dose and increased dose and frequency versus BNFC

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation audit: 7% of levels in therapeutic range at 48 hours; lack of support for appropriate dosing and monitoring.

result.intervention: New trust guideline for intermittent IV vancomycin (loading dose, higher dose and frequency) with pharmacist intervention.

cycle2.result: Loading dose used appropriately in 83%; levels at correct times in 90%; 40% in range at 48 hours; 100% reviewed at 48 hours; out-of-range levels reviewed per guideline in 40%, rising to 80% with pharmacist intervention.

result.other_findings: 30% still needed dose adjustment at 48 hours. Authors plan for pharmacist prescribers to adjust treatment directly.

result.topic: Risk assessment on psychiatric admission and discharge
result.setting: Psychiatry inpatient unit, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
result.standard: Risk assessment within 24 hours of admission covering all risk domains, risk management plan, and review and update before discharge

cycle1.result: Admission risk assessment within 24 hours 64%; documentation in notes 84%; risk from others 68%; risk management plan 72%; review before discharge 40%; update before discharge 40%.

result.intervention: Staff education, risk-assessment checklists displayed on the ward, and ward-round reminders.

cycle2.result: Admission risk assessment within 24 hours 92%; documentation 96%; risk from others 88%; risk management plan 88%; review before discharge 84%; update before discharge 80%.

result.other_findings: Audit ran over two months. Standardised admission and discharge proformas are recommended.

result.topic: Factors associated with prolonged psychiatric length of stay
result.setting: Female acute psychiatric inpatient ward, East London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHS England ambition of about 32 days average acute adult mental health stay

cycle1.result: Mean LoS 29.76 days (SD 29.71), median 17 days (IQR 9–31); 40 (24.8%) stayed ≥32 days.

result.other_findings: Prolonged stay was associated with Mental Health Act detention (aOR 6.07), schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (aOR 5.55) and mood disorders (aOR 4.77).

result.setting: South West London & St George's Mental Health NHS Trust; initial seclusion reviews by resident doctors
result.standard: Mental Health Units (Use of Force) Act 2018; target 80% compliance with all domains

cycle1.result: 75% of reviews met all required criteria.

result.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: seclusion proforma made accessible at handover, proforma circulated by email, teaching in the academic programme, and small-group core trainee teaching.

cycle2.result: 83% of reviews met all required criteria; minimal change in overall compliance on SPC chart.

result.other_findings: Small numbers and variation between on-call doctors caused wide fluctuations. Risk assessment and physical health documentation improved; authors suggest mandatory completion of all domains.

result.setting: Two CAMHS learning disability services (Hereford and Worcester)
result.standard: NHS England STOMP principles

cycle1.result: Hereford (n=20) v Worcester (n=12): rationale documented 90% v 100%; reduce/stop plan 10% v 17%; MDT at initiation 30% v 67%; ongoing MDT review 0% v 0%; review ≤6 months 100% v 100%; monitoring complete 11/14 (79%) v 5/6 (83%); capacity/best interests 60% v 100%.

result.other_findings: Planned actions include a mandatory medication review field in the MDT proforma, scheduled MDT follow-ups and standardised monitoring systems.

result.topic: Medication prescribing in children with autism
result.setting: CAMHS across Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust localities
result.standard: NICE guidelines on psychotropic and sleep medication in children with autism

cycle1.result: Alternative interventions before medication 44%; consent documented 62%; follow-up within 3–4 weeks 70%; side effects recorded 61%; indication documented 83%.

cycle2.result: Alternative interventions 60%; consent 93%; follow-up within 3–4 weeks 75%; side effects 70%; indication 93%.

result.other_findings: Medications continued to be started at minimum effective dose. Recommendations include trust-wide clinic letter templates and consistent follow-up intervals.

result.topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
result.setting: Emergency departments of eight UK hospitals; re-audit in one hospital
result.standard: BOAST 11 standard 1: documented radial pulse, digital capillary refill time and individual radial, median (including AIN) and ulnar nerve function on presentation

cycle1.result: Nerve motor and sensory function documented in 201 (46%) to 232 (54%); radial pulse 318 (73%); capillary refill time 247 (57%).

result.intervention: Quality improvement proforma for emergency department assessment, piloted in one hospital.

cycle2.result: Nerve function documented in 72 (71%) to 80 (78%); radial pulse 84 (82%); capillary refill time 82 (80%).

result.other_findings: Only 44 (43%) of re-audit cases used the proforma; when used, adherence was 40 (91%) to 43 (98%) across all items.

result.setting: All-male acute psychiatric ward, Livewell Southwest
result.standard: Lester UK Adaptation: Positive Cardiometabolic Health Resource (screening and action on red-zone risk factors)

cycle1.result: 50/63 had a Rethink template; of 41 smokers, 15 not offered cessation support; 28 of 31 with BMI >25 had no documented support; 8 of 12 hypertensive patients had no documented action; 27 of 32 with dyslipidaemia had no further intervention; 15 had no glucose test and 25 had no bloods.

result.intervention: Changes to admission physical health assessments, well-man clinics and improved inpatient–community communication at discharge.
result.other_findings: 9 patients had no smoking status documented. Re-audit was pending.

result.topic: Anticholinergic burden reduction in older inpatients
result.setting: Acute Integrated Frailty Unit, Royal Liverpool University Hospital
result.standard: Anticholinergic Burden (ACB) score below 3

cycle1.result: 28% (28/100) had ACB ≥3 on admission; 27% (27/100) still ≥3 at discharge; 33% of these readmitted at 3 months.

result.intervention: Automated Excel ACB calculator; frailty specialist nurses calculated pre-admission ACB scores on in-reach ward rounds and recorded them in electronic notes.

cycle2.result: 33.7% (27/80) had ACB ≥3 on admission; 30% (24/80) still ≥3 at discharge.

result.other_findings: A third cycle after a poster and teaching presentation is planned, with 3-month readmission rates.

result.setting: Adult and older adult acute psychiatric inpatient wards, Cheshire and Wirral Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust SOP 13 (Management of ligatures): every inpatient who ligatures should have a medical review

cycle1.result: Approximately 50% had a medical review after the ligature incident; 5/112 (about 4%), or 5/55 (9%) of those reviewed, had new management as a result.

result.other_findings: No serious harm outcomes; medical input was minor (e.g. steristrips, CT after seizure). The authors question whether mandatory medical review is needed.

result.topic: Functional status follow-up after rheumatoid arthritis rehabilitation
result.setting: Inpatient RA rehabilitation programme, Tallaght University Hospital and Peamount Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: EULAR treat-to-target: disease activity and functional status monitored every six months

cycle1.result: 33/36 (92%) completed six-month functional follow-up; median EQ-5D 46 at admission, 65 at discharge, 62.5 at six months; median self-efficacy 3.4, 7.0 and 5.5.

result.other_findings: 45% had lower EQ-5D and 58% lower self-efficacy at six months than at discharge; home-exercise adherence was 79% and community support engagement 57%.

result.topic: Valproate prescribing in women of childbearing potential
result.setting: Hamad Medical Corporation psychiatric inpatient units
result.standard: MHRA and NICE guidance on valproate in women of childbearing age

cycle1.result: Teratogenicity discussion documented in 1 (3%); benefits 7 (21%); side effects 3 (9%); pregnancy test 21 (65.6%); contraception education 0.

result.intervention: Results disseminated in the department and educational sessions for doctors and pharmacists.

cycle2.result: Teratogenicity discussion 10 (47.6%); benefits 5 (23.8%); side effects 14 (66.7%); pregnancy test 19 (90%); contraception education 8 (38.1%).

result.other_findings: Female bed capacity expanded during the re-audit. The audit prompted national guideline development and a QI project.

result.topic: Obesity assessment in patients on antipsychotics
result.setting: Forensic community mental health team, supported accommodation, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE obesity guideline (2014): BMI categorisation, waist circumference, lifestyle programme and interventions for risk factors

cycle1.result: 10/12 (83%) overweight or obese; only 4 had waist circumference measured; all overweight or obese patients received lifestyle advice; QRISK calculated for most eligible patients except two.

result.other_findings: One patient was pre-diabetic and one diabetic.

result.setting: East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust (pathology requests from outpatients, inpatients and GPs)
result.standard: BSR Choosing Wisely recommendations on ANA testing

cycle1.result: Only 17% of requests met the standards; 41% inappropriate; 42% had insufficient details.

result.intervention: Local ANA testing guidelines devised from Choosing Wisely standards.
result.other_findings: 180 (11.86%) tests were positive. Following the guidance could save about £12,000 a year; re-audit planned in 6 months.

result.setting: Psychiatric rehabilitation and acute wards, Cygnet Churchill Hospital, London
result.standard: Carers Trust Triangle of Care partnership accreditation criteria

cycle1.result: Compliance 87% on rehabilitation wards and 68% on acute wards.

result.intervention: Formalised stakeholder communication, more carer lead staff and carer awareness training, carer communication forms and logs, monthly carer events, and an infographic Carer Involvement Protocol.
result.other_findings: Cycle 2 (September 2024) also showed 100% adherence; carer event attendance rose by 28% and Triangle of Care accreditation was achieved in May 2024.

result.topic: BMI monitoring in early intervention in psychosis
result.setting: Northamptonshire Early Intervention Psychosis Service (NSTEP North and South)
result.standard: National Clinical Audit of Psychosis EIP standards: routine BMI monitoring with intervention at BMI ≥25 (≥23 for South Asian and Chinese patients)

cycle1.result: 182/187 (97%) had BMI recorded; 64% overweight or obese (34% 25–29.9, 29% ≥30); 68% (13/19) of South Asian/Asian patients had BMI ≥23.

result.other_findings: 68% (23/34) of Black Caribbean/African patients were overweight or obese; about half were on no antipsychotic or aripiprazole. Planned resource packs and links to exercise and diabetes prevention programmes.

result.topic: Paget's disease of bone investigation and treatment
result.setting: All departments, University Hospital Southampton (including rheumatology and medicine for the elderly)
result.standard: Paget's Association, ECTS and IOF clinical guideline (February 2019)

cycle1.result: Targeted X-ray or CT in 127/143 (88.8%); bone scan in 38.4% (68.3% rheumatology v 22.6% other departments); ALP available in all rheumatology and 88.7% of other patients; bisphosphonates in 36.1% (73.3% rheumatology v 9.4% other).

result.other_findings: Bisphosphonates were mostly given for symptoms (65.4%) rather than ALP reduction. Targeted education for non-rheumatology specialties and re-audit are recommended.

result.topic: Self-harm assessment in children and young people in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency departments of nine teaching hospitals in Scotland, England and Wales
result.standard: NICE NG225 self-harm guideline (2022)

cycle1.result: Consent for family involvement documented in 73.5%; social media interactions documented in 21.5%; delayed psychosocial assessment in 17.8%; only 26.1% of 16–17-year-olds needing admission went to age-appropriate wards.

result.other_findings: Student-led multicentre audit; further training for clinical teams recommended.

result.setting: Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment (CRHT) service, Telford and Wrekin (MPFT)
result.standard: Triangle of Care national framework (Carers Trust), six standards; Trust policy and Health and Care Act 2022 duty to involve carers

cycle1.result: Overall compliance across ToC standards 77%. S1 identification 55%, S2 staff training 100%, S3 confidentiality/information sharing 50%, S4 defined carer roles 67%, S5 carer introduction and information 90%, S6 range of carer support 100%.

result.other_findings: Key gaps: recording special circumstances 27%, documented consent/limits 54%, revisiting non-disclosure 33%, offering support when disclosure declined 0%, carer involvement in discharge planning 50%. Action plan in development with re-audit scheduled for 2026.

result.topic: ADHD shared care prescribing after private diagnosis
result.setting: North Peterborough Adult Locality Team (community mental health), Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE ADHD guideline (2018): prescribing and monitoring after titration under shared care arrangements with primary care

cycle1.result: 2/325 (0.6%) had private ADHD diagnoses. The Right to Choose patient was managed under shared care with GP for two years; the self-funded patient reverted to the NHS waitlist, then returned to private care.

result.other_findings: No mechanism exists for privately diagnosed patients to access NHS treatment without joining standard waiting lists. Further audit in a larger cohort recommended.

result.topic: Clozapine and lithium plasma level monitoring
result.setting: Eight inpatient psychiatric wards, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidelines: clozapine levels pre-morning dose or 10–12 h post-dose after at least 3 days on stable dose; lithium levels 5–7 days after initiation, 12–14 h post-dose, weekly until stable. Target 100%

cycle1.result: Clozapine (n=6): all had levels after at least 3 days on stable dose; 4 (66.67%) sampled within recommended post-dose window; 2 (33.33%) unconfirmed due to missing lab reports. Lithium (n=9): 7 (77.8%) checked within 5–7 days of initiation; 2 sampled outside 12–14 h window. Overall 66.67% fully monitored in line with guidelines.

result.intervention: Planned: guidelines displayed on wards, targeted teaching, patient education, accountability for uploading clozapine monitoring forms, work with IT on report uploads
result.other_findings: Missing clozapine monitoring forms limited assessment of compliance. Re-audit planned.

result.topic: Oral health assessment in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Inpatient mental health units (acute, older adult, low-secure forensic, rehabilitation), Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust inpatient policy: comprehensive physical health assessment including oral health examination on admission, and dental hygiene in ongoing nursing care reviews

cycle1.result: 'Eating, Drinking and Oral Health' questionnaire partially completed for 61.4% (70/114), fully completed for none. Formal oral health examination recorded for 10.5% (12/114), 0% in forensic unit. No patients had a completed oral health risk assessment.

result.other_findings: Of 30 patients with acute dental issues during admission, 18 accessed professional dental care, with variation between ward types.

result.setting: Clock View Hospital, general adult inpatient unit, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Mersey Care EUPD prescribing guidelines

cycle1.result: EUPD with comorbidity (n=25): 80% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new medication; 4 of 7 new prescriptions as advised by guidelines. EUPD without comorbidity (n=25): 96% on psychotropics before admission, 28% started new regular medication; 5 of 8 new prescriptions as advised. 78% of 50 prescribed PRN psychotropics; PRN for over one week in 21 patients.

result.other_findings: Antipsychotic prescribing higher in those without comorbidity (72% vs 60%). Benzodiazepines were the most consistently prescribed PRN medication.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness on antipsychotics
result.setting: Peterborough Adult Locality Team (community mental health), Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE: annual SMI physical health check including Core 6 parameters, and regular physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotics

cycle1.result: 59% had an SMI physical health check in the preceding 12 months despite 98% engaging with PALT. Core 6 components 78–84%. Antipsychotic blood monitoring 79–84%. Annual ECG 63%. Metabolic monitoring for moderate-high risk antipsychotics 46%; prolactin monitoring 27%.

result.other_findings: Of the 41% who did not attend a physical health check, only 34% had documented invitation. Antipsychotic blood monitoring improved compared with previous audits.

result.setting: Assertive Outreach and Rehabilitation (AORT) service, NHS mental health trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 28% of service users reported negative symptoms; only half of the sample were prescribed medication; those with negative symptoms were less likely to receive occupational or psychological therapies.

result.other_findings: No significant associations with age, gender or ethnicity. Proposed co-learning workshops and simpler assessment proformas.

result.setting: Orthopaedic operating theatre, Regional Headquarter Hospital Skardu
result.standard: WHO surgical hand hygiene guidelines (structured checklist)

cycle1.result: Scrub duration at least two minutes 45%, coverage of all hand surfaces 50%, proper antiseptic use 60%, correct drying technique 55%, overall aseptic protocol 70%.

result.intervention: Live demonstrations of correct hand-scrubbing technique and visual reminder posters in the scrub area

cycle2.result: Scrub duration 90%, hand surface coverage 88%, antiseptic use 93%, drying technique 87%, overall aseptic protocol 95%; all improvements statistically significant.

result.other_findings: Approximately 40 personnel (consultants, residents, nurses, theatre assistants) were observed.

result.topic: Antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring in CAMHS
result.setting: Red Kite View CAMHS inpatient unit and Leeds Community Healthcare community CAMHS
result.standard: NICE NG11, CG155, CG170, Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and local Trust protocols

cycle1.result: Appropriate indication 100% in both. Specialist initiation 100% inpatient, 85% community. Psychological interventions tried first 77% inpatient, 54% community. Standardised behavioural rating scales 0%. Baseline movement disorder assessment 54% inpatient, 0% community. Baseline bloods 92% inpatient vs 38% community.

result.other_findings: Community monitoring: 0% weekly weight monitoring during titration and 0% six-month liver function tests.

result.topic: Risk scores in acute severe ulcerative colitis
result.setting: UK IBD audit 2010 round (national data)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Surgery in high risk groups: Travis 49% (n=93), Ho 51% (n=84); Ho medium 35% (n=53), Ho low 26% (n=17), Travis low 32% (n=65).

result.other_findings: Comparison of prognostic scores using audit data, not an audit against a standard. Travis and Ho scores were equally able to identify high-risk patients.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness on antipsychotics
result.setting: Intellectual Disability community psychiatry service
result.standard: NICE guideline (CG11): secondary care prescribing and monitoring of antipsychotics for at least 12 months with primary care collaboration; audit tool based on physical health CQUIN targets and Lester adaptation tool

cycle1.result: Baseline cardio-metabolic assessment in 50–65%; less than 15% at 3–6 months. Body weight and blood pressure documented at 3–6 months in 15% and 2.5% respectively. Collaboration with GP for annual health check 78–100%.

result.other_findings: Compliance was significantly better when the nursing team was involved. Re-audit planned in one year after action plan dissemination (community nurse involvement, sphygmomanometers in every clinic).

result.setting: All Trusts in the Northern Deanery (regional audit)
result.standard: NCEPOD 'Measuring the Units' report recommendations on early management of decompensated liver disease in the first 24 h

cycle1.dates: Consecutive admissions over a 3 month period
cycle1.result: Of 82 with ascites, 62% had a diagnostic tap within 24 h, 21% after 24 h, 17% not at all. Previous alcohol history documented in 43%, current consumption 81%. Of variceal bleeds, 19% did not receive terlipressin and 30% no vitamin K; endoscopy within 12 h 67%, within 24 h 78%. 17% not seen by a consultant within 12 h.

result.intervention: Planned: regional 'care bundle' for decompensated liver disease
result.other_findings: 28% with renal impairment did not have all nephrotoxins stopped; 42% with hyponatraemia did not have diuretics stopped; 39% not seen by gastroenterology/hepatology consultant within 24 h. Re-audit planned.

result.topic: Substance misuse screening and documentation in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Mixed acute general adult psychiatry ward, St John's Hospital, Livingston
result.standard: NICE and SIGN guidance on co-occurring substance misuse and mental health; local target 80% compliance with substance use assessment

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Staff reminders for biological testing and incentivised staff, patient and carer feedback on substance misuse history, on-ward substance misuse and testing

cycle2.result: Biological testing compliance 57% (35.18% increase); substance misuse history documentation 75% (51.36% increase).

result.other_findings: Alcohol was the most reported substance (33.33%), then cannabis (27.03%) and cocaine (11.71%). Compliance remains below target; part of a larger QI project.

result.setting: Southern Gambling Service (specialist gambling disorder service), Hampshire and Isle of Wight NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE CG115, Department of Health and Social Care guidance and Royal College of Physicians guidance on alcohol assessment and management by risk bracket

cycle1.result: Full AUDIT completion 0%, brief interventions 7%, advice on safe alcohol reduction 0%.

result.intervention: Previously implemented recommendations from the initial audit (details not reported)

cycle2.result: AUDIT-C and EWAC 100%. Full AUDIT completed in 100% meeting criteria (55). Score 8 or above: brief intervention 18 (66.7%), formulation 20 (74%). Score 20 or above: advice on avoiding abrupt reduction 7 (70%), formulation 8 (80%). Signposting 7/10 (70%).

result.other_findings: 124 of 301 referrals (41.2%) were accepted and assessed. Documentation consistency and staff education still needed.

result.setting: Psychiatric Liaison Team, Newcastle acute hospitals
result.standard: NCEPOD 'Treat as One' seven documentation elements

cycle1.result: 58% of documentation contained at least 50% of NCEPOD elements. Formulation 0%, legal status and capacity 47%, risk assessment 2%, risk management 18%, discharge plan 2%. Acute trust documentation completed 74%.

result.intervention: Streamlined e-template in acute hospital eRecord prompting NCEPOD standards, structured clinician training, and nominated 'Treat as One Guardians'

cycle2.result: 98% contained at least 50% of NCEPOD elements. Formulation 8%, legal status and capacity 79%, risk assessment 28%, risk management 53%, discharge plan 29%. Acute trust documentation completed 96%.

result.other_findings: Mean time from assessment to documentation fell from 6.02 to 3.53 hours in acute trust records (p = 0.04) and 6.12 to 3.50 hours in mental health records (p = 0.05).

result.setting: Community Mental Health Team, Northern Health and Social Care Trust, Antrim
result.standard: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summary standards for antipsychotic monitoring (revised January 2026); target 100%

cycle1.result: Monitoring compliance 26%. FYI flag on chart 21%; HDAT therapy plan in place 26%.

result.intervention: Epic EHR 'FYI Flag' for HDAT and active HDAT 'Therapy Plan' generating investigation orders and appointments for every patient

cycle2.result: Monitoring compliance 58%. FYI flag 100%; therapy plans 100%. All patients with incomplete monitoring had an appointment scheduled.

result.other_findings: Most common reason for incomplete monitoring was investigations outside the timeframe; prolactin and ECG most often omitted. Ongoing PDSA cycles planned.

result.topic: Giant cell arteritis fast-track pathway adherence
result.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, ambulatory care, Chelsea and Westminster Trust
result.standard: Ambulatory Care Giant Cell Arteritis Fast Track Pathway Guidelines (Chelsea and Westminster Trust)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Staff education on the GCA pathway, results presented at trust ambulatory emergency care governance meeting, and streamlined documentation

cycle2.result: GCA probability score calculated in 69% (21% improvement); TAUS within 72 h 85% (9% improvement); appropriate steroid dose 100% (29% improvement); appropriate bone protection 46% (41% increase).

result.other_findings: Delays in scheduling temporal artery biopsy persisted with no significant change; TAUS probe frequencies varied between hospitals. Cerner Autotext recommended.

result.setting: Hospital pharmacy dispensary serving high turnover paediatric wards
result.standard: Trust KPIs: 85% of urgent items (TTAs) dispensed within 1 hour; 85% of non-urgent items (inpatient orders) within 3 hours

cycle1.result: TTAs (n=12): average 2 hours from logging in to checking (standard 1 hour); writing to screening averaged 1 hour 34 minutes. Inpatient orders (n=22): average 5 hours 51 minutes to leave dispensary (standard 3 hours). Standards not met.

result.intervention: Proposed: additional labelling staff at peak times, IT review of dispensing system, induction teaching on sending TTAs to pharmacy
result.other_findings: Labelling was the rate-limiting step (TTA log-in to labelling 1 hour 25 minutes; inpatient 1 hour 56 minutes). Re-audit planned in 3 months.

result.setting: GP practice, Oxford
result.standard: NICE gout guideline: titrate allopurinol to serum urate below 360 µmol/L with annual monitoring

cycle1.result: 68/141 had a urate level in the past 12 months; of these 40 (58.8%) had urate below 360 µmol/L or allopurinol increased. 6 had never had a urate level on EMIS.

result.intervention: Clinician education on NICE treat-to-target guidance

cycle2.result: 65/142 had a yearly urate; 57 (87.7%) managed in line with NICE. Six-fold decrease in patients with no urate ever recorded.

result.other_findings: Annual monitoring rates did not improve; 23.4% of 77 without yearly urate had levels above 360 µmol/L. EMIS and NICE reference ranges for urate differed.

result.setting: Psychiatry of Later Life Community Mental Health Team, Mid-West Ireland
result.standard: 'Safe Prescribing and Dispensing of Controlled Drugs' Joint Guidance, Irish Medical Council and Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland; Misuse of Drugs Regulation 2017

cycle1.result: 100% for date, patient name, strength, frequency, signature, profession and registration number; 98% prescriber name and telephone; 97% prescriber address; 94% patient address; 61% form and 47% quantity of medication.

result.intervention: Results circulated to prescribers and presented at weekly MDT meeting, emphasising poorly compliant components
result.other_findings: 158 files reviewed initially; controlled drugs were exclusively benzodiazepines and z-hypnotics.

result.setting: Russell's Hall Hospital, Dudley
result.standard: European Joint Guidelines (2017) on management and follow-up of gallbladder polyps

cycle1.dates: Since 2017 guideline publication (ten year retrospective cohort)
cycle1.result: 36% managed according to guidelines; adherence 62% at 3 years post introduction compared with an average of 35%.

result.other_findings: Adherence better for polyps over 10mm (p < 0.01) and when straight to laparoscopic cholecystectomy; surveillance adherence poor. No difference surgeons versus non-surgeons (p = 0.32).

result.setting: Beech Ward, older adult functional psychiatric ward, Rochford Hospital
result.standard: Royal College of Physicians NEWS2 recommended monitoring frequencies and clinical responses

cycle1.result: 42% of 476 NEWS2 entries (9 patients) had appropriate monitoring frequency (81% adherence for 12-hourly routine monitoring at NEWS 0); 58% monitored less often than the recommended minimum.

result.intervention: Planned: MDT discussions on NEWS2 documentation and intradepartmental teaching on handover and escalation
result.other_findings: Minimum 1-hourly observations were done up to 12-hourly; inappropriate responses related to incomplete escalation documentation and no medical escalation for a single-parameter score of 3.

result.topic: Paediatric sepsis management in the emergency department
result.setting: Emergency Department, university hospital (single centre, 30,000 paediatric attendances per year)
result.standard: RCEM adult severe sepsis audit standards applied to children (e.g. vital signs within 15 mins 100%, fluid bolus within 1 hour 75%, antibiotics within 1 hour 50%)

cycle1.result: Vital signs within 15 mins 47%; capillary glucose 84%; IV fluid bolus within 1 hour 42%; lactate 89%; antibiotics within 1 hour 42%; blood cultures before antibiotics 37%. No RCEM standard was met.

result.other_findings: Urine dip obtained in 21%; doctor assessment within 30 mins 84%. All patients survived to discharge.

result.topic: Medicines reconciliation between mental health and GP records
result.setting: Community forensic supported accommodation, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust medicines reconciliation guidance; 100% concordance between mental health and GP records for medication and allergy status

cycle1.result: Allergy status discordant in 2 patients (25%); medication discrepancies in 2 patients (25%).

result.other_findings: Medication discrepancies were vitamin D supplements omitted during transcription. Primary care asked to update allergy records; re-audits every four months planned.

result.setting: Older Adult Community Mental Health Services covering care homes in West Essex (Epping, Uttlesford, Harlow)
result.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics for BPSD: documentation of BPSD, exclusion of causes, non-pharmacological interventions first, structured assessment (ABC chart), review every 6 weeks

cycle1.result: BPSD documentation 100%; investigations to exclude organic causes and delirium 91%; ABC chart 38.5%; initial 6-week review 59 (75.6%); subsequent 6-weekly reviews 43 (55.2%).

result.other_findings: Documentation of environmental causes and non-pharmacological measures was too unclear to audit. A standardised antipsychotic review record was proposed.

result.topic: Sleep assessment and management in older adults
result.setting: Older adult inpatient wards and Community Mental Health Teams, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, Bromley
result.standard: NICE NG97 and NG222, NHS and RCPsych guidance on sleep assessment and management

cycle1.result: Records: 23.3% detailed assessment aligned with guidance, 70% brief mention, 6.7% no documentation; pharmacological management 88.2%. Clinician survey (n=20): 45–50% routinely assessed sleep, 80% no structured tools, 10% sleep diaries, 80% unfamiliar with guidance.

result.intervention: Targeted teaching on sleep assessment in older adults and dissemination of guidance on non-pharmacological approaches

cycle2.result: Clinician survey only: 90% reported routine sleep assessment, structured tools 81%, sleep diaries 72%, 72% familiar with guidance, 90% offering sleep hygiene advice.

result.other_findings: Post-intervention data were self-reported by clinicians; records were reviewed only at baseline. Re-audit planned.

result.setting: 20-bed acute mixed adult inpatient ward, South West London and St George's NHS Mental Health Trust
result.standard: NICE: 4–6 week trial of antipsychotic at optimal dosage

cycle1.result: Mean time to first antipsychotic change 11.6 days, first to second 13.8 days, second to third 16.0 days. Counselling attempted for initial changes in 73%.

result.other_findings: Changes were due to inadequate response in 84.6%, side effects 9.6% and adherence 5.8%.

result.topic: Tier 4 CAMHS admissions via crisis team
result.setting: Alliance Crisis and Home Treatment Team, West London NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: National guidance on avoiding unnecessary Tier 4 admissions (not specified)

cycle1.result: 20 of 465 referrals (4.3%) admitted to Tier 4; Alliance Team involved in gatekeeping in 70%; 80% already known to CAMHS; 65% admitted to local beds.

result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit with admission rate improved on previous years, but earlier figures not given. 35% stayed over 100 days; 60% had no recorded ADHD or ASD diagnosis.

result.setting: 12 UK and Irish patch test centres (multicentre)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 201 of 3118 (6.4%) positive to at least one baseline formaldehyde releaser; formaldehyde and MDBGN both 1.3%, 2-bromo-2-nitropropane-1,3-diol 1.2%, Quaternium-15 0.9%.

result.other_findings: Frequency study without a practice standard. Current relevance highest for Quaternium-15 (48.1%); MDBGN low relevance (17.5%), so its inclusion in the baseline series warrants review.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness on antipsychotics
result.setting: Older Adults Female ward, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines on antipsychotic prescribing documentation, baseline assessment and monitoring

cycle1.result: Indication 80%; consent to treatment 66.66%; MCA 53.33%; baseline ECG 86.66%; repeat ECG 53.33%; glucose/HbA1c, lipids, LFTs each 73.33%; side-effect monitoring 46.66%; GP follow-up recommendations 50%.

result.intervention: Refined ward round process and physical health monitoring poster for junior doctors

cycle2.result: Indication 100%; consent and MCA 100%; baseline ECG 100%; repeat ECG 79.17%; glucose/HbA1c 88%; lipids 92%; LFTs 100%; side-effect monitoring 100%; GP follow-up recommendations 100%.

result.other_findings: Age, diagnosis and MHA status documentation stayed at 100%. Repeat ECGs remained below target.

result.setting: Department of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences EEG service, Allied II Hospital, Faisalabad
result.standard: International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology (IFCN), American Clinical Neurophysiology Society (ACNS) and NICE guidance

cycle1.result: 13.9% (n=405) abnormal, 85.8% (n=2,494) normal, 0.2% unclear. Wake 69.8%, sleep 28.4%, state unclear 1.6% (n=47). Mean duration 25.2 minutes (median 19.0, IQR 16–23), some below minimum recommended duration. Missing data: weight 12.8%, height 4.0%, gender 0.4%.

result.other_findings: Annual volumes stable through Covid-19, reaching 503 EEGs in 2024. Action plan implemented with re-audit planned within 12–18 months.

result.setting: North Essex Specialist Community Mental Health Team, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: EPUT DNA/disengagement guideline (April 2018, amended August 2022): document risk-based actions, liaise with carers/GP, offer another appointment, review care plan, discuss in MDT

cycle1.result: Documenting risk 48.2%; risk management plans 49.4%; notifying professionals/MDT 50.5%; offered another appointment 77.6%; confirming appointments 94.1%; contacting patients after DNA 81.1%.

result.intervention: Increased staff awareness of the trust guideline and the importance of documenting the action plan

cycle2.result: Documenting risk 95%; risk management plans 58%; notifying professionals/MDT 60%; offered another appointment 92%; confirming appointments 92%; contacting patients after DNA 74%.

result.other_findings: Confirming appointments and contacting patients after DNA fell. A disengagement care plan and decision support tool are recommended.

result.topic: Interstitial lung disease screening in myositis
result.setting: Royal United Hospital Bath / Royal National Hospital of Rheumatic Diseases, general connective tissue disease clinic
result.standard: British Society for Rheumatology guidelines for managing idiopathic inflammatory myositis (no target stated)

cycle1.result: 65% (46/70) of adult IIM patients screened for pulmonary involvement. 31% (22/70) had IIM-ILD; 21/22 had PFTs; 76.2% (16/22) had ILD changes on imaging.

result.other_findings: NSIP (44%) and OP (22%) were the commonest CT patterns; 20/22 received high-dose steroids, csDMARDs or aggressive immunosuppression, and 52% progressed on serial PFTs.

result.topic: External prescription requests between clinic visits
result.setting: National Centre of Paediatric Rheumatology, Children's Health Ireland at Crumlin, Dublin (outpatients)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Parents gave a dose in 10/36 requests; charts available for 27; 21 had blood tests on hospital database in the last 3 months; 27 had clinic appointments in the preceding 6 months.

result.intervention: Planned: prescription request form for parents detailing dose, route and latest blood results
result.other_findings: 28 routine, 6 emergency and 2 change-of-medication requests; 17 for biologics. Re-audit planned 3 months after the form is introduced.

result.setting: 27 independent mental health hospital sites across London and South region (Cygnet Health Care)
result.standard: National clinical governance standards and the STEELL agenda (Safety, Training, Effectiveness, Experience, Leadership, Lessons Learned)

cycle1.result: Variability in leadership engagement, MDT attendance, safety reporting and documentation of clinical effectiveness (figures not reported).

result.intervention: Mandatory co-chairing of meetings by Medical Directors and Hospital Managers, leave planned around monthly governance meetings, enhanced contraband processes, lessons-learnt dissemination, structured carer events

cycle2.result: Improvements in leadership accountability, pharmacy attendance, lessons-learnt dissemination, GAP completion at admission and discharge, and carer engagement (figures not reported).

result.other_findings: Some inter-site variability persisted.

result.topic: STOMP psychotropic review in learning disability
result.setting: CAMHS Learning Disability Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHS England STOMP Pledge and local Trust guidelines for antipsychotic physical health monitoring

cycle1.result: 66 (62%) prescribed medication, all eligible for STOMP review; 64 had a behavioural support plan. Of 66: 35% undergoing reduction plan, 35% reduction not suitable, 30% no review or reduction plan.

result.other_findings: Antipsychotics were the commonest psychotropics (60%); 20 patients (38%) on more than one psychotropic; about 80% on psychotropics over 12 months. Re-audit in a year planned.

result.setting: Addictions service, Plummer Court, Newcastle upon Tyne
result.standard: NICE: all patients completing alcohol detoxification should be considered for acamprosate or oral naltrexone

cycle1.result: Anti-craving medication considered in 47%; acamprosate offered in all but one case; accepted in all but one case where offered.

result.intervention: Monthly follow-up with addictions service for six months, template letter to GPs requesting acamprosate prescription, audit presented to medical team, pathway amended to specify medical role at initial appointment
result.other_findings: Several GPs declined to prescribe acamprosate citing an outdated local policy. Re-audit planned in six months.

result.topic: Resuscitation and physical health equipment checks
result.setting: Four acute adult inpatient wards, mental health hospital, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: RCPsych Physical Health in Mental Health scoping group report and Resuscitation Council UK Mental Health Inpatient Care Equipment and Drug Lists

cycle1.result: Overall 90.0% of standards met; physical health equipment 83.8%; resuscitation equipment 94.2%.

result.intervention: Awareness presentations at governance meetings, complete equipment sets on each ward, registration of equipment on maintenance database with engineering servicing, weekly (previously monthly) resuscitation checks

cycle2.result: Overall 90.0% (144/160 items available and functional); physical health equipment 76.6% (49/64); resuscitation equipment 99.2% (95/96).

result.other_findings: Physical health equipment availability fell. Proposed named staff checker, physical health equipment checklist and electronic 'My Kit Check' platform.

result.setting: GP practice, South London
result.standard: NICE (2022): review within 2–4 weeks of diagnosis, or 1 week if suicide risk; QOF review within 10–56 days

cycle1.result: 41% (n=23) had a documented review; 25% (n=14) reviewed within 2–4 weeks; 39% met the QOF 10–56 day target. Suicide risk assessment documented in 91%.

result.other_findings: 27% of patients reporting suicidal ideation had no documented referral to specialist or psychological services.

result.setting: Children and Young People's Neurodevelopmental Service, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust (Hull and East Riding)
result.standard: NICE and local prescribing guidance: shared care with primary care after titration and dose stabilisation

cycle1.result: 62 (55%) had shared care requests; of these 43 (69%) accepted, 13 (21%) no response, 6 (10%) declined.

result.other_findings: 4 of 6 declines were from one GP practice citing local guidelines on methylphenidate. No clear documentation of prescribing decisions despite shared care; recommendations circulated and re-audit planned.

result.setting: National clinical audits: NOGCA (England and Wales) and Scottish QPI data
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Staging CT: England 83.1%, Scotland 98.5%, Wales 92.2%. MDT curative treatment plans: England 40%, Scotland 29%, Wales 34%; actual curative treatment 24–31%. Longitudinal margin positivity: Scotland 2.4%, England 5.4%, Wales 8.2%.

result.other_findings: Metastatic disease at presentation highest in Scotland (40%–42%). Mortality similar across the three nations; excision of more than 15 lymph nodes highest in England.

result.topic: Physical health monitoring in severe mental illness on antipsychotics
result.setting: 28-bed older adult inpatient psychiatric unit
result.standard: NICE CG178 (1.3.5.1, 1.3.6.1–1.3.6.4): shared choice of antipsychotic, baseline investigations, ECG, therapeutic trial, systematic monitoring

cycle1.result: Benefits discussed 9/19 (47%); side effects discussed 5/21 (23%). Baseline HbA1c, weight, pulse and BP 100%; lipids 86%; prolactin 77%; fasting glucose 38%; movement disorder assessment 22%; waist circumference 0%. ECG offered 94%. Rationale recorded 86%. Monitoring: glycaemic control 57%, movement disorders 14%, side effects 13%.

result.other_findings: Adherence and response to treatment monitored in 95%; no doses above BNF maximum.

result.topic: Integrated psychological medicine service and healthcare utilisation
result.setting: Integrated Psychological Medicine Service (liaison with physical health specialties)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Of 5 randomised patients with complete data, 1 reduced healthcare utilisation, 1 was static and 3 increased after referral.

result.other_findings: Service evaluation without a standard; healthcare utilisation judged a crude outcome measure and PHQ9/GAD7 not reliably recorded.

result.topic: Mental Health Act documentation and patient rights
result.setting: In-patient psychiatric unit
result.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice guiding principles

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Weekly MHA action email template, section paper scrutiny template, MHA actions in morning handover and review record form, easy-read leaflets, pharmacist and key nurse discussions, nurse teaching on reports and rights, liaison to keep capacity and treatment certificates filed

cycle2.result: 100% for capacity assessments, treatment certificates and timely reports. Patient knowledge of rights and MHA improved by 68%.

result.other_findings: Organising managers' hearings before section renewal still needed improvement.

result.topic: Under-18 admissions to adult psychiatric wards
result.setting: Adult psychiatric unit, Royal Cornhill Hospital, Aberdeen
result.standard: Mental Welfare Commission for Scotland (2013), Scottish Government Best Practice Guideline for Admission to Adult Mental Health Wards for Under 18s (2013), Mental Health (Care and Treatment) (Scotland) Act 2003 ADM notification

cycle1.result: ADM forms completed for only 40% (n=2). Average stay 20.4 days (range 7–42).

result.other_findings: 60% voluntary, 40% on Short-Term Detention Certificate. Most referrals came from regions without dedicated CAMHS beds.

result.topic: Time to cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
result.setting: Emergency general surgery, Southport and Ormskirk Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours (biliary colic, cholecystitis), 2 weeks (gallstone pancreatitis) or 6 weeks

cycle1.result: Biliary colic (9 pre-COVID, 5 during COVID): none had LC within 72 hours. Cholecystitis (20 pre-COVID, 16 during COVID): none within 72 hours. Gallstone pancreatitis: only 1 patient had LC within 2 weeks.

result.other_findings: Waiting times were longer during COVID. Delays linked to limited ultrasound, staff and theatre access; a hot gallbladder service with dedicated theatre slots was proposed.

result.setting: General surgery unit, University Hospitals Birmingham (emergency laparotomy and laparoscopic bowel resection)
result.standard: GIRFT, RCS and ASGBI Best Practice for Laparotomy and Laparoscopic Bowel Resection Surgery Documentation

cycle1.result: Indication 99%; operator names, position, incision and findings 100%; anaesthetist name 48%; WHO checklist 20%; bowel perfusion at transection 43% (of 64 resections); VTE prophylaxis 87%; antibiotics 65%; suture/clip plan 13%.

result.other_findings: An electronic documentation template or checklist is being trialled, with re-audit planned.

result.topic: Community treatment order paperwork and hearings
result.setting: General adult male and female inpatient wards, North East Essex
result.standard: Mental Health Act guidance on CTO paperwork completion and renewal hearings

cycle1.dates: Discharges over the last 3–5 years, each followed for 2 years
cycle1.result: CTO3 paperwork missing in 2 cases; one tribunal hearing missed; one CTO lapsed; remaining patients had regular timely hearings.

result.other_findings: Six of 13 patients were never readmitted in two years; sample too small to judge whether CTOs prevent relapse. Reminders from the MHA Office proposed.

result.topic: Transfer of older adults from acute hospital to psychiatric wards
result.setting: Liaison psychiatry, district general hospital transfers to inpatient psychiatric units
result.standard: Locally agreed gold standards and transfer checklist (medical optimisation, handover, documentation, informing patient and next of kin)

cycle1.result: MHA paperwork 36/36; patient informed 40; GP discharge letter 40; medical optimisation confirmed 38. NEWS charts sent 17, oral intake records 13, DOLS paperwork 4/9. Other items 50% (26) to 90% (40).

result.other_findings: Teaching for acute trust staff and a repeat audit planned; quality control of transfers to be added to liaison standard operating procedures.

result.topic: Impact of smoke-free policy in psychiatric units
result.setting: Intensive Psychiatric Care Unit, New Craig's Psychiatric Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 58 incidents analysed, mostly agitation, with lorazepam the most administered medication; all 9 staff survey respondents reported increased workload.

result.other_findings: Impact evaluation of the Smoke-Free Perimeter Law without a practice standard. One patient's clozapine levels changed with altered smoking, worsening symptoms.

result.topic: Appropriateness of GP referrals to community mental health teams
result.setting: Oxford City and NE Oxon Adult Mental Health Team, Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 21% of referrals inappropriate.

result.intervention: Team remodelled in January 2020 into separate assessment and treatment functions, with medics covering both

cycle2.result: 19.5% (546/2803) of referrals inappropriate; 14.7% (97/658) pre-COVID-19 vs 20.9% (449/2145) during the pandemic. 32.9% returned to GP after a single assessment.

result.other_findings: Students were 26% of referrals, with more ADHD referrals (17.7%) than non-students (3%). Automated logging of referral outcomes planned to expedite re-audit.

result.topic: Sexual side effects of antipsychotics documentation
result.setting: Meadowbank Ward, 12-bed adult male inpatient rehabilitation ward, Berrywood Hospital, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE CG178: annual review of antipsychotic side effects including sexual side effects; target 100%

cycle1.result: Sexual side-effect discussion documented within 12 months for 18 patients (82%).

result.other_findings: Nursing staff documented 14/18 using the trust physical health template. Four (22%) reported sexual side effects, one with no documented action. Staff survey, pathway, training and re-audit planned.

result.setting: Stroud Recovery community mental health service, Gloucestershire
result.standard: NICE guidelines: antipsychotics not recommended for EUPD and should be reviewed with the aim of reducing and stopping

cycle1.result: 30/37 (81%) with EUPD ever prescribed antipsychotics; 24 (80%) had no licensed comorbid indication. Mean prescription duration 36.79 months in this subgroup; only 10 (42%) reviewed with aim to stop or reduce; none offered a routine physical review.

result.other_findings: Subgroup was 75% female and 46% aged 20–29; 12 (50%) had more than one antipsychotic, quetiapine most common.

result.topic: Anticholinergic burden scoring in older adults
result.setting: Community Mental Health Team for Older People, Louth Meath Mental Health Services
result.standard: Local QI target: 90% of eligible patients with documented anticholinergic burden score by January 2026

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: PDSA cycles: MDT teaching, ACB prompt and ACBcalc.com link in new patient proforma, patient leaflet for ACB 3 or more, refined eligibility criteria, ACB recommendations in GP letters and MDT discussions, monthly run charts

cycle2.result: ACB scoring reached 100% of eligible patients by December 2025; overall 66% (23/35) across the period. All high-burden patients (8/8) had optimisation plans; 96% (22/23) of scores communicated to GPs.

result.other_findings: 100% of high-ACB patients had shared decision-making discussions; efficiency improved after the quick-reference guide.

result.topic: Perinatal assessment documentation of children's dates of birth and due dates
result.setting: Community Perinatal Mental Health Service
result.standard: RCPsych Standards for Community Perinatal Mental Health Services 5th Edition (2020), Section 5: record baby's age, date of birth and mother's due date at initial assessment

cycle1.result: 15/42 (36%) had children's age, dates of birth and due date recorded; 27/42 (64%) lacked this.

result.intervention: Results presented at a multidisciplinary team meeting
result.other_findings: Children's ages and gestational ages were more often recorded than dates of birth and due dates.

result.setting: Community learning disability psychiatry service, Caerphilly
result.standard: NICE and Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on regular review and documentation of indication

cycle1.result: 114 (97.4%) on at least one psychotropic; 77 (65.8%) on antipsychotics. Indication: clear mental health diagnosis 23/77 (29.9%), behaviours that challenge 15 (19.5%), no clear indication 39 (50.6%). Antidepressants (44): no documented indication in 8 (18.2%).

result.other_findings: 47 (61.0%) on antipsychotic doses at or below 25% BNF maximum. Medication increased in 27 (23.1%) and reduced in 23 (19.7%).

result.topic: Sexual history and sexual safety documentation
result.setting: Haytor Ward, acute psychiatric inpatient ward, Devon Partnership NHS Trust
result.standard: Devon Partnership NHS Trust Sexual Safety Policy (C60); NICE, CQC and Sexual Safety Collaborative guidance

cycle1.result: Documentation of sexual health and sexual safety below expected Trust standards (figures not reported). 50% of surveyed doctors aware of the policy.

result.other_findings: No sexual health section in the admission clerking proforma; the s1 template missed policy elements such as gender identity and history of sexual harm. Template improvement and training recommended.

result.setting: Two London hospitals, single histopathology laboratory
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 33 of 74 (45%) pigmented lesion biopsies reported as normal tissue; diagnostic rate 66%; 4 (12%) labelled inadequate.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic yield study without a practice standard. Only two biopsies orientated by the dermatologist; orientation and embedding recommended.

result.setting: Royal Bolton Hospital, Greater Manchester (fluoroscopy-guided stent insertion)
result.standard: Published international standards (not specified)

cycle1.result: 45% had stent-related complications; 14% stent migration into the stomach; 25% tumour overgrowth. Median survival after stenting 94 days.

result.other_findings: No difference in complications by stent type, covering or antimigration device. No stent-related deaths or perforations.

result.topic: Vitamin D supplementation in children and pregnant or breastfeeding women
result.setting: Two hospitals, pharmacist-led data collection
result.standard: SACN (2016) vitamin D recommendations and local guidelines

cycle1.result: Under 30% of parents (16/54) received advice on childhood vitamin supplementation; 24.5% of children (25/102) received supplementation. 77% (30/39) of pregnant/breastfeeding mothers received advice but only 54% (21) took supplements.

result.other_findings: 93 of 164 questionnaires returned (57%). Midwives and health visitors most often gave advice.

result.setting: Tertiary care children's hospital, all paediatric surgical services
result.standard: ACS NSQIP-Paediatric UTI rates; project aim of a 30% reduction in paediatric perioperative UTIs within 1 year

cycle1.result: Institution's paediatric UTI rate had an odds ratio of 1.9x compared with the predicted rate (NSQIP 'Needs Improvement'); audits of catheterisation practice identified areas for improvement.

result.intervention: Multidisciplinary working group; 'permissive list' of procedures for which catheters may be required; standardised early catheter removal except urological procedures; education on insertion and maintenance; standardised equipment and technique; electronic medical record order sets as a forcing function.
