result.intervention: QI approach with 4 PDSA cycles: MDT strategies to improve engagement with monthly physical health clinics, care plan points, diary reminders for bloods and ECGs, MDT and patient health education, and a designated support staff member for observations and physical health files.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 92%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 100%; monthly physical health clinics 88%; annual HIP 75%; annual antipsychotic monitoring/bloods/ECG 95%.

result.other_findings: At baseline 10 female and 12 male patients regularly refused observations, weights and physical health monitoring.

result.setting: NHS Tayside colonoscopy surveillance programme, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee
result.standard: BSG guidelines for colorectal cancer screening and surveillance

cycle1.result: 319 requests adhered to guidelines (73.5%); 328 (75.6%) scoped; 44 colonoscopies fell outside guidelines, 38 of them brought back too early or late.

result.other_findings: 58% of surveillance colonoscopies were normal and 1% showed cancer, with the highest normal rate in genetic family history patients. Nurse specialist review saved many appointments.

result.setting: Macclesfield Memory Services, Jocelyn Solly Resource Centre (nationally accredited memory service)
result.standard: NICE NG97 and Memory Services National Accreditation Programme standards

cycle1.result: 23/140 (16.4%) referred to the Involvement, Recovery and Wellness Centre, 12 booked onto workshops; 16 (11.4%) clinic letters documented referral, none gave a rationale; 100% compliance for trained staff and carer support standards; 99.3% offered pharmacological intervention.

result.other_findings: No access to individual/maintenance CST, creative therapies, psychology or OT due to vacancies, and no under-65s signposted to work or education. Recommended amending clinic letter proformas and educating staff.

result.setting: Danby Ward, adult psychiatric inpatient ward, Cross Lane Hospital (Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: Trust PRN guidance PHARM-0041-v4.2 (standard 100%): indication, dose/formulation/frequency, minimum interval, maximum 24-hour dose, review date, first-/second-line guidance, review if unused for four weeks

cycle1.result: 15 prescriptions with 32 PRN medicines: indication and dosing parameters 32/32 (100%); documented review date 0/32; first-/second-line guidance 0/18 where applicable; review or discontinuation after four weeks unused 0/8.

result.intervention: Trust-wide post-audit actions: automatic 14-day review date on PRN oral and IM regimens, updated PRN guidance on first-/second-line options with EPMA content and training materials, EPMA upgrade, and EPMA e-learning plus a quick reference handbook.
result.other_findings: Customisation of regimen dose screens is still in progress. A re-audit is planned after full implementation.

result.setting: Community mental health service (Monash Health)
result.standard: Monash Health clozapine patient management guidelines and RANZCP clinical practice guidelines

cycle1.result: Monthly weight, physical examination, medical officer review and full blood examination 97%; BMI monitoring 66.7%; six-monthly consultant review 42.4%; lipid profile 90.1%; echocardiogram 75.8%; most metabolic bloods 70–90%; all doses within recommended range.

result.other_findings: Clozapine level was subtherapeutic in 54.5% and 54.5% were on an adjunct psychotropic. Hypersalivation (57.6%) and weight gain (39.4%) were the commonest side effects.

result.setting: George Mackenzie House low-secure unit (CPFT) and HMP Whitemoor Fens Unit prison personality disorder unit (NHFT)
result.standard: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust and Northamptonshire NHS Foundation Trust physical health monitoring guidelines for antipsychotics

cycle1.result: 17/18 GMH and 23/50 Fens Unit patients eligible; laboratory markers monitored in 88–100%; waist circumference omitted in 100% at both sites; ECG omitted in 60% in prison and 14% at GMH.

result.other_findings: Suggested staff and service user teaching on metabolic syndrome and electronic reminders for due measurements.

result.setting: Working-age and old-age psychiatric inpatient wards, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines for baseline and follow-up prolactin monitoring with medium- to high-risk antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 47% for patients established on antipsychotics before admission and 43% for inpatient initiation.

cycle2.result: Prolactin monitoring compliance 100% both before admission and at inpatient initiation; of 25 started on medium- to high-risk antipsychotics, 9 had hyperprolactinaemia, 4 had appropriate management and 3 had repeat testing.

result.other_findings: Trust-wide recommendations from the 2021 audit were implemented but not described. Management of raised prolactin remains poor; a standardised pathway with electronic prompts and education is proposed.

result.setting: Community intellectual disability service; residential homes and carers
result.standard: PRN protocol standards (source not named): written protocol accessible to care staff, when to use, de-escalation methods, expected effect, minimum dose interval, maximum 24-hour dose and recording of use

cycle1.result: Medical file standards 100% achieved; PRN protocol standards achieved in only 53% of cases.

result.other_findings: Protocol gaps included when to use PRN, non-pharmacological de-escalation, expected effect, minimum interval and maximum 24-hour dose.

result.topic: Physical health screening in Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia
result.setting: Five Mental Health Services for Older Persons inpatient wards, Leicestershire
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Antipsychotics considered in 11/11 (100%) with psychosis; bloods in 20/24 (83%); ECG before antipsychotic or cholinesterase inhibitor in 21/24 (88%); cholinesterase inhibitors considered in 13/17 (76%); dopaminergic therapy optimised in 8/18 (44%); PD specialist advice sought in 5/24 (21%).

result.other_findings: Screening for autonomic dysfunction was poor and the pathway to PD specialist input unclear. Planned: raising awareness on parkinsonian medication review and autonomic screening, and discussions with PD specialists before re-audit.

result.setting: Rheumatology, University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay NHS Foundation Trust, Royal Lancaster Infirmary
result.standard: BSR draft guidance on patient-initiated follow-up

cycle1.result: 9/100 triggered a review; 8 received a nurse call-back within 48 hours; 1 needed urgent consultant review and was seen within 7 days; all 9 reverted to regular follow-up.

result.other_findings: 420 patients were on PIFU; commonest trigger was inflammatory arthritis flare (7). Authors concluded the pathway was safe with no worse outcomes.

result.setting: UK multi-regional audit, 85 hospitals (NHS trusts with BSG representation)
result.standard: Guidelines on use of red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, platelets and cryoprecipitate

cycle1.result: 391/1313 (30%) transfused; Hb >8 g/dL before RBC transfusion for bleeding in 69/220 (31%); prophylactic transfusion without a planned procedure in 94/153 (61%); FFP at INR ≤1.5 for high-risk procedures 3/16 (19%) and INR ≤2 for low-risk 6/18 (33%); platelets at count >50 before a procedure 9/25 (36%).

result.other_findings: Case fatality 10% (128/1313) and in-hospital VTE 2%. Prophylactic transfusion needs greater scrutiny.

result.setting: Acute medical unit and urgent care, Countess of Chester Hospital
result.standard: NICE NG225 self-harm guidance and NHS England Mental Health Access Standards (referral and assessment within 1 hour)

cycle1.result: Mean time to referral 20.03 hours (0% within 1 hour); mean time from referral to assessment 21.53 hours (9.09% within 1 hour); mean presentation to assessment 41.88 hours (0% within 1 hour); full psychosocial assessment 63.6%; risk assessment 0%; risk formulation 63.6%; safe prescribing in follow-up plan 33%.

result.other_findings: The commonest cause of delay was waiting for medical optimisation. Formal staff training and re-audit were recommended.

result.setting: Two regional dermatology departments, Royal Cornwall Hospital, Truro and Derriford Hospital, Plymouth
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Median EASI improved from 18 to 2.2 and DLQI from 20 to 7 at 16 weeks; EASI 50, 75 and 90 in 73%, 67% and 33% at 16 weeks.

result.other_findings: 39 patients were treated and 10 excluded for missing data. Ocular surface problems occurred in 8 (27%), newly in 3 (10%); six stopped treatment.

result.setting: Three dermatology departments: University Hospitals Southampton, University Hospitals Dorset and Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust
result.standard: UK guidelines for the management of soft-tissue sarcomas (2016 and 2024) follow-up schedule

cycle1.result: Wide variation in management and follow-up; at one centre (22 patients) 4/22 had 5-year follow-up, 4/22 had staging investigations and 3/22 had tumour grade stated.

result.other_findings: Results from the other two centres were still being analysed. Authors call for a UK-wide PDS guideline with standard histopathology reporting, staging and follow-up.

result.topic: Resuscitation trolley drug contents and checks
result.setting: 47 hospital clinical areas with resuscitation trolleys and/or emergency drug boxes
result.standard: Resuscitation Council (UK) acute care equipment and drug lists (2013) and local Trust trolley content list; daily trolley checks

cycle1.result: Drug content compliance 50%; oxygen cylinders on trolley 5/29; daily trolley checks 29/32; guidelines present on 31/32 trolleys but needed revision.

result.intervention: Trolley content list changed from 250 mL to 500 mL sodium chloride 0.9% bags kept as routine stock, and resuscitation guidelines revised for clearer paediatric dosing.
result.other_findings: 84.4% of areas did not stock 250 mL sodium chloride bags and 20 trolleys held unlisted drugs. The resuscitation committee agreed to re-audit at least every 6 months.

result.setting: Trainee induction, Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Aim to improve trainee confidence in remote psychiatric assessment by at least 40%; consent documentation audited against NHS England remote consultation guidance

cycle1.result: Pre-induction confidence: extremely uncomfortable 16%, not confident 31%, neutral 47%, confident 6%, very confident 0%.

result.intervention: Article of remote consultation tips, trust-wide video presentation, and an induction session with a video-simulated remote consultation, over three PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Post-induction confidence: extremely uncomfortable 0%, not confident 22%, neutral 52%, confident 26%, very confident 0%.

result.other_findings: Only 2/34 respondents had previous remote consultation training; early PDSA cycles had low response rates. The local consent documentation audit cycle is not yet complete.

result.topic: Bone health management in primary hyperparathyroidism
result.setting: Osteoporosis service, Basildon University Hospital, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE NG132 (2019): parathyroidectomy as definitive treatment, cinacalcet if surgery inappropriate

cycle1.result: Parathyroidectomy in 21 (32.8%); cinacalcet 10 (15.6%); alendronic acid 37 (68.5%), denosumab 24 (37.5%), zoledronic acid 10 (18.5%), risedronate 2 (3.7%); fragility fractures in 41 (64%).

result.other_findings: Denosumab and zoledronic acid gave consistent spine and hip BMD gains, while parathyroidectomy improved spine BMD but hip BMD declined. Local pathways are to be standardised.

result.setting: Old age liaison psychiatry covering 3 hospitals in Glasgow City
result.standard: Existing referral pathway using a Microsoft Word referral template

cycle1.result: 114 referrals (82%) adhered to the referral template; 72 (52%) contained adequate information.

result.other_findings: Delirium was the referral reason in 23% but the diagnosis in 34%, suggesting under-recognition. An electronic referral pathway with mandatory fields is pending.

result.topic: Menopause screening in women with intellectual disability
result.setting: Greenwich Learning Disability Team, Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Perimenopause screening of women over 40 at psychiatric assessment; target 90% of clinicians confident in identifying menopause symptoms

cycle1.result: None of the 7 eligible patients were screened for perimenopause, menopause or menstruation status.

result.intervention: Gynaecologist-led teaching for clinicians, an easy-read perimenopause screening tool adapted from the Greene Climacteric Scale, a prompt on the psychiatry assessment template, and menopause groups for patients and carers, developed through PDSA cycles.
result.other_findings: After teaching (31 clinicians), knowledge rose from 9% to 70%, confidence discussing symptoms from 57% to 80% and service awareness from 17% to 90%. All group patients improved by >1 point on a 3-point Likert scale.

result.setting: Long-stay dementia (old age) psychiatry inpatient unit, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Local QIP objectives: MDT notes to separate current and resolved issues, track progress, and assign actions to named individuals with review dates

cycle1.result: Key clinical elements recorded in only 0–15% of MDT entries; responsible team documented in 1.67%; review dates in 0%.

result.intervention: Co-designed structured MDT template (current issues, better/same/worse progress, named actions with review dates), closed-loop communication and weekly MDT summary sheets for nursing handover, through PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 100% completion across all measured domains by the second cycle; responsible team 100% and review dates 100%.

result.other_findings: Core fields reached 84–100% after the first cycle. Nursing staff used the summaries unprompted during handovers.

result.topic: Sexual health screening in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Female acute psychiatric inpatient ward, later extended to a neighbouring ward
result.standard: Current national guidance on sexual and reproductive health (not named)

cycle1.result: 12.5% of inpatients offered at least one of contraceptive counselling, cervical and breast screening or STI screening.

result.intervention: Women's health assessments with provision of emergency contraception and STI swabs, sexual health clinic referral protocol, dedicated clinic time, poster and leaflet, and an outcome proforma, over six PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 87.7% offered a leaflet and 63.1% offered counselling; 48.8% of these accepted at least one intervention.

result.other_findings: Dedicated clinic time gave the highest offer rate (94.1%, cycle 3); compliance fell to 54.2% at junior doctor changeover. Neighbouring ward offers rose from 28.6% to 63.6%; seven STIs were detected and treated.

result.setting: Behavioural Sciences Institute, Al Ain Hospital, tertiary child and adolescent mental health service
result.standard: Local hospital guidelines aligned with NICE CG155: prolactin at baseline, 12 weeks and six months after starting risperidone

cycle1.dates: Data collected April–July 2025 (patients started from January 2023)
cycle1.result: Prolactin at 12 weeks documented in 12%, with reasons for non-monitoring in 8%; baseline and six-month monitoring more often completed (figures not given).

result.other_findings: 86% of patients were male and 96% had psychosis with neurodevelopmental conditions. Electronic reminders, staff education and better documentation were recommended.

result.setting: Psychiatry inpatient unit, Allied Hospital 2, Faisalabad (tertiary care)
result.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines pre-lithium workup

cycle1.result: LFTs 50/72 (69.4%); TFTs 3 (4.2%); ECG 14 (19.4%); weight measured in none.

result.intervention: Results discussed at a departmental meeting with a faculty-led presentation on guidelines and targeted teaching for all residents.
result.other_findings: Weight measurement remained below 40%. Ongoing education, standardised pre-lithium checklists and regular re-audit were recommended.

result.setting: On-call psychiatry handover across Dykebar, Leverndale and Inverclyde hospitals, South Glasgow
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: All 8 resident doctors found the Excel handover inefficient and unclear.

result.intervention: New Microsoft Teams (Planner) handover with private access and automated retention workflow, launched across all three sites in April 2025.

cycle2.result: All 15 respondents agreed the Teams handover improved usability, clarity and clinical efficiency.

result.other_findings: The system was later adopted at Gartnavel and Stobhill hospitals in North Glasgow.

result.setting: Behavioural Sciences Unit, Al Ain Hospital, tertiary mental health service
result.standard: NICE and MHRA Valproate Pregnancy Prevention Programme guidance: documented counselling on teratogenic risk, contraception, pregnancy prevention and informed consent

cycle1.result: Full documented counselling on teratogenic risks with pregnancy prevention and contraception in 12 (24.5%); partial or none in 37 (75.5%); partner involvement 5 (10.2%); alternatives discussed 8 (16.3%).

result.other_findings: Electronic prompts, templates, multilingual leaflets and clinician awareness were recommended, with a follow-up audit.

result.setting: 5th National Audit Project, national reporting with a parallel anaesthetic activity survey
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Incidence of certain/probable and possible awareness ~1:19 600 anaesthetics; ~1:8200 with neuromuscular blockade and ~1:135 900 without; ~1:670 for caesarean section.

result.other_findings: 82 (66%) cases arose at induction or emergence. Risk factors included female sex, younger adults, obesity, junior anaesthetists, out-of-hours and emergency surgery and neuromuscular blockade; an anaesthetic checklist within the WHO checklist was recommended.

result.setting: Psychiatric inpatient units (male, female, forensic), Behavioural Sciences Institute, Al Ain Hospital
result.standard: Local guidelines informed by RCPsych Core Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: social work and psychology referral within a week of admission and input documented in MDT notes

cycle1.result: Social work referral within one week 29.0%; psychology referral within one week 32.6%; social work input documented in MDT notes 38.3%; psychology input 44.0%.

result.other_findings: The male unit had the lowest early referral (16.0% social work, 22.0% psychology); the forensic unit had the highest MDT documentation (75.0% and 56.3%).

result.setting: Psychiatric unit for older adult females, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust
result.standard: Antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring guidelines (not named)

cycle1.result: Age, MHA status, weight, BMI, blood pressure, QTc, indication and weekly reviews 100%; baseline ECG 86.66%; rationale for changes 83.33%; EPS and sedation monitoring 46.66%; lipid profile and LFTs 73.33%; repeat TFTs 26.66% and prolactin 46.66%; repeat ECG on time 53.33%; GP recommendations for yearly ECG and bloods 50%.

result.other_findings: Action plan: amended ward round template and a physical health monitoring poster for junior doctors and ward staff, with a re-audit planned.

result.setting: Acute inpatient psychiatric unit, two working-age and one old-age ward
result.standard: Local Trust VTE assessment policy (standard 100%)

cycle1.result: VTE assessment on admission 68%; questionnaire completed correctly 66.6%; examination findings documented 63.4%; reassessed at consultant review 1.8%; at-risk patients reassessed within 24 hours 33.3%; thromboprophylaxis offered when indicated 100%.

result.other_findings: Recommendations: VTE policy in resident doctor induction, handover of incomplete assessments, a poster, and consultant discussion at MDT, with a second cycle in 6–8 months.

result.setting: Female later life psychiatry ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE and National Osteoporosis Guideline Group guidance on FRAX screening, DEXA and treatment of fragility fracture risk

cycle1.result: FRAX calculated in 8/16 (50%) without pre-existing osteoporosis; FRAX communicated to GP in 2/8 (25%).

result.intervention: Fracture risk scoring added to a structured ward round template and osteoporosis information posters in clinical areas.

cycle2.result: FRAX calculated in 15/17 (88%); FRAX communicated to GP in 11/15 (73%); BMD measured in 1/10 (10%) intermediate-risk patients and recommended to GP in 3/10 (30%); 0/4 high-risk patients started on bisphosphonates.

result.other_findings: Assessment and treatment of intermediate- and high-risk patients remained poor.

result.topic: Lifestyle risk factor screening in psychiatry outpatients
result.setting: Community psychiatry outpatient and medication monitoring clinics, North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare
result.standard: Trust and national standards: physical activity, weight/BMI, diet, smoking and alcohol assessed at each appointment with interventions offered where appropriate

cycle1.result: No lifestyle factor was assessed at every opportunity; only 2 interventions (4%) were offered.

result.other_findings: Medication monitoring clinics did not perform better than outpatient follow-up clinics, and findings were consistent across staff grades and diagnoses.

result.setting: New Victoria Court, acute adult psychiatric inpatient unit (HPFT)
result.standard: HPFT Section 17 Leave of Absence Policy

cycle1.result: 157 leave episodes; incidents during leave 8.8%.

result.intervention: Leave feedback template completed by the safety nurse at the end of each shift to record leave outcomes.

cycle2.result: 137 leave episodes; documented leave outcomes up by 13.2% and documentation of what went well up by 50.3%; incidents during leave 0%.

result.other_findings: Nurses supported the template but raised workload concerns, and some forms recorded general observations. Staff training and trust-wide rollout are planned.

result.setting: ECT service, Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: ECT Accreditation Service (ECTAS) standards for consent, capacity and monitoring of target symptoms and cognitive side effects

cycle1.result: Legal framework and consent documentation met standards; baseline monitoring 100% for all measures, falling below 75% by course completion and declining further at months two and three of follow-up.

result.other_findings: Compliance was similar to previous local and national audits; inpatients had more missing data (11.5 vs 8.2). Mean MADRS fell from 42.1 to 21.3 and mini-ACE rose from 19.7 to 23.9 (p<0.01).

result.setting: High Risk Antenatal Clinic, Barts Health NHS Trust, London
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 18 patients with 22 pregnancies; 45% had preconception counselling before referral; 59% induction of labour, 23% caesarean section; 59% antenatal flare, 45% postpartum flare; 32% of pregnancies had no postpartum follow-up.

result.other_findings: Mean 3.4 clinic visits per patient (median 4); median delivery 39 weeks. The team planned a formal preconception counselling clinic for patients with AS.

result.setting: Harrogate Older Adult Community Mental Health Team
result.standard: NICE NG97 (2018) Dementia guideline and local trust guidance on antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring

cycle1.result: 88% had assessment of sources of distress; 42% had a non-pharmacological intervention before antipsychotic (58% after starting); 63% had documented risk discussion; 63% baseline bloods, 54% baseline ECG; 33% on treatment over 12 weeks had a discontinuation or dose-reduction trial; under 22% had physical health monitoring at one year.

result.other_findings: Random sample of 24 of 55 patients. Recommended a pre-prescribing checklist and a system to flag when monitoring and review are due.

result.setting: Adult male and female psychiatry wards, Lahore
result.standard: BNF guidance on prescription writing

cycle1.result: Generic names used in 40.6%; block letters 17%; start date recorded 82.8%.

result.intervention: Presentation of BNF prescription-writing guidelines on 7 December 2022 and copies placed at male and female nursing counters.

cycle2.result: Generic names used in 84.69%; block letters 71.42%; start date recorded 99.18%.

result.other_findings: Three cycles; an interim re-audit (December 2022, 170 prescriptions) showed improvement but documentation of prescription changes still needed work. Legibility stayed high throughout.

result.setting: Tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit, London
result.standard: Trust guidelines on seclusion monitoring and documentation, including consultant review within 24 hours and care plan modification

cycle1.result: Average seclusion 30 h; assault on staff as indication in 50%; consultant review within 24 h documented in under 70%; care plan modified in 63%.

result.intervention: Daily nursing safety huddles, weekly Incidence Reduction meetings and an ongoing QI project on restrictive practice.

cycle2.result: 18 patients, 46 incidents: average seclusion 20 h; consultant review within 24 h over 90%; care plan modification over 95%; just under half of seclusions monitored and documented per Trust guidelines.

result.other_findings: Assault on staff was the indication in 80.4%; rapid tranquillisation in 45.7% and restraint in 84.8% of incidents; over half had psychotic symptoms.

result.setting: Resident doctors' first on-call rota, Blackburn area
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 57 shift changeovers: complete handover (in person and written) 28% (16); in person only 23% (13); written only 35% (20); no handover 14% (8).

result.intervention: Handover importance to be covered at induction, reminder emails, and a poster placed in the doctors' on-call room; re-audit planned.
result.other_findings: Some written handovers were not found in the assigned Teams channel, suggesting handover was sent elsewhere; recommended one assigned location and senior involvement in monitoring.

result.setting: Four Teesside child and adolescent community teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: TEWV ADHD prescribing guidelines and NICE NG87 (2018)

cycle1.result: Verbal information given in 92% and written in 58%; pre-treatment assessment completed in all but 3; methylphenidate not first line in 4 cases; lisdexamfetamine used second line in 75%.

result.other_findings: Of the 4 not started on methylphenidate, 3 received atomoxetine by parental choice and 1 had contraindications. Recommended updated NICE-compliant trust guidance and a trust-wide audit.

result.setting: Community forensic supported accommodation, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: DVLA guidelines and GMC advice on informing patients of their duty to notify the DVLA

cycle1.result: DVLA discussion documented in 4/12; the 4 licence holders (2 full, 2 provisional) had 100% documented discussion and notification; 8 patients had no documentation about driving or DVLA.

result.other_findings: Authors recommend DVLA discussions for all patients with notifiable diagnoses regardless of driving status.

result.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, Chesterfield Royal Hospital (acute hospital)
result.standard: MHA Code of Practice; target at least 95% completion of core assessment and capacity-to-consent documentation within six months

cycle1.result: 33% (10/30) of MHA referrals did not result in detention; 90% of patients without a recorded core assessment and 70% without documented capacity were admitted informally or discharged.

result.intervention: Two PDSA cycles being implemented: mandatory digital fields in the referral pathway (core assessment, capacity, consideration of informal admission) and structured teaching for MHLT staff with visual prompts.
result.other_findings: Follow-up audit planned; baseline compliance percentage for documentation not given.

result.setting: Northern training scheme core psychiatry trainees, NHS trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 12/33 responded (36%); 11/12 (92%) received the report in time and agreed with RCPsych teaching and audit records; 58% said locality teaching attendance was accurate.

result.other_findings: Leave, on-calls and rest days were often captured inaccurately; 10/10 who contacted medical education had the issue resolved. Re-evaluation planned for July 2023.

result.topic: Sensitive language for suicide in discharge summaries
result.setting: Mount Carmel Hospital (psychiatric hospital) discharge summaries
result.standard: International Association for Suicide Prevention (IASP) language guidelines

cycle1.result: 26% of included discharge letters did not use appropriate suicide-related terminology; commonest issues were excessive description of the attempt (53%) and 'commit suicide' (28%).

result.intervention: Short presentation to foundation doctors on using sensitive language about suicide in discharge summaries.

cycle2.result: 20% of discharges did not use appropriate terminology (n = 34); use of 'commit suicide' fell significantly (OR 0.279; CI 0.0921 to 0.8452, p = 0.0240).

result.other_findings: Sample sizes are total admissions screened; only discharges with suicidal behaviour were assessed.

result.setting: Older adult psychiatric inpatient ward
result.standard: VTE and bleeding risk assessment on admission and at 24 hours (Department of Health VTE risk assessment tool)

cycle1.result: 3/23 (13%) had VTE and bleeding risk assessed on admission.

result.intervention: New paper VTE risk assessment proforma attached to drug charts (DoH tool plus psychiatric risk factors), education for ward doctors, and VTE risk review added to weekly MDT meetings.
result.other_findings: No patient needed mechanical prophylaxis; one was on treatment for pulmonary embolism.

result.setting: Three community mental health teams, East of North Wales, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: RCPsych 'ADHD in Adults: Good Practice Guidelines'

cycle1.result: Referrals documented ASRS in 34%, AQ-10 in 18%, W-FIRS in 0%; 46% diagnosed with a standardised instrument over more than one session; baseline BP 58%, pulse 70%, weight 50%, height 44%.

result.other_findings: Functional impairment and comorbid anxiety, depression and substance use were documented in over 90%; family and neurodevelopmental history and corroborative history were mostly below 50%.

result.setting: ECT clinic, Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NHFT ECT protocol: restimulate missed seizures per stimulus dosing protocol (or 10% dose increase in treatment phase), or document reasons

cycle1.result: 268 sessions, 26 courses, 23 patients: missed fit rate 12.6%, restimulation rate 67.5%; only 8/22 ST-phase restimulation doses matched the dosing chart; 2/3 treatment-phase restimulations used less than a 10% increase; reasons for deviation not documented.

result.other_findings: 30 missed seizures in seizure-threshold phase (22 restimulated) and 7 in treatment phase (3 restimulated); 47% stayed on the same maintenance dose.

result.setting: Pan-trust mental health services across four Black Country localities
result.standard: NCISH suicide prevention toolkit standards

cycle1.result: No deaths as inpatients; 6 suicides within three months of discharge; risk assessment and follow-up inconsistent, with structured risk tools used in only three cases.

result.intervention: Post-review changes: formal risk assessment tools, improved documentation, training on difficult conversations and better GP-mental health collaboration.
result.other_findings: Described as a re-audit but earlier results are not given. Recommendations include follow-up within three months of discharge and suicide prevention training for GPs and staff.

result.topic: Eating disorder referrals from primary care (children and young people)
result.setting: Manchester Foundation Trust Community Eating Disorders Service, referrals from primary care across Greater Manchester
result.standard: NICE guidance: children and young people with suspected eating disorders referred immediately and directly to specialist services

cycle1.result: 35% of GP referrals made correctly; 58% made immediately; 43.5% not initially made to MFT-CEDS; correct referral rates 10% (North) and 8% (South Manchester).

result.other_findings: Of 10 GP survey respondents, most did not know the referral guidelines or feel confident identifying eating disorders. Recommended an information video, GP referral template and re-audit after 6 months.

result.setting: Six acute mental health wards across two sites (UHH and UHW), NHS Lanarkshire
result.standard: MHLDA minimum admission standards: admission assessment, physical health assessment, medicines reconciliation and HEPMA prescribing within 12 hours

cycle1.result: Admission statement completed in 81%; MSE included 71%; risk assessment 18%; overall poor adherence.

result.intervention: Admission proforma with prompts, presentations at postgraduate and ANP teaching, standards and proforma circulated by email and on shared drive; proforma added to induction.

cycle2.result: Admission statement completed in 90%; MSE 91%; risk assessment 59%; where the proforma was used (57%) all components present in 97-100%.

result.other_findings: Physical health assessment components improved except a small fall in medicines reconciliation; all undocumented missing components occurred where the proforma was not used.

result.setting: Rose Ward, Prospect Park Hospital (acute mixed adult inpatient unit), Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust guidance: all admitted patients have serum prolactin measured on admission; prolactin >1000 mIU/L should prompt clinical intervention

cycle1.result: 69% had prolactin measured on admission.

cycle2.result: 76% (32/42) had prolactin measured on admission; 4 patients had prolactin >1000 mIU/L and 100% had clinical intervention.

result.other_findings: Six refused bloods and four had no documentation; symptom documentation was poor. Action plan: induction booklet guidance, posters and a symptom screening tool.

result.setting: Early Intervention Service, Limbrick Centre, Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Documentation of at least one specific side effect discussed for newly prescribed psychotropic medication; target 100% within 12 months

cycle1.result: 40% of first medical reviews documented side effects; 60% did not.

result.other_findings: Entries stating only that side effects were 'discussed' without naming them were not counted.

result.setting: Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, district general hospital (emergency laparoscopic appendicectomy)
result.standard: GIRFT documentation recommendations (34 criteria) for laparoscopic appendicectomy

cycle1.result: 23% of criteria documented well (>75%), e.g. closure 96%, recovery instructions 97%; 19% moderately (port location 70%, haemostasis 62%); 23% poorly (ports under direct vision 38%, residual appendix 39%); 36% very poorly (e.g. histology, doctor grade).

result.other_findings: Several items were recorded only in unscanned paper records. Changes to the electronic operation note format are under discussion before re-audit.

result.setting: Psychiatry trainees, Somerset NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Severn deanery and trust recommendation of one hour of supervision per week

cycle1.result: 17/27 (63%) responded; over half had no time set aside for e-portfolio; 4/7 core trainees discussed audit/QI with supervisors most/always; 100% found supervisors supportive; WPBA and portfolio review completion suboptimal.

result.intervention: Supervision template created; extension to a regional quality improvement project underway.
result.other_findings: Survey-based; CBDs achieved more often than ACEs/mini-ACEs, and 2 GP/foundation trainees could not obtain community experience.

result.setting: Two specialist inpatient units for adults with learning disability and mental health conditions
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Mean ACB calculator score 6.68 including prn medication (double the 3+ threshold linked to harm in the general population); mean AEC 4.21; LUNSERS 23.13; GASS 8.87.

result.other_findings: 89% were on antipsychotics and 58% on antimuscarinics; clinical improvement was good (CGI global improvement 2.37). Authors call for specific practice standards for ACB monitoring.

result.setting: Two acute inpatient psychiatric units, Fieldhead Hospital
result.standard: POMH-UK guidance: BMI, blood pressure, blood glucose and lipids checked at least once a year for patients on continuing antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Lipids screened in 68%, BMI 71%, blood glucose 74%, blood pressure 87%.

result.other_findings: 86% were on atypical antipsychotics. Authors recommend a tailored physical health monitoring guideline and staff training.

result.setting: 5th National Audit Project (NAP5) of the Royal College of Anaesthetists and AAGBI
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 75% of experiences lasted under 5 min, yet 51% (95% CI 43-60%) had distress and 41% (95% CI 33-50%) longer-term adverse effects; care before the event good in 26%, poor 39%, mixed 31%; 75% judged preventable.

result.other_findings: Awareness during sedation (~1:15 000) was similar to general anaesthesia (~1:19 000); paralysis was linked to distress and harm. Eight patients (6%) had taken legal action and 12 (11%) complained.

result.setting: National multicentre prospective audit (ARROW)
result.standard: NICE, ICARUS, BSG and AUGIS commissioning guidelines for anti-reflux surgery

cycle1.result: OGD before surgery in 156 (91.2%); manometry in 105 (61.4%); 24-hour pH study in 97 (56.7%); median referral to surgery 471 days.

result.other_findings: 240 registered, 171 with complete data; 93.3% had fundoplication (posterior 360° 44%). Two returns to theatre, 9 short-term complications and 24 delayed discharges.

result.setting: Rheumatology department, Northampton General Hospital
result.standard: BSR guideline on idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (March 2022), 26 recommendations

cycle1.dates: Patients seen within the last five years
cycle1.result: Steroids tapered 100%; DMARDs for muscle inflammation 91%; treatment for active skin disease 100%; ILD screening 100%; therapist-led exercise for active muscle disease 56%; psychological well-being formally considered 45%.

result.other_findings: Diagnostic and drug domains were strong; therapy access and psychological support were weaker. The SF-36 was suggested to address psychosocial domains.

result.setting: Enfield Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 46.9% of inappropriate referrals were accepted; 38% of all referrals were inappropriate; 71% of GP referrals and 55.5% of CMHT referrals were inappropriate.

result.intervention: Consultant psychiatrist based in the assessment team, then teaching for GPs and the crisis telephone service and weekly meetings with liaison and community teams.

cycle2.result: Inappropriate referrals fell to 27.4% overall (difference 10.6%, 95% CI 1.3-19.8%, p < 0.05); GP inappropriate referrals 36%; CMHT 12%.

result.other_findings: At an interim re-audit (February 2019, n = 175) acceptance of inappropriate referrals fell to 16.9% (difference 30%, p < 0.001). Liaison team referrals did not change significantly.

result.topic: Ethnic equity in perinatal mental health access
result.setting: Southwark Perinatal Mental Health Service
result.standard: RCPsych gold standards for equitable access to care

cycle1.result: 6.6% had no ethnicity recorded; no clear inequity at referral; 3/4 admissions were Black women, all detained; 5/6 antipsychotic prescriptions to Black women; 48% of 31 safeguarding alerts involved Black women; few psychology referrals for Asian and Mixed groups (2/35).

result.other_findings: The service was judged not to meet RCPsych gold standards for equitable care.

result.setting: General adult inpatient mental health units, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NICE guideline 'Smoking: acute, maternity and mental health services'

cycle1.result: 71.88% asked about smoking history; under 10% assessed in detail.

result.intervention: PowerPoint presentation shared on measurement tools for assessing smoking behaviour (after a first re-audit with no intervention).

cycle2.result: 57.14% assessed for smoking; under 40% assessed in detail.

result.other_findings: The first re-audit without intervention (19 admissions) fell to 36.84%, under 16% in detail. Doctor rotation may explain the small change; teaching at the start of each rotation is planned.

result.setting: ECT service
result.standard: Scottish ECT Accreditation Network (SEAN) standards: MoCA, MADRS and CGI before, after and at 3 and 6 months after ECT

cycle1.result: Pre-ECT MoCA 20/32, MADRS 28, CGI 26; post-ECT MoCA 10, MADRS 11, CGI 13; no 3- or 6-month follow-up assessments.

result.other_findings: Recommended robust processes and specialist nurse-led clinics for post-ECT follow-up assessments.

result.topic: Group and save before emergency cholecystectomy
result.setting: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Preston
result.standard: Trust guideline: preoperative group and save for all emergency cholecystectomies

cycle1.result: 447 (90.1%) had G&S; 3 (0.6%) of the G&S group and none of the 49 without G&S had perioperative transfusion (p = 0.331); only 1 transfusion truly indicated.

result.other_findings: Omitting routine G&S could have saved £24,976; authors suggest G&S only for selected higher-risk patients.

result.topic: Research and audit training for medical students
result.setting: Final-year medical students at 32 UK and Irish medical schools (cross-sectional survey)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 47.2% reported no formal audit training and 27.1% no formal research training; 53.4% had not performed an audit and 29.9% had not taken part in research during their course.

result.other_findings: Confidence was higher with previous clinical research experience (OR 4.21), additional degrees (OR 2.34) and male gender (OR 1.90); audit skills training in the curriculum was linked to more perceived opportunities (OR 1.52).

result.topic: Bone health assessment on androgen deprivation therapy
result.setting: Urology and osteoporosis services at two hospitals, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton
result.standard: National and international guidelines: fracture risk assessment with clinical factors and BMD to guide bone agent use and bone protection advice for patients on ADT

cycle1.result: 4.9% were already known to the osteoporosis service, but none had been referred for bone health assessment when ADT started.

result.intervention: Joint urology-osteoporosis guideline and management pathway for bone health assessment on ADT, with patient information, signposting and bone agent initiation by a trained team.
result.other_findings: Detailed performance against guidelines is given only in a table. The new pathway is estimated to need 114 new fracture risk assessments and up to 372 DXA scans a year.

result.setting: Community mental health team, rural Wales
result.standard: 10 standards derived from NICE QS80 (quality statement 6) on physical health checks for people on antipsychotics

cycle1.result: Average compliance across the three previous cycles used as comparator (figures not given).

cycle2.result: Compliance increased in 2/10 standards and decreased in 8/10 compared with the average of the three previous cycles.

result.other_findings: During lockdown (26 March to 26 June 2020) staff-patient contact rose by 79% versus 2019, with 61.75% non face-to-face compared with 84.31% face-to-face in 2019.

result.setting: Teledermatology 2-week-wait pathway triaged straight to surgery, Royal Stoke University Hospital (tertiary care)
result.standard: British Association of Dermatologists Teledermatology Quality Standards

cycle1.result: Response rate over 60%; 95% rated community photography good; 99% found pre-surgery information easy to understand; 100% rated overall care good or very good; 94% would recommend; 58% would still have preferred a clinic or telephone contact before surgery.

result.other_findings: Recommended a telephone review to complete stage one consent before surgery.

result.setting: St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Of 15 operated patients: 1 pathological complete response, 6 partial response, 8 non-response; 50% (n = 4) on ipilimumab plus nivolumab had adverse events.

result.other_findings: Results were less favourable than in the SWOG S1801 and OpACIN-neo trials; toxicities included dermatitis, colitis, hepatitis, hyperthyroidism, arthritis and neurovasculitis.

result.setting: 16 general adult inpatient wards and PICU, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust HDAT policy: 13 baseline physical health assessments and cardiovascular assessment before starting HDAT; NICE advice that doses above BNF range are justified and recorded

cycle1.result: Baseline assessments completed on 226 (81%) of eligible occasions and not on 54 (19%), excluding 98 refusals; cardiovascular assessment before HDAT in 12/29 (41%).

result.other_findings: Authors recommend raising ward nursing and medical staff awareness of the Trust HDAT policy.

result.topic: Smoking status and cessation in psychiatric inpatients
result.setting: Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.dates: Two cycles over 2 months (dates not stated)
cycle1.result: Smoking status documented in 66.7%; among 12 smokers: brief advice 33.3%, NRT offered 25%, referral 8.3%, follow-up plan 16.7%.

result.intervention: Staff education, reminders during admission clerking and emphasis on documenting smoking cessation measures.

cycle2.result: Smoking status documented in 93.3%; among 13 smokers: brief advice 84.6%, NRT 76.9%, referral 53.8%, follow-up plan 69.2%.

result.other_findings: Regular re-audit recommended to sustain compliance.

result.topic: Anticholinergic burden review in older adults
result.setting: Older adult ward, psychiatric hospital
result.standard: MediChec AEC score: individual AEC above 2 or total above 3 requires medication review; AEC recorded at admission, during admission and at discharge

cycle1.result: AEC documented for 22/24; 22.7% (n = 5) within 7 days of admission; no patient whose score indicated review had a documented medication review or follow-up AEC score.

result.other_findings: AEC scores were recorded only by the lead pharmacist. Recommended a poster and adding AEC to the ward-round template.

result.setting: Tower Hamlets Community Learning Disability Service
result.standard: Latest guidance: valproate not recommended for men under 55 unless no alternative, with completed Risk Acknowledgement Form

cycle1.result: 25 men on valproate (16 under 40); 10/25 had completed the risk acknowledgement form; 11 received valproate from other services and 4 were pending; 2 took over 2000 mg per day.

result.other_findings: Indications were epilepsy (12), bipolar disorder (10) and schizoaffective disorder (2). Authors recommend dose reduction or switching where possible.

result.setting: Department of psychiatry, Faisalabad Medical University (residents' records)
result.standard: C-SSRS: documentation of ideation, behaviour and use of a structured tool 100%; risk level and safety planning 90%

cycle1.result: Suicidal ideation documented 79.7%; behaviour 47.5%; intensity or frequency 25.4%; C-SSRS used 0.8%; risk level 2.5%; protective factors 0.8%; safety plan 0.8%.

result.other_findings: Poor documentation was consistent across all residency levels. Recommended resident training and building C-SSRS into electronic records.

result.setting: Community mental health team, Glasgow
result.standard: Annual physical health monitoring (Lester tool), including blood tests and ECG

cycle1.result: 60% up to date with blood tests; 28% had an up-to-date ECG; poor documentation of smoking, alcohol and weight and of interventions offered.

result.intervention: 30-minute all-inclusive physical health check-up in the psychiatry clinic (bloods, lifestyle advice, on-site ECG with Kardia 6L), with a shared letter to GP, psychiatrist and patient.

cycle2.result: 18/35 invited (51%) attended; 88% compliance with up-to-date ECGs.

result.other_findings: 88% were overweight, 50% exercised under 30 minutes a day and half needed active medical intervention (statin, blood pressure or diabetes medication).

result.setting: Chebsey Ward, St George's Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Average of seven days for staff to obtain eCPMS access.

result.intervention: Simplified ward-specific registration guide and closer collaboration with the CPMS registration team to expedite approvals.

cycle2.result: Average registration time fell to three days (57% improvement).

result.other_findings: Staff satisfaction with the registration process increased; the guide is to be shared with other inpatient wards.

result.topic: Index cholecystectomy timing after gallstone pancreatitis
result.setting: General surgery department, Northampton General Hospital
result.standard: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission for biliary acute pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 32.6% compliance.

cycle2.result: 64.5% had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission.

result.other_findings: Persistent barriers: limited ultrasound slots, insufficient hot gallbladder lists, pre-assessment clinics and reluctance to perform acute laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

result.topic: Annual structured risk assessment in community mental health
result.setting: Older adult community mental health team, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (Gartnavel Royal Hospital)
result.standard: Local guidance: CRAFT risk assessment updated at least annually, or sooner if risk changes

cycle1.dates: 16 December 2024 to 14 March 2025 (medical); mid-February to mid-March 2025 (nurse-led)
cycle1.result: Overall compliance 81.8% (108/132): medical 77.6% (83/107), nursing 100% (25/25).

result.intervention: Findings presented at the community MDT meeting and email to clinicians with updated guidance on CRAFT completion and how to find the date of the last CRAFT.

cycle2.dates: Mid-April to mid-July 2025 (medical); mid-June to mid-July 2025 (nurse-led)

result.other_findings: Time pressure in medical clinics and lack of automated EMIS prompts were likely causes; electronic prompts suggested.

result.setting: Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, Allied II Hospital, Faisalabad (inpatients)
result.standard: American Heart Association recommendations for ECG monitoring during withdrawal

cycle1.result: Baseline ECG in 7.1%; no ECG interpretation or QTc recorded; no repeat ECGs or cardiac laboratory tests, including in the 37.1% with cardiovascular symptoms.

result.other_findings: Recommended mandatory baseline ECG policy, staff education, ECG prompts in admission workflow and re-audit at 6-12 months.

result.setting: Plas Gororau community mental health team, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
result.standard: NICE guidelines on physical health monitoring for patients with SMI on antipsychotics or lithium

cycle1.result: Pulse 30.4%, BP 56.5%, weight 20.7%, HbA1c/glucose 41.4%, LFTs 58.6%, renal function 65.5%, lipids 58.6%; prolactin 75% of 4 needing it; lithium levels ≥4/year in 1/9 (11.1%).

result.intervention: Planned: a dedicated health worker to monitor all patients with SMI on antipsychotics, followed by re-audit.
result.other_findings: Patients on lithium or clozapine (dedicated clinics) had weight monitored more often (45.5% vs 5.6%) but bloods less often than those on other antipsychotics.

result.setting: Rheumatology department, Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Departmental PIFU-LTC standard operating procedure based on GIRFT guidance (entry and exclusion criteria, documentation standards, response to contacts)

cycle1.result: 81% (n = 42) met diagnostic entry criteria; 92% joined ≥12 months after diagnosis; 40% (n = 21) had no record of an information leaflet; 33% (n = 17) had no documented flare plan; contact to telephone review 1-3 days.

result.other_findings: 10% random sample of 520 patients; 15% contacted the department, and face-to-face review took 2-22 days.

result.topic: Depression care pathway for children and young people
result.setting: 26 community children and young people's teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust depression pathway based on NICE QS48/CG28 and NG134 (2019)

cycle1.result: ICD-10 diagnosis recorded in 19%; RCADS symptom tracking under 40%; 0% identification/referral to other pathways for mild depression in 16-18 year olds; 29% of teams did not respond.

result.intervention: Action plan after the first audit (details not given).

cycle2.result: ICD-10 recording 30%; RCADS tracking over 50%; identification and referral for mild depression in 16-18 year olds 82% and 100%; over 90% for comorbidity and context; 100% offered psychological intervention.

result.other_findings: Weekly side-effect monitoring in the first 4 weeks (43%) and referral of parents/carers (40%) remained poor; only 1/26 teams did not respond at re-audit.

result.setting: ECT clinic, Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE guidance and ECT accreditation service standards (indication, consent, monitoring)

cycle1.result: Pre-ECT assessment documented 70%; consent by psychiatrist 70%; baseline CGI/CPRS 20%; baseline MADRS 40% with no weekly monitoring; baseline MoCA 100% but not repeated every four treatments; under a quarter had post-ECT clinician review.

result.other_findings: Ongoing consent was not reviewed at each treatment. Revision of the local ECT record pathway by December 2023 and re-audit in March 2024 recommended.

result.setting: Bolton Early Intervention Team and inpatient mental health services
result.standard: NICE CG178: documented prescribing rationale, discussion of side effects and weekly weight monitoring for six weeks after starting

cycle1.result: Inpatients (15): rationale 5/15, side effects discussed 3/15, weekly weight 7/15. EIT starts (17): rationale 12/17, side effects 13/17, weekly weight 0/17.

result.other_findings: 52 FEP patients identified, 38 prescribed antipsychotics; 16 prescriptions (42%) changed within six months, mostly for side effects. Olanzapine and zuclopenthixol were common inpatient choices.

result.setting: Joint Perinatal Mental Health Clinic, Milton Keynes University Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 83% attended all appointments; of 32 who attended, 94% were seen by at least 3 MDT members and 74% had a perinatal mental health plan recorded; 28% seen with a relative.

result.other_findings: 82% had two or more psychiatric diagnoses and 26% were on two or more psychotropics. A standardised template and clinic model for other sites are planned.

result.setting: Nine general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Trust policy: admission clerking form and physical examination completed within 24 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Clerking within 24 h in 124 (78%); physical examination within 24 h in 83 (52%); of these, cardiovascular 86%, respiratory 90%, gastrointestinal 83%, neurological 76%.

result.other_findings: Recommended daily review of patients who decline examination on admission.

result.setting: Four South-West hospitals, Severn Deanery (North Bristol, Bath, Gloucestershire, University Hospitals Bristol)
result.standard: Draft BCSP guidelines for management of large (>2 cm) colonic polyps, 9 auditable outcomes

cycle1.result: All 6 malignant polyps tattooed; mean time to definitive resection 34 (BCSP) and 30 (symptomatic) days; adenoma recurrence at 12 months 0/22 and 2/37; 17 benign polyps referred for surgery, none discussed with local EMR experts; 1 haemorrhage, 0 perforations.

result.intervention: Large polyp referral pathway established at two centres in the region.
result.other_findings: Fewer EMR sites were checked when the index endoscopy was by a non-BCS colonoscopist (8/24 vs 10/13). Overall management was comparable to draft guidelines.

result.topic: At-risk mental state recognition and management in CAMHS
result.setting: Four Tier 3 CAMHS multidisciplinary teams, South West London and St George's Mental Health NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE recommendations and NHS England guidance on ARMS management in children and young people

cycle1.result: Significant variation in clinicians' confidence and knowledge of ARMS identification criteria and management.

result.intervention: 30-minute teaching seminar on ARMS criteria, CAARMS, psychological and family interventions and guidance against antipsychotic use, delivered in CPD slots.

cycle2.result: Improved clinician confidence in ARMS identification and management; all participants wanted further support.

result.other_findings: Suggestions included specialist CBTp and family intervention training, validated assessment tools and a dedicated ARMS service.

result.setting: Tertiary oesophagogastric cancer centre, University Hospitals Birmingham, accepting referrals from seven hospitals
result.standard: NHS England target: 21 days from OGD to communication of treatment plan

cycle1.result: 13.8% met the 21-day target; only 13.3% had next-day CT after OGD (median 5.0 days); median pathway 49.0 days curative vs 35.0 palliative.

result.other_findings: Oesophageal and gastric pathways were similar (44.0 vs 44.5 days); patients diagnosed at the tertiary centre reached first staging faster than those from non-specialist centres.

result.setting: Knowsley Assessment Team (outpatient), North West Boroughs
result.standard: Baseline cardiometabolic monitoring for patients prescribed or advised a dose increase of antipsychotics

cycle1.result: 50% (20) attended physical health review; 35% (14) not offered one; BP documented in 1 and BMI in 2; HbA1c within 12 months 67.5% and lipids 62.5%; abnormal HbA1c acknowledged in 4/7 and lipids in 1/5.

result.other_findings: 15% (6) did not attend two offered appointments; smoking, alcohol and drug use documented in 42.5%, 57.5% and 67.5%.

result.setting: Medical staff at James Cook University Hospital (acute hospital) and South Tees Liaison Psychiatry team
result.standard: Trust lithium guidelines; target 100% staff awareness

cycle1.result: Aware of renal and thyroid checks 96%; lithium effect on eGFR 84%; toxicity signs 68%; referral to liaison psychiatry 60%; interacting drugs 40%; checking lithium level on admission 24%; average 57% positive responses.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based knowledge audit; teaching sessions on lithium monitoring were planned.

result.setting: Two autism rehabilitation wards (Spring Center locked, Spring Wing open)
result.standard: Gold Standard Environmental Standards for LD and ASD inpatient hospitals and QNLD standards (22 parameters)

cycle1.result: Both wards met 15/22 parameters and failed 7, including no consultation with autistic people on sensory spaces, no patient/family feedback, insufficient autism training for all staff, no soft furnishings, no odour control and no unscented products.

result.other_findings: Findings shared with ward and hospital managers for a business case; re-audit planned in six months.

result.setting: Psychiatry junior doctors in North Wales
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Pre-intervention questionnaire of junior doctors (results not given).

result.intervention: New induction folder for psychiatry, refined over three PDSA cycles (e.g. adding emergency medication and deanery contact details).

cycle2.result: Overwhelmingly positive response from new and previous doctors after the PDSA cycles (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Sustainability is uncertain; plan to update the folder yearly at least 4 weeks before August induction and share it as a PDF handbook.

result.topic: Coagulation screening before central line removal
result.setting: Upper GI, HPB, lower GI and transplant surgery departments, Churchill Hospital, Oxford
result.standard: Same-day coagulation screen before CVC removal

cycle1.result: 41.8% had same-day coagulation screens, 17.9% the day before and 40.3% more than one day before; non-compliance 44%; INR normal in 88%, PT 74.6%, APTT 58.2%.

result.other_findings: 78 patients averaged 5.07 coagulation tests per stay; cost £64.76 per patient. Authors suggest a targeted, risk-based approach to testing.

result.topic: Staff knowledge of Parkinson's disease medication
result.setting: University Hospital Waterford
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 71 surveys returned (34 doctors, 23 nurses, 14 others). Only 11 (15%) correctly identified all PD medications; 32 (45%) could not identify when to give PD medications in relation to mealtimes; 29 (41%) would consider inserting a nasogastric tube for a fasting patient; 12 (17%) did not know Sinemet could be given via nasogastric tube.

result.other_findings: Non-motor symptoms identified: constipation (n=54, 76%), hallucinations (n=48, 68%), anosmia (n=18, 25%). Education sessions and hospital-specific guidelines were suggested.

result.setting: Warrington and Halton Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: NICE guidelines: early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis

cycle1.result: Admission covid swabs 64.7%, interval covid swabs 0%; hot gallbladder rate 8.8%; median admission to operation 4 days; readmission for complications 20.6%.

result.intervention: Green elective surgical pathway, clinical priority coding for elective surgery, a hot gallbladder pathway, and a dedicated weekend and evening list; findings presented at departmental meeting.

cycle2.result: Admission covid swabs 97.3%, interval covid swabs 54.1%; hot gallbladder rate 10.8%; median admission to operation 1.5 days; readmission for complications 29.7%.

result.other_findings: Overall performance still behind NICE recommendation; theatre pressure and cancer fast-track priority during Covid-19 were identified as factors.

result.setting: Cherrywood Clinic, three community mental health teams
result.standard: Royal College guidance on outpatient letters

cycle1.result: Consultant letters: diagnosis 93%, medication 93%, dosage 90%, mental state 66%, risks 83%, follow-up 96%. Junior doctor letters: diagnosis 88%, medication and dosage 76%, mental state 100%, risks 80%, follow-up 100%. More than 85% of data met the standard.

result.other_findings: Registrar letters had MSE in 80% of 5 letters. Areas to improve: MSE, medication and dosages, diagnosis and risks.

result.topic: Care plan documentation in clinic letters
result.setting: Sandwell CAMHS, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: BCHFT guidelines requiring a documented care plan covering 5 key criteria; GMC advice on contemporaneous records

cycle1.dates: clinic letters from the past 12 months
cycle1.result: Medication information included in 79% when relevant; physical health considerations 36%; crisis planning 20%; 15% of letters had no clear 'Care Plan' subheading.

result.other_findings: A standardised clinic letter template with a 'Care Plan' section and standard crisis contacts was recommended; re-audit planned.

result.topic: Bone health assessment after fragility fracture
result.setting: Off-site in-patient rehabilitation unit, Galway University Hospital
result.standard: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group: all patients with fragility fracture should have bone health assessment and pharmacological therapy if indicated

cycle1.result: 100% had corrected calcium measured; 93% (n=65) vitamin D; 91% (n=64) PTH; 66% (n=46) discharged on antiresorptive therapy; 33% (n=23) not prescribed any bone protection.

result.intervention: Education session for NCHDs and a discharge checklist prompting bone health review and consideration of pharmacological therapy.
result.other_findings: 74 patients had a fracture, 4 excluded for high-impact trauma; 6% (n=4) were discharged without calcium/vitamin D or antiresorptive therapy.

result.setting: Community hospital rehabilitation unit, St Ita's Community Hospital
result.standard: HSE medicines management programme anticoagulation guidelines and 2021 EHRA practical guide on NOACs in atrial fibrillation

cycle1.result: 9 of 25 inpatients (36%) on OAC. All had indication and treatment duration documented; 3 on reduced dose all with documented indication; only 3 had creatinine clearance documented; 1 on medications with a documented drug–drug interaction; none co-prescribed antiplatelet.

result.other_findings: Point prevalence audit; 7 on DOACs and 2 on warfarin. Interventions to improve creatinine clearance documentation were planned.

result.setting: Intensive care, district general hospital (Ashford and St Peter's NHS Trust), Surrey
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Significant difference (p<0.01) between infrared and tympanic readings, mean difference 1.18°C; pyrexia undetected in 4 of 40 patients with digital thermometers.

result.intervention: Infrared thermometers replaced with tympanic thermometers.

cycle2.result: Second cycle again showed a significant (p<0.01) difference with mean difference 1.92°C.

result.other_findings: Two patients undergoing hypothermia correction were not adequately measured with infrared thermometers.

result.setting: Geriatric ward, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: HIQA National Standard for discharge summaries

cycle1.result: Only 4 (20%) had all relevant information; 8 (40%) had complete clinical course; 8 (40%) had medication omissions; 5 (25%) omitted stopped medications and reasons; 5 (25%) had incomplete future plans; 4 (20%) omitted complications.

result.intervention: Discharge Summary Flowchart introduced as a guide; ongoing continuous audit by SHOs and interns.
result.other_findings: Authors recommended prioritising e-prescribing and electronic health records.

result.topic: Type A aortic dissection diagnosis and transfer times
result.setting: 28 UK cardiac centres (Association for Cardiothoracic Anaesthesia and Critical Care national audit)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Median symptom onset to ED arrival 2.3 h (IQR 1.4–4.7); median ED arrival to start of surgery 9.5 h (IQR 6.1–18.2); delays in diagnosis and transfer in 158 (47.3%); initial misdiagnosis in 52 (15.6%).

result.other_findings: 56 (16.8%) deteriorated before theatre; a doctor accompanied 50 (15.0%) during transfer; 64 (19.2%) died in hospital, 41 (12.3%) within 5 days of surgery.

result.setting: Emergency department, Ipswich Hospital
result.standard: BTS guidelines on emergency oxygen (2017): oxygen prescribed with target saturations

cycle1.result: 14% of patients had target oxygen saturations prescribed.

result.intervention: Results and BTS recommendations presented in departmental teaching sessions.

cycle2.result: 20% had target oxygen saturations prescribed (p=0.595, not significant).

result.other_findings: Teaching alone was insufficient; nursing prompts and senior spot checks were recommended.

result.setting: Five geriatric medical, orthogeriatric and rehabilitation wards across three inpatient sites, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: 2017 Medicines Management Programme directive for label-only Versatis (lidocaine 5% plaster) prescribing, licensed only for postherpetic neuralgia

cycle1.result: 26/129 (20%) prescribed Versatis, all off-label; potential cost €28,297/year; cost per plaster €2.58.

result.intervention: 2017 Medicines Management Programme directive restricting reimbursement to label-only Versatis prescribing.

cycle2.result: 4/127 (3%) prescribed Versatis, all off-label and all started before admission; no patient newly prescribed during admission; cost per plaster €3.46.

result.other_findings: Indications were osteoarthritis and spinal stenosis; three of four patients noted little analgesic benefit. Seventeen different analgesics were prescribed across 127 kardexes.

result.setting: LSCFT (psychiatry trust), training and non-training posts
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 84% of doctors satisfied with supervision; 72% had weekly supervision, 10% monthly and 16% bi-monthly; no difference in frequency between training and non-training posts.

result.other_findings: Limited discussion of QI, audit, research and psychotherapy in supervision. Proposed a supervision checklist, timeline chart, a menu of QI projects and QI training packages.

result.setting: Five rheumatology centres across Wales
result.standard: 2018 British Society for Rheumatology guideline for the management of adults with SLE

cycle1.result: No widespread significant changes in care compared with 2019; blood pressure and urinalysis not consistently measured; 48% of consultations were virtual.

result.other_findings: Results compared with previous Welsh and UK multi-centre SLE audits; group education on facilitating observations in virtual consultations followed.

result.topic: Memory service assessment and diagnosis waiting times
result.setting: West Leeds Memory Assessment Service, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Leeds KPIs: initial assessment within 8 weeks of referral, diagnosis within 12 weeks, post-diagnostic support within 2 weeks of diagnosis; target 80% of cases

cycle1.result: 19/59 (32%) assessed within 8 weeks; 23/41 (56%) diagnosed within 12 weeks; 25 (61%) of those diagnosed allocated a PDS appointment, none within 2 weeks.

result.other_findings: 26 (44%) had delayed assessment with no clear reason; 6 (15%) had delayed diagnosis with no clear reason. Re-audit planned in 12 months.

result.setting: Geriatrics COVID-19 cohort ward, Whiston Hospital
result.standard: Documented oxygen therapy on observation charts (correct device, flow rate and target saturations)

cycle1.result: not reported

result.intervention: Multiple PDSA cycles: staff education session, bedside oxygen guideline posters, a short quiz and reminder lanyard cards.

cycle2.result: 100% correct use of oxygen device and correct flow rate after the 2nd and 3rd PDSA cycles; overall improvement after 4 PDSA cycles.

result.other_findings: All staff reported feeling more confident in oxygen management after teaching; quiz results showed improved knowledge.

result.setting: Two orthopaedic wards, University Hospital Waterford
result.standard: Irish national guidance: daily delirium screening for all at-risk acute in-patients (RADAR twice daily within a Delirium Care Bundle); 4AT on ED admission

cycle1.result: 35 (71.4%) had the Delirium Care Bundle commenced; RADAR completed to an estimated 46% of target; 7 (16.6%) screened with 4AT in ED.

result.other_findings: 11 (22.4%) had a positive RADAR, four of whom had a negative 4AT in ED; documentation of actions after a positive screen was suboptimal.

result.setting: Acute frailty ward, St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: NICE Delirium Guidelines (CG103)

cycle1.result: Initial admission proforma used in 86% of admissions; 53% had completed delirium assessments; delirium prevalence 25%; resuscitation forms 86%; CFS 60%.

result.intervention: Admission proforma co-developed with patients and the MDT was modified based on feedback.

cycle2.result: Modified proforma used in 94%; delirium assessments completed in 79%; delirium diagnosed in 43%; resuscitation forms 93%; CFS 79%.

result.other_findings: These were cycles three and four of an ongoing project. Delirium and CFS 6/7 were associated with longer length of stay.

result.setting: Older person's rehabilitation service, post-acute rehabilitation hospital (The Royal Hospital Donnybrook, Dublin)
result.standard: 4AT recommended delirium detection tool

cycle1.result: 0% compliance with any formal delirium screening tool.

result.intervention: Staff education on delirium, a multidisciplinary Delirium Champions Group, and a Delirium Screen proforma with an attached 4AT sticker for all new admission charts.

cycle2.result: 92% compliance with 4AT use at admission, with full completion of the Delirium Screen proforma including risk factors.

result.other_findings: Most patients had at least 2 delirium risk factors on admission. The champions group continues staff education and is exploring environmental design.

result.topic: Colorectal cancer resection volume and outcome
result.setting: 144 hospitals in the National Bowel Cancer Audit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: No significant difference between centre or surgeon volume for adjusted 90-day and 2-year mortality; high ACPGBI membership associated with reduced 90-day mortality (p=0.006) but not 2-year (p=0.198).

result.other_findings: CUSUM threshold 36 per year for centre volume (p=0.003) and 15 per year for surgeon volume (p=0.241); 17,703 patients in the 2016 dataset and 781 surgeons.

result.setting: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
result.standard: British Hernia Society guidance on postoperative information after inguinal hernia repair

cycle1.result: Analgesia 0%, bruising/swelling 45%, heavy lifting 75%, DVT/mobility 63%, numbness/pain 0%, closure type 36%, safety-netting 45%, exercise 45%, dressing changes 16%, mesh 90%, postoperative bleeding 50%, showering/bathing 50%.

result.intervention: Standardised patient information leaflet on analgesia, exercise and lifting, wound care, closure type and red-flag symptoms given to all patients.

cycle2.result: GP and ED attendances for postoperative concerns decreased substantially; 98% of patients reported improved understanding of postoperative instructions.

result.other_findings: Second-cycle documentation compliance figures were not reported.

result.topic: Barriers to national stroke audit data collection
result.setting: Irish health professionals involved in the Irish National Audit of Stroke
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Main barriers: lack of time and resources, infrastructural challenges (computers, desk space, IT) and perceived uselessness of the audit. Facilitators: shared data-input systems and leadership valuing the audit.

result.other_findings: Qualitative semi-structured interview study; professionals who valued the audit viewed data input more positively.

result.topic: Stroke outcomes in patients aged 90 and over
result.setting: Irish National Audit of Stroke national data
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: People ≥90 had higher in-hospital mortality (26.8% vs 17.4%, P<.001) and were less likely to have mRS <3 at discharge (17.0% vs 35.8%, P<.001) than those aged 80–89.

result.other_findings: 7329 events in 80–89 year olds and 1708 in ≥90; AF detection did not differ (33.9% vs 32.4%, P=.38).

result.setting: St Mary's Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Formal pain assessment documented on admission in post-stroke patients

cycle1.result: Only 25% of patients had formal pain assessment documented on admission.

result.intervention: Pain assessment proforma incorporated into the admission proforma, with the Numerical Pain Scale and the Abbey Pain Scale.
result.other_findings: Staff found the proforma a useful prompt; barriers were time constraints, unfamiliarity with tools and possible inaccuracy of scores.

result.setting: District general hospital (North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust)
result.standard: International standards for imaging in suspected acute appendicitis (not specified)

cycle1.result: Ultrasound performed in 10%: sensitivity 44%, specificity 88%, PPV 57%, NPV 84%. CT performed in 22%: sensitivity 99%, specificity 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 88%.

result.other_findings: Use of imaging versus diagnostic laparoscopy was associated with greater length of stay and readmission rates.

result.setting: Two general medical wards, Naas General Hospital (Model 3 hospital)
result.standard: HSE National Guidelines: 4AT cognitive screening within 24 hours, delirium and risk factor documentation, non-pharmacological management and antipsychotic use

cycle1.result: Cognitive screening within 24 hours in 34% (n=16); delirium documented in 8.5% (n=4); 15% (n=7) newly prescribed antipsychotics within 24 hours, 57% (n=4) of whom lacked a formal delirium diagnosis.

result.other_findings: Of those screened, 75% (n=12) were abnormal. A 'Delirium Tool' for 4AT and PINCH-ME risk factors with education sessions and re-audit were planned.

result.setting: Nationwide Dutch Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer Audit (DUCA)
result.standard: DUCA predefined quality measures, including treatment start within 5 weeks of diagnosis and at least 15 examined lymph nodes

cycle1.result: Oesophageal cancer treatment started within 5 weeks in 32.5%; ≥15 lymph nodes examined in 50.3% (oesophageal) and 47.5% (gastric); gastric postoperative mortality 8.0%.

result.intervention: Nationwide web-based registration with weekly updated, benchmarked feedback on process and outcome measures.

cycle2.result: Treatment within 5 weeks 41.0% (P<0.001); ≥15 lymph nodes 73.0% oesophageal and 73.6% gastric (both P<0.001); gastric postoperative mortality 4.0% (P=0.031).

result.other_findings: 2786 oesophageal and 1887 gastric cancer patients registered 2011–2014; case ascertainment approached 100% in 2013; oesophageal postoperative mortality stable around 4.0%.

result.setting: General surgery, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin (university hospital)
result.standard: Electrolytes monitored every 48 hours; abnormalities treated within 24 hours; dietetics referral within 48 hours of nil-by-mouth

cycle1.result: 51 (98%) had electrolytes every 48 hours; magnesium, phosphate and/or calcium not measured before dietetics input in 9 (17%); only 18 (64%) of 28 patients with abnormalities treated within 24 hours; 46% referred to dietetics after 48 hours.

result.other_findings: Phosphate and calcium were most often not corrected within 24 hours (50%). A local protocol with streamlined dietetics referral was proposed.

result.setting: National Major Trauma Centre, Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin
result.standard: Irish national trauma guidelines for specialist ward admission and neurosurgical referral

cycle1.result: 123 (60.6%) managed on trauma wards; 29 (14.3%) needed intensive care; 28 (13.8%) transferred to a neurosurgical centre, with GCS change the only significant predictor (p = 0.017).

result.other_findings: 107 (52.7%) were aged ≥65; their 30-day mortality was 7.4% vs 2% and median stay 9 vs 5 days. A TBI unit has opened and a second cycle is planned.

result.setting: North Kirklees community mental health team, old age psychiatry services (SWYPFT)
result.standard: SWYPFT standards, NICE guidelines and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines (14th edition) for prolactin monitoring

cycle1.result: Prolactin done at initiation in 2/12; on LAI 7/11; on oral antipsychotic needing monitoring 5/11.
