result.intervention: Recommendations made to improve completion rate; audit tool updated to reflect changes to the electronic form.

cycle2.result: 95% completion; 74% completed on day of admission or next day; 26% no documentation of prior prophylactic anticoagulants; 7% no documented outcome.

result.other_findings: The 100% target was still not met.

result.topic: Pre-operative blood tests before minor surgery
result.setting: Surgical Emergency Unit, Walsall Manor Hospital; incision and drainage of abscess
result.standard: NICE NG45: no routine bloods for ASA 1 or 2 patients having minor surgery

cycle1.result: 93 patients had pre-operative blood tests; 7 were ASA 3 or higher; cost of unnecessary tests £4,092 (£24,552 per year).

result.other_findings: Blood tests did not change management; 16 had CRP >50 and 9 had WCC >15.

result.topic: Abdominal wall closure and incisional hernia
result.setting: University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff; colorectal cancer resections
result.standard: European Hernia Society guidelines: small bites closure and off-midline incisions

cycle1.result: Incisional hernia rate 31.4% at mean 24.9 months; small bites used in 38 (23.6% hernia) vs large bites in 80 (35.0%); midline 40.7% vs off-midline 6.3%.

result.other_findings: Hernia rates 44.1% laparotomy, 37.2% midline extraction, 8% Pfannenstiel, 0% transverse; uptake of small bites and off-midline incisions low.

result.topic: Carotid endarterectomy symptom to surgery time
result.setting: Vascular unit, Cumberland Infirmary; patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy
result.standard: National standards (National Vascular Registry): surgery within 14 days and referral within 7 days of symptoms

cycle1.result: 60% had surgery within 14 days (national 49%); median symptom to surgery 13 days (national 14); 60% referred within 7 days (national 72%).

result.other_findings: No post-operative deaths; adjusted stroke and death rate 2.5% vs national 1.9%; average stay two days.

result.topic: Treatment escalation plan and CPR documentation
result.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, district general hospital; emergency surgical admissions
result.standard: Target of TEP completion on first consultant ward round

cycle1.result: 19 (15%) had TEP forms; 5 (26%) by parent surgical team; median time to completion 2 days; 39 of 47 operated patients (83%) had no TEP.

result.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and target set for TEP completion on first consultant ward round.

cycle2.result: 26 (17%) had TEP forms; 11 (42%) by parent surgical team; median time 1 day; 56 of 69 operated patients (81%) had no TEP.

result.other_findings: Completion rates remained low across both cycles.

result.setting: York Teaching Hospital; endoscopy service
result.standard: PC-CRC rate as endoscopy performance benchmark

cycle1.result: 32 PC-CRCs; most plausible cause missed lesion despite adequate bowel preparation (76%); commonest subtype non-interval C (38%); 3 of 18 endoscopists poor performers (≥4 PC-CRC).

result.other_findings: Withdrawal time, CIR and ADR did not differ between good and poor performers; overall rate described as acceptable.

result.topic: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis
result.setting: District general hospital; patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis
result.standard: NICE CG188: LC within 1 week of diagnosis; BBUGSS morbidity <10%

cycle1.result: None (0/61) had LC within 1 week; 26 (43%) had grade II and IIIa complications.

result.other_findings: All LCs were elective, many as day cases.

result.topic: Treatment escalation plan and CPR documentation
result.setting: NHS Fife; General Surgery admissions and referrals
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 42% completion after intervention in the 2019 audit (12% before).

cycle2.result: 46.6% (34/73) had CPR and escalation status completed; all not-for-resuscitation patients had DNACPR forms, discussion and documentation.

result.other_findings: Earlier audits in 2017 and 2018 showed 0% and 2% completion.

result.setting: Great Western Hospital; patients admitted from A&E or SAU with acute bowel obstruction
result.standard: NCEPOD 2020 report on acute bowel obstruction (avoid imaging delays and AXR before CT)

cycle1.result: 70.1% had CT, 42% of these after AXR; average time to definitive radiological diagnosis 27.8hr.

result.intervention: Evidence-based acute bowel obstruction care pathway implemented and publicised.

cycle2.result: 18% had both AXR and CT; average time to diagnosis 10.7hr.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Royal Preston Hospital; junior clinicians and patients prescribed maintenance fluid
result.standard: Trust/NICE guidelines: 0.18% saline in glucose 4% as recommended maintenance fluid

cycle1.result: 16% prescribed the recommended maintenance fluid; Plasma-Lyte most prescribed (42%).

result.intervention: Posters and email reminders of trust IV fluid prescribing guidelines.
result.other_findings: Junior knowledge (n=21) improved: recommended fluid 52% to 80%, ml/kg/day 66% to 70%, monitoring 52% to 100%.

result.setting: Warwick Hospital; ED referrals with biliary disease
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 5 biliary colic, 4 cholangitis, 13 cholecystitis; 16/17 with cholecystitis/cholangitis had raised bloods and 16/17 had US; 1 cholecystitis patient had LC, 7 on waiting list.

result.other_findings: Biliary colic patients had near-normal bloods, suggesting a group for discharge with outpatient US; access to timely LC needs improvement.

result.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; children undergoing tonsillectomy
result.standard: National standards; new ibuprofen guidance 7.5mg/kg QDS

cycle1.result: 95% prescribed inadequate ibuprofen (mean 5.5mg/kg); 6% presented with bleeding, none returned to theatre.

result.intervention: New ibuprofen prescribing guideline (7.5mg/kg QDS instead of 5mg/kg TDS) with reduced opioid prescribing.

cycle2.result: 55% prescribed correct 7.5mg/kg QDS; no readmissions for pain; low number of bleeds.

result.other_findings: All readmissions for pain or haemorrhage in cycle 1 were on TDS ibuprofen; about 110 tonsillectomies per cycle (approximate).

result.topic: Preoperative risk optimisation in hernia repair

result.setting: Single centre (George Eliot Hospital, Nuneaton)
result.standard: Standard checklist by Kikuchi et al

cycle1.result: Pre-op rectal examination recorded in 24%; tumour number 40%; completeness of resection 32%; tumour location 96%.

result.intervention: Teaching session at departmental teaching and a template operation note.
result.other_findings: Described as a 2-cycle audit but second-cycle results not given.

result.topic: Paediatric vulval psoriasis presentation and management
result.setting: Combined dermatology and gynaecology private vulval disease referral practice, Sydney
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Nonspecific erythema in 85%; psoriasis elsewhere on skin in 78%; 5% required systemic treatment.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Postoperative ICU admission for high-risk emergency laparotomy
result.setting: Hospital NELA database (Whiston Hospital)
result.standard: NELA recommendation: high-risk patients (predicted mortality >5%) managed on ICU post-operatively

cycle1.result: Over 80% of high-risk patients admitted to ICU; 46 high-risk patients managed on the ward.

result.other_findings: ICU patients had higher predicted NELA mortality and higher mortality; authors suggest ward care may suit some with 5–10% predicted mortality.

result.topic: GP review before surgical assessment unit referral
result.setting: Surgical assessment unit, Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 3 (12.5%) not seen face-to-face by GP, all admitted; 7 (29%) of those seen by GP discharged same day.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Tertiary care centre (Aberdeen Royal Infirmary)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: No inpatient or 30-day deaths; length of stay 3 to 138 days.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: St. Luke's General Hospital, Kilkenny (Endorad reports)
result.standard: BSG and AUGIS: photo-documentation of 8 standard stations in OGD

cycle1.result: No report had photo-documentation of all 8 stations; most (40%) had 5 stations; retroflexion 95%, D2 84%.

result.other_findings: 60% of OGDs done by surgeons, 25% by gastroenterologists, 15% by ANPs.

result.setting: District general hospital (Wirral University Teaching Hospital), A&E CT hip requests
result.standard: NICE CG214 hip fracture management; expected compliance 95%

cycle1.result: Full examination documented in 85%; weightbearing status documented in 33%.

result.intervention: Teaching at A&E induction on the referral process and pathway.

cycle2.result: Full examination documented in 93%; weightbearing status 76%; 44% improvement in hot reporting before CT; CT did not delay surgery beyond 36 hours in 95%.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Colorectal urgent suspected cancer referrals (NHS Ayrshire & Arran)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: After phone assessment 29% had colonoscopy; invasive cancer in 0.14% (n=4); 225 not initially assessed were re-invited at 6 months and no cancer was found.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Graduate medical education residency programme
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: not reported

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: North Manchester General Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Five (7.8%) returned to theatre: one (1.5%) during inpatient stay for haematoma, four (6.3%) at 3 to 12 weeks.

result.other_findings: Infection rates higher in smokers and BMI >35; results used to reintroduce reconstruction with strict criteria.

result.setting: Mater Dei Hospital, Malta
result.standard: Royal College of Radiologists recommendations: CT at least 72 hours after symptom onset, prognostic factors in report, gallbladder US within 24 hours

cycle1.result: Of 99 CTs, 25.3% at least 72 hours after symptoms; 24.2% reported all 3 prognostic factors; 20.2% had gallbladder US within 24 hours.

result.intervention: Planned educational sessions for emergency doctors, surgeons and radiologists.
result.other_findings: 47.3% of those with early CT had further CT or MRCP in the same admission.

result.setting: Surgical FY1 doctors (Altnagelvin Hospital, Londonderry)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Average confidence 5 out of 10; 82% never shown a Tiemann-tip catheter; 90% never shown a 3-way catheter.

result.intervention: Teaching session on difficult catheters including Tiemann-tip and 3-way catheters.

cycle2.result: 100% felt more confident with difficult catheters.

result.other_findings: Confidence survey rather than audit against a standard.

result.topic: Home breast milk fortifier after preterm discharge
result.setting: Tertiary surgical neonatal unit
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Baseline growth measured as change in SD score from birth (figures not given for baseline).

result.intervention: Home breast milk fortifier until 48 weeks' gestational age, supported by an electronic patient information sheet developed over four PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Improved growth: at discharge cSDS weight −0.7, head circumference 0.4, length −0.8; at 1 year weight 0.9, length 0.8.

result.other_findings: Home fortifier appeared safe and acceptable to parents.

result.setting: Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust; inpatient admissions for acute cholecystitis
result.standard: Revised AUGIS guidelines for acute cholecystitis management during Covid-19

cycle1.result: 19 patients (80%) managed non-surgically in accordance with AUGIS guidelines; 10 (41.7%) antibiotics alone, 4 (16.6%) cholecystostomy; 12 (50%) discharged within 3 days; 5 (20.8%) needed laparoscopic cholecystectomy for lack of progress.

result.other_findings: 5 conservatively managed patients (20.8%) were readmitted with ongoing cholecystitis or pancreatitis; authors recommend laparoscopic cholecystectomy remains an option during the pandemic.

result.setting: Royal Preston Hospital; surgical handover sheets
result.standard: RCS England essential and desirable handover criteria; essential criteria documentation should be 100%

cycle1.result: Essential criteria: date of admission 47%, responsible consultant 0%, current diagnosis 83%, investigations 84%. Desirable: past medical history 42%, management plans 96%, COVID status 52%.

result.intervention: New handover template introduced, posters displayed and email reminders of RCS guidelines sent.

cycle2.result: Essential criteria: date of admission 60%, responsible consultant 100%, current diagnosis 100%, investigations 100%. Desirable: past medical history 62%, management plans 100%, COVID status 79%; VTE documented in 58%.

result.other_findings: Busy ward rounds, multiple clinicians leading rounds, frequent patient relocation and outlying patients made handover complex.

result.setting: Acute Receiving Unit, Dumfries and Galloway Royal Infirmary; emergency surgical admissions
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: VTE prophylaxis plans documented in only 24% of admissions; omission rates out-of-hours vs in-hours: systemic enquiry 42 vs 100%, family history 31% vs 66%.

result.intervention: Departmental meeting convened to stress the importance of accurate and comprehensive clerk-ins to ARU doctors.
result.other_findings: Documentation quality was worse for out-of-hours admissions.

result.setting: Barnsley Hospital (district general hospital); nurse-led colorectal cancer follow-up
result.standard: NICE guidelines for colorectal cancer surveillance with CEA and CT chest, abdomen and pelvis
result.other_findings: 3-year CT surveillance in high-risk patients was the weakest area (46%).

result.setting: Care of the Elderly wards, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital
result.standard: NICE guidelines: 100% of patients on geriatric wards to have delirium considered via the 4AT

cycle1.result: 50.7% (21) suspected delirious; of these 9.5% (2) had a delirium assessment on the same day.

result.intervention: Lanyard prompt card with the 4AT distributed to all physicians and a departmental teaching session on delirium for juniors (PDSA).

cycle2.result: 36% (14) suspected delirious; of these 43% (6) had a 4AT score on the same day.

result.other_findings: 4AT assessments roughly tripled but remained well below target; plan to expand to all medical and surgical wards.

result.setting: General surgery, Worcestershire Royal Hospital
result.standard: PRSB electronic discharge summary guidance (endorsed by NICE), 13 categories

cycle1.result: 8% overall compliance.

result.intervention: Poster outlining EDS criteria placed in doctors' office after cycle 1; teaching session for junior doctors before cycles 3 and 4.
result.other_findings: Four cycles 2020–2022: 8%, 22%, 34%, 69% compliance. Comorbidities section remained poorly completed.

result.setting: Brighton and Sussex University Hospitals NHS Trust; patients with open limb fractures
result.standard: BOAST 4: prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury; BSUH antibiotic guidelines

cycle1.result: 48 (92.3%) prescribed antibiotics before definitive surgery, mean time to administration 271 minutes; 41 (78.8%) prescribed per BSUH guidelines; 15.4% initial STAT prescriptions.

result.intervention: Targeted teaching for orthopaedic trainees, prompt posters and alterations to the trauma clerking proforma.

cycle2.result: 29 (100%) prescribed antibiotics before definitive surgery, mean time to administration 233 minutes; 26 (89.7%) per BSUH guidelines; 51.7% initial STAT prescriptions.

result.other_findings: STAT once-only prescriptions significantly reduced mean time to administration, by 154 minutes.

result.setting: Depot clinic, City East Adult Community Mental Health Team, Leicester
result.standard: BNF, Trust and Maudsley guidelines for long-acting antipsychotic prescribing

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for licensed indication and dose/frequency within BNF range; 14% received polypharmacy; 86% had regular outpatient review; only 46% had side effect review.

result.other_findings: Recommendations included better documentation, automatic review reminders, a clinic checklist and re-audit.

result.setting: Emergency (CEPOD) theatre, Walsall Manor Hospital
result.standard: Hospital policy: first patient sent for by 08:40 AM and arrival by 09:00 AM

cycle1.result: Single on-call registrar: mean time sent for 09:33, arrival 10:00, turnover 00:39.

result.intervention: Dedicated CEPOD registrar separate from the on-call registrar.

cycle2.result: Dedicated CEPOD registrar: mean time sent for 09:08 (p=0.015), arrival 09:32 (p=0.010), turnover 00:11 (p=0.018).

result.other_findings: Overall 90.4% (47/52) first cases sent for after 08:40, 88.5% (46/52) arrived after 09:00, 94.2% (49/52) knife-to-skin after 09:30 and 36.5% (19/52) had turnover over 30 minutes.

result.topic: Junior doctor knowledge of enhanced recovery
result.setting: Surgical department, Kettering General Hospital (district general hospital)
result.standard: Local hospital guidelines: 100% awareness and knowledge of colorectal ERP among surgical team

cycle1.result: Average knowledge score 52.9%; 5/8 (62.5%) aware of ERP.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based; recommends PowerPoint education then re-audit.

result.setting: Community Learning Disability Team; CNTW NHS Foundation Trust and TEWV NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: STOMP pathway criteria for psychotropic prescribing in people with learning disabilities

cycle1.result: Clinical rationale documented 100%; medication review within 12 months 93%; non-pharmacological interventions 87%; person/carer involvement 90%; attempted or completed reduction documented 70%.

result.other_findings: Documentation of medication reduction attempts was the weakest area.

result.setting: General surgery department, Royal Sussex County Hospital (tertiary care hospital)
result.standard: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges guidance on writing clinic letters

cycle1.result: Missing data by parameter: plan for patient/carer 37.5%, care planning arrangements 44.6%, complications 67.5%, anaesthesia issues 89.4%, allergies 94%, diagnosis 94%, time 99.4%, preferred name 100%, personal identifiers 100%.

result.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance meeting and a generic clinic letter template with mandatory parameters introduced; induction teaching planned.
result.other_findings: Repeat cycle planned in 3–5 months; abstract states documentation improved after the intervention but gives no figures.

result.setting: Single centre, UH Bristol NHS Foundation Trust; adult appendicitis patients
result.standard: Locally proposed appendicitis diagnostic algorithm

cycle1.result: Cross-sectional imaging rate 36.6%; normal appendicectomy rate 5.22%.

result.intervention: Increased use of cross-sectional imaging during the Covid-19 pandemic; diagnostic algorithm developed.

cycle2.result: Cross-sectional imaging rate 76%; normal appendicectomy rate 2.4%; 36% not managed in accordance with the proposed algorithm.

result.other_findings: 194 patients across both periods; the algorithm may have prevented up to 87.5% of normal appendicectomies.

result.setting: Primary care practices in the Avon region, South West England
result.standard: Prostate Cancer Risk Management programme guidelines; NICE guidelines

cycle1.result: Overall good practice with room for improvement in advice on limitations of prostate biopsy and relevance of testing in the elderly; nearly half of abnormal primary-care PSA tests were repeated.

result.other_findings: Consistent year-on-year increase in PSA requests across all age groups and regions.

result.setting: General Surgery Department, district general hospital (single centre)
result.standard: GMC guidance on clear, accurate and legible records; drug chart domains 100% complete

cycle1.result: Alerts/allergies 4/22 (18%), signatures 2/22 (9%), VTE risk assessment 5/22 (24%), antithrombotic 0/21, regular 1/22 (5%), as-required 0/21, IV fluids 1/16 (6%).

cycle2.result: Alerts/allergies 18/25 (72%; p<0.001), signatures 17/25 (68%; p<0.001), VTE risk assessment 24/25 (96%; p<0.001), antithrombotic 9/25 (36%; p=0.002), regular 10/25 (40%; p=0.04), as-required 5/22 (23%; p=0.020), IV fluids 20/21 (95%; p<0.001).

result.other_findings: 10 of 17 domains showed no significant change (p≥0.05).

result.topic: Tip-apex distance in dynamic hip screw fixation
result.setting: Orthopaedic department, Wrexham Maelor Hospital
result.standard: Tip-apex distance <25mm

cycle1.result: Mean TAD 22.85mm (range 15–36mm); TAD >25mm in 13 cases (26%).

result.intervention: Posters on TAD recommendations displayed in theatre and a weekly departmental metalwork meeting reviewing imaging from all surgeries.
result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: Ulster Hospital, Belfast
result.standard: AUGIS/BSG: all acute pancreatitis patients to have a validated severity score documented within 48 hours of admission

cycle1.result: 4 (17%) had severity scores documented.

result.intervention: FY/SHO teaching, staff posters summarising guidelines and an electronic documentation template.

cycle2.result: 7 (30%) had severity scores documented, all within the first 24 hours; one further case incomplete due to pending labs.

result.other_findings: Scores used were Glasgow-Imrie, Modified Glasgow and BISAP according to clinician preference.

result.setting: Level III Surgical ICU, Christian Medical College, Vellore
result.standard: ICU protocol to remove unused central lines after five days, using an electronic alert system

cycle1.result: Alerts created for 17 (25%) of 68 lines; mean central line days 6.4 (SD 3.1).

result.intervention: Educational session with a step-by-step guide to using the electronic alert system, following a survey of ICU doctors.

cycle2.result: Alerts created for 41 of 63 lines (65%); mean central line days 4.2 (SD 2.8) (P<.05).

result.other_findings: Survey showed about 30% of doctors were unfamiliar with the alert system.

result.setting: A&E and emergency general surgery, Salford Royal NHS Trust
result.standard: BSG guidelines on risk stratification with Shock Index and Oakland score

cycle1.result: 1 patient (3%) had shock index documented; Oakland score rarely used.

result.other_findings: 16 (44%) admitted under EGS, of whom 7 (44%) needed inpatient endoscopy and 3 (19%) transfusion; 2 (6%) needed CT angiogram.

result.setting: Colorectal 2WW service, Bristol Royal Infirmary (single centre)
result.standard: South West clinical network 2WW referral criteria with emphasis on FIT (2023)

cycle1.result: 837 referrals; FIT performed in 374 (44.8%); 560 colonoscopies; 24 colorectal cancers.

result.intervention: Change in network 2WW referral criteria placing greater emphasis on FIT.

cycle2.result: 399 referrals; FIT performed in 297 (75.0%); 270 colonoscopies; 20 colorectal cancers (p=0.06).

result.other_findings: Referrals fell by more than 50% with reduced endoscopy demand and no reduction in cancer diagnosis.

result.setting: Five community intellectual disability psychiatry teams, Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Best practice for medication review and side-effect monitoring using the ACB Scale

cycle1.result: Medication indication documented 100% in two boroughs but as low as 7.7% in others; cognition monitored in 44.5%; LUNSERS documented in 0.7%; anticholinergic side effects mentioned in 7.5%.

result.other_findings: 15.1% of the cohort had documented hallucinations.

result.setting: General surgery, surgical assessment unit and ED, Royal Sussex County Hospital
result.standard: GMC guidance on chaperones during intimate examination

cycle1.result: 9/168 (5.3%) had chaperone documentation, of which 1/9 (11%) complete; perianal examination 1/23 (4.3%); abdominal examination 8/141 (5.6%).

result.intervention: Results shared with the department with education; chaperone stickers (name, position, gender) to be attached to notes.
result.other_findings: All 9 documented cases were male doctors examining female patients; prospective post-intervention data collection ongoing.

result.topic: Metabolic screening in urinary tract stones
result.setting: District general hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust; patients with urinary tract calculi
result.standard: NICE and EAU guidelines: serum calcium and uric acid measured as metabolic screening

cycle1.result: Serum calcium measured in 65%; uric acid measured in 46%.

result.intervention: Education and posters after previous audits.

cycle2.result: Serum calcium measured in 46%; uric acid measured in 37%.

result.other_findings: Compliance declined despite education; an electronic 'renal colic' requesting bundle auto-selecting calcium and uric acid has since been implemented, with re-audit planned in 6 months.

result.topic: Enhanced recovery (ERAS) compliance in colorectal surgery
result.setting: Elective colorectal surgery, teaching hospital, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: ERAS 2025 guidelines (10 of 23 recommendations with high-grade evidence)

cycle1.result: More than 90% compliance in PONV prophylaxis, NG tube removal, multimodal analgesia, post-op enteral nutrition, IV antibiotics and VTE prophylaxis; mechanical bowel prep routinely prescribed in more than 85% of resections (not recommended); more than 78% minimally invasive; 73% no drain.

result.other_findings: All patients receiving mechanical bowel prep had oral antibiotics.

result.topic: Genetics referral for family history of colorectal cancer
result.setting: Colonoscopy surveillance programme for hereditary cancer, York Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: Amsterdam criteria and BSG/ACPGBI/UKCGG 2019 guidelines on hereditary colorectal cancer risk and referral

cycle1.result: 18/72 (25%) average-risk patients unnecessarily referred to genetics; 5/41 (12%) high-risk patients not referred; 19/34 (55.8%) indeterminate patients referred.

result.other_findings: Risk categories: 72 (31.6%) average, 81 (35.5%) moderate, 41 (18%) high, 34 (14.9%) indeterminate; a family history questionnaire/template is recommended.

result.setting: Medway Maritime Hospital
result.standard: RCS Good Surgical Practice (2014): eighteen items in operation notes

cycle1.result: 45% of notes produced using the electronic proforma.

result.intervention: Electronic operation note proforma introduced in 2015.

cycle2.result: 28% of notes produced using the electronic proforma; significantly more notes recorded elective/emergency status (p<0.0001 vs 2015), intraoperative diagnosis (p<0.01) and estimated blood loss (p<0.05).

result.other_findings: Notes produced with the electronic proforma were of higher quality than those without.

result.setting: Two general surgical wards, Royal Alexandra Hospital, Paisley
result.standard: SIGN guidelines (16 criteria) plus 3 locally agreed criteria for immediate discharge letters

cycle1.result: 0% of IDLs had all SIGN criteria present.

result.intervention: IDL template created and distributed to junior doctors after presentation at a local research meeting.

cycle2.result: 6% of IDLs had all SIGN criteria present (not significant); 15/16 SIGN criteria documented more often, 5 significantly (p<0.05); all 3 local criteria improved, 1 significantly.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.topic: Anastomotic leak rate in emergency surgery
result.setting: Specialised Surgical Emergency Unit, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford
result.standard: Expected anastomotic leak rates of 0.5-18% from the literature

cycle1.result: Anastomotic leak and return to theatre rates both 4% (n=3); mortality 4% (n=3); median length of stay 10 days.

result.other_findings: Two leaks were small bowel anastomoses and one ileocolic; stoma versus anastomosis rates not assessed.

result.topic: Non-operative hip fracture management and coding
result.setting: Southport and Ormskirk NHS Trust; hip fracture admissions
result.standard: NHFD national standard of 5% non-operatively managed hip fractures

cycle1.result: 9.76% of hip fractures managed non-operatively.

result.intervention: Joint clinico-radiological review by orthopaedic staff and the clinical coding department and a new Neck of Femur Proforma.

cycle2.result: 512 cases reviewed, 50 excluded after correct coding; 440 operated and 22 (4.8%) managed non-operatively.

result.other_findings: 30-day mortality in the non-operative group rose from 30.5% to 54.50%, possibly due to COVID-19.

result.setting: Multi-centre, tertiary and secondary hospitals; patients undergoing appendicectomy
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: USS sensitivity 57.6%; CT sensitivity 95.7%; 26.4% had no scan (clinical diagnosis PPV 85%); negative appendicectomy 12.1% (16.4% females vs 7.8% males, p=0.008).

result.other_findings: Females and secondary hospital patients had more scans (p<0.001).

result.setting: Four surgical wards (emergency and elective), Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Operation date 76.1%, abnormal blood results 89%, outpatient investigations 72%, urgency 39.6%, GP plans 73%, outpatient appointments 85%, clinical summary 98%, VTE prophylaxis duration 99%.

result.intervention: Discharge summary checklist introduced at junior doctor induction.

cycle2.result: Operation date 90.1% (p=0.019), abnormal blood results 97% (p=0.323), outpatient investigations 85% (p=0.025), urgency 43.3% (p=0.741), GP plans 81% (p=0.178), outpatient appointments 93% (p=0.037), clinical summary 94% (p=0.149), VTE prophylaxis duration 90% (p=0.005).

result.other_findings: Clinical summary and VTE prophylaxis duration documentation worsened on re-audit.

result.setting: Minor injuries unit, Wrexham Maelor Hospital
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: IV sedation group (retrospective cohort): mean time between reduction radiographs 157.7 minutes (95% CI 92.3 to 223.2).

result.intervention: Methoxyflurane (Penthrox) inhalational analgesia introduced for closed reduction without sedation.

cycle2.result: Penthrox group: all reduced successfully; mean time between radiographs 40.8 min (95% CI 27.4 to 54.3), p=0.0026; no documented adverse events.

result.other_findings: 22 patients in total; mean age 44.6 years, 72% male.

result.setting: General surgery elective and CEPOD lists, a major trauma centre and a DGH (Royal Sussex County Hospital)
result.standard: RCS 'Consent: Supported Decision-Making': patient offered a copy of the consent form after signing

cycle1.result: 0% of patients provided a copy of the consent form.

cycle2.result: 28% of patients offered a copy of the consent form.

result.other_findings: not reported

result.setting: NELA aggregate hospital reports, years 4 to 6
result.standard: NELA key performance indicators

cycle1.result: 559 hospital aggregates; average mortality 9.6%; no significant correlation between mortality and any performance indicator.

result.other_findings: Indicators examined included preoperative risk documentation, timely theatre arrival, consultant presence, critical care admission and elderly care assessment.

result.topic: VTE prophylaxis on discharge after hip fracture
result.setting: Royal Infirmary Edinburgh; hip fracture patients on discharge
result.standard: NICE: LMWH or fondaparinux for one month after hip fracture; local policy of dalteparin for 30 days after surgery

cycle1.result: 13% had not received VTE prophylaxis in line with guidelines; six of these had no documented contraindication or alternative prophylaxis.

result.intervention: Template discharge letter with a prompt for appropriate VTE prophylaxis prescription; results disseminated locally.

cycle2.result: 95% received appropriate VTE prophylaxis on discharge.

result.other_findings: The template also prompted documentation of contraindications to prophylaxis.

result.topic: Scrotal ultrasound in acute scrotal pain
result.setting: Surgical Assessment Unit, University Hospitals Birmingham
result.standard: EAU guidelines (routine ultrasound not recommended)

cycle1.result: 109/141 underwent scrotal US; urgent indications only in 9 (collection/abscess 5, testicular mass 4); 66/109 for 'soft' indications; US changed immediate management in 1/109.

result.other_findings: Unexpected findings: one occult testicular tumour, one acute torsion and two inguinal herniae; early outpatient US suggested as sufficient.

result.setting: Complex abdominal wall reconstruction (general and plastic surgery), Royal Free Hospital, London
result.standard: Accurate ICD, OPCS-4 and HRG coding based on clinical documentation

cycle1.result: ICD and OPCS-4 codes changed in all 4 cases after clinician validation.

result.intervention: Clinician-validation of codes with the clinical coding team and amendment of HRG codes.
result.other_findings: Recoding led to average financial savings of £6,000 per case.

result.setting: Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Hospital, Oswestry; orthopaedic surgery
result.standard: RCS COVID-19 guidance: all patients made aware of the risk of contracting COVID-19 in hospital (0.45%)

cycle1.result: 44% of consent forms documented COVID-19 risk; 56% did not.

result.other_findings: Of forms omitting COVID risk, 34% were completed by consultants, 18% by fellows and 48% by registrars; 6% tested for suspected COVID post-operatively and 0% contracted it.

result.setting: Queen's Hospital, Royal Derby and Burton NHS Trust (district general hospital)
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: 37% developed post-operative wound infection; of these 52% were smokers, 52% obese (BMI >30) and 83% smokers or obese.

result.other_findings: Procedures: Karydakis 52%, modified Bascom 27%, rhomboid flap 13%, not primarily closed 8%.

result.setting: Tertiary cardiac surgery centre, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London
result.standard: Guidelines recommending 12 months DAPT after PCI followed by emergency CABG

cycle1.result: All except 2 received lifelong aspirin or a DOAC/NOAC; of 3 with STEMI/NSTEMI in the preceding 12 months, 2 received DAPT and 1 aspirin plus DOAC; variation in DAPT duration for stable CAD.

result.intervention: Antiplatelet prescription aid designed, taking surgeon preference into account.

cycle2.result: Improvement in consistency of prescribing (no figures given).

result.other_findings: Variation in DAPT prescribing existed between consultants and between patients of the same consultant.

result.setting: University Hospital Limerick; non-consultant hospital doctors
result.standard: Local University Hospital Limerick PPE guidelines

cycle1.result: What PPE includes 91%; donning sequence 52%; FIT test steps 57%; doffing sequence 47%.

result.intervention: Emails with results and local guidelines and a Zoom educational session.

cycle2.result: What PPE includes 100%; donning sequence 88% (p<0.05); FIT test steps 74% (p=0.247); doffing sequence 81% (p<0.05).

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based audit of awareness.

result.setting: District general hospital (Lister Hospital / West Suffolk Hospital); ultrasound-diagnosed gallbladder polyps
result.standard: ESGAR/EASES/EFISDS/ESGE joint guidelines (6, 12 and 24 monthly scans for 6-9mm polyps; cholecystectomy >10mm); local trust guideline of 12 and 24 monthly scans

cycle1.result: Of 82 (36.6%) 6-9mm polyps, 62 (75%) followed up; mean time to second scan 472 days, median 556 days; timing not within recommended guidelines.

result.other_findings: Correct scan modality used; 17 had cholecystectomy with 1 malignancy; 14 polyps increased in size.

result.setting: Two acute adult psychiatric units and one old age mental health ward, Southern Health NHS Foundation Trust
result.standard: Driving status confirmed on admission (target 100%); driving advice given to all patients unfit to drive (target 100%)

cycle1.result: 42% (15) had driving status confirmed on/during admission.

cycle2.result: 47% (24) had driving status confirmed; 6% improvement in drivers informed they were unfit to drive; 22% increase in DVLA advice given; DVLA notifications increased by 18%.

result.other_findings: 15 current drivers identified in cycle 2.

result.setting: Two inpatient wards, Wexford General Hospital (level 3 general hospital)
result.standard: HSE National Clinical Guideline no. 26 on sepsis protocol initiation (sepsis 6 bundle)

cycle1.result: 36 (12.2%) positive sepsis triggers; HSE proforma used in 13.89% and completed in 1 case; average completion of sepsis 6 bundle 55.5%; antibiotics given in 31/36.

result.other_findings: Revision of the sepsis proforma and further clinician education recommended.

result.topic: Lynch syndrome testing in colorectal cancer
result.setting: Trust-wide, West Middlesex University Hospital
result.standard: NICE 2017: all patients with colorectal cancer tested for Lynch syndrome

cycle1.result: 79% tested for Lynch; biopsy to result 2 to 276 days (average 45); 54% within 30 days, 34% 30–90 days, 12% over 90 days.

result.other_findings: Results within 30 days rose by year: 30% (2017), 55% (2018), 71% (2019); median days 39, 28 and 16.

result.setting: BAUS national database of laparoscopic renal surgery
result.standard: not reported

cycle1.result: Overall complication rate 14.7%; intra-operative 3.5%; post-operative 12.1%; decreased from 16.6% in 2002 to 15.1% in 2012.

result.other_findings: Capture rate estimated at 30% with self-reporting bias.

result.setting: ENT and plastic surgery, University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust; SHOs and house officers
result.standard: Local trust guidelines; target 100% trained to access healthcare records

cycle1.result: 0% trained to access healthcare records at induction; 25% confident accessing records.

result.intervention: Induction changed to include training on accessing healthcare records.

cycle2.result: 80% trained at induction; 100% confident accessing records.

result.other_findings: Questionnaire-based; further cycles needed to assess sustainability.

result.setting: Orthopaedic ward, BBH Rawalpindi
result.standard: RCS guidelines for operation notes (18 items)

cycle1.result: Deficiencies in elective/emergency, operative diagnosis, findings, complications, extra procedures, tissue removed/added, closure details, blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis.

result.intervention: Three-step intervention: presentations, brochures and aide memoires, and introduction of proformas.
result.other_findings: Analysed with Fisher's exact test after 4 weeks.

result.setting: Royal Wolverhampton Hospital; RARC by two surgeons
result.standard: Pasadena consensus panel (2015) best practice for RARC

result.topic: Dexamethasone in metastatic spinal cord compression
